````
#### **Build System: Quake + cm3 Executor**

**Quake Language:**
- Configuration scripting language (simpler than Make, inspired by C, shell, C preprocessor)
- Used in `cm3.cfg` (compiler configuration) and `m3makefile` (per-package build scripts)
- Quake functions: `import()`, `include_dir()`, `Module()`, `module()`, `Library()`, `Program()`, `build_standalone()`, `m3_option()`, `include()`, `override()`
- Files: `/scripts/version.quake`, `/scripts/branch.quake`

**Quake Functions in m3makefile Examples:**
```quake
import("libm3")              % Import dependency
include_dir("subdir")        % Include module subdirectory
Module("ModName")            % Interface-only module (.i3)
module("modname")            % Implementation module (.m3)
Library("libname")           % Build library
Program("progname")          % Build executable
build_standalone()           % Build as standalone (self-contained)
m3_option("-O")              % Compiler options
```

**Platform/Target Support** (from `/scripts/sysinfo.sh`):
- Auto-detect: `uname -s`, `uname -r`, `uname -p`
- Targets: ARM, x86, x86_64, MIPS, PowerPC, etc.
- OS: POSIX (Linux, BSD, macOS, Solaris) and WIN32 (Cygwin, native)
- Backends: Native (x86), GCC-based, LLVM (v13, 18, 22)
- Default: GCC backend (`CM3_GCC_BACKEND=yes`)

### **3. KEY CONVENTIONS**

#### **File Naming & Module Structure**

```
Interface:  ModuleName.i3    (defines module interface/signature)
Implementation: modulename.m3 (implements the interface)
Generic:    ModuleName.mg    (interface template)
Generic impl: modulename.mg   (implementation template)
Makefile:   m3makefile        (per-package build script in Quake)
Overrides:  m3overrides       (local package location mapping)
```

**Key File Extensions:**
- `.i3` - Interface definition (public API)
- `.m3` - Implementation module (private code)
- `.mg` - Generic interface template
- `.ig` - Generic implementation template (rare)
- `.c` - C source (for C code integration)
- `.h` - C header
- `.quake` - Quake configuration scripts

#### **Package Structure Convention**

```
PackageName/
├── src/
│   ├── m3makefile          (BUILD INSTRUCTIONS - Quake scripts)
│   ├── m3overrides         (LOCAL PACKAGE MAPPING)
│   ├── Module.i3           (Interface)
│   ├── module.m3           (Implementation)
│   ├── SubDir/
│   │   ├── m3makefile      (Nested subpackage)
│   │   └── *.i3, *.m3
│   └── ...
├── test/                   (Optional test files)
└── TARGET/                 (Generated: platform-specific binaries)
    ├── m3core/
    ├── libm3/
    └── ...
```

**Example: m3-sys/m3front/src/**
```
m3front/src/
├── m3makefile (imports libm3, m3middle; builds Library "m3front")
├── m3overrides (include(ROOT & "/m3overrides"))
├── builtinAtomic/ (subdir with m3makefile)
├── builtinOps/   (subdir with m3makefile)
├── builtinTypes/ (subdir with m3makefile)
├── builtinInfo/  (subdir with m3makefile)
├── builtinWord/  (subdir with m3makefile)
├── exprs/        (expressions - subdirs for different expr types)
├── stmts/        (statements)
├── types/        (type system)
├── values/       (value representations)
├── misc/         (main drivers: M3Front.m3, M3Compiler.m3, etc.)
└── *.i3, *.m3    (interface/implementation pairs)
```

#### **m3overrides Pattern**

**Top-level m3overrides** (`/Users/hosking/Downloads/cm3-d5.12.0/m3overrides`):
```quake
proc Override(a, b) is
  if not equal(pn_last(PACKAGE_DIR), a)  
    override(a, ROOT & "/" & b)
  end
end

Override("m3core", "m3-libs")
Override("libm3", "m3-libs")
Override("m3front", "m3-sys")
Override("m3middle", "m3-sys")
Override("m3linker", "m3-sys")
Override("m3back", "m3-sys")
... (140+ package mappings)
```

**Purpose:** Maps package names to their source locations (m3-sys, m3-libs, m3-comm, m3-ui, etc.)
- Allows `-override` flag to use local workspace packages instead of installed system packages
- Prevents circular dependency issues

**Local m3overrides** (e.g., `/m3-sys/m3front/src/m3overrides`):
```quake
include(ROOT & "/m3overrides")
```
- Simply includes top-level overrides

#### **Import Dependencies**

**m3makefile imports pattern:**
```quake
% Interfaces import
import("libm3")      % Standard library
import("m3middle")   % Intermediate representation
import("m3core")     % Runtime/GC

% Then include subdirectories
include_dir("exprs")
include_dir("types")
...

% Finally define output
Library("m3front")   % or Program("name")
```

**Module Declaration Pattern:**
```quake
Module("PublicInterface")      % Only .i3 file
module("privateimpl")          % Full module (.i3 + .m3)

% Uppercase = interface-only (abstract)
% lowercase = concrete implementation
```

#### **Package Tags** (from pkginfo.txt)

Packages tagged with build categories:
```
m3core    [base, core, front, headless, min, unicode]
libm3     [base, core, front, headless, min, unicode]
m3front   [core, front, headless, unicode]
m3middle  [base, core, front, headless, unicode]
tcp       [base, comm, core, headless]
cm3ide    [core, headless]
... (tags describe which collections include them)
```

**Categories:**
- `base` - Base system
- `core` - Core compiler
- `front` - Frontend compiler
- `headless` - No GUI
- `min` - Minimal set
- `unicode` - Unicode support
- `comm` - Communication
- `devlib` - Developer library
- `webdev` - Web development
- etc.

### **Summary Command Reference**

**To build just the compiler:**
```bash
cd /Users/hosking/Downloads/cm3-d5.12.0/scripts
./do-cm3-front.sh buildship    # Build and install frontend
./do-cm3-core.sh buildship     # Build full bootstrapped compiler
```

**To build a single package:**
```bash
./do-pkg.sh buildship m3-sys/m3front
```

**To build everything:**
```bash
./do-cm3-std.sh buildship      # Standard system
./do-cm3-all.sh buildship      # Everything
```

**Build without overrides (use installed system packages):**
```bash
./do-cm3-front.sh buildglobal  # Uses /usr/local/cm3 packages
```

**Clean:**
```bash
./do-cm3-front.sh clean        # Clean with overrides
./do-cm3-front.sh cleanglobal  # Clean globally
```

**Test:**
```bash
cd /Users/hosking/Downloads/cm3-d5.12.0/m3-sys/m3tests/src
# Tests in subdirs like p2/p215/ with m3makefile
cm3 -build                     # Build and run tests
```
````

```
CM3 Free Distribution -- scripts/README

This directory contains various scripts that can be used to compile /
build / bootstrap part or all of the CM3 source distribution.

These scripts can be divided in those that can be called directly and
those intended for inclusion only. They are all standard Bourne shell
scripts and should be executable on every system (sometimes probably
some minor tweaks might be needed). On Windows, you can use the Cygwin
distribution which comes with bash and most of the GNU tools, or the
MKS tool kit and its Korn shell. Alternatively, you may want to use
the Windows CMD scripts contributed by Randy Coleburn. See README-WIN32
for details. Alternatively, you may want to use the Windows CMD scripts
in the win directory contributed by Jay Krell. They work very much like
the sh scripts documented here. Or the Python scripts in the python
directory.

You are probably most interested in one of the following:

 o Use boot-cm3-with-m3.sh and do-cm3-core.sh to boot the system using
   another M3 compiler.

 o Use do-cm3-min.sh to compile the minimal set of CM3 libraries.

 o Use do-cm3-base.sh to compile a basic system without GUI.

 o Use do-cm3-std.sh to compile a standard system with GUI and full
   networking support.

 o Use do-pkg.sh to compile or clean one or more arbitrary packages.

 o Use do-cm3-front.sh to build (and install) a build system, i.e., the 
   compiler, its support libraries, and support utilities.

 o Use do-cm3-unicode.sh to build (and install) what do-cm3-front builds,
   plus the unicode encoding suport library libunicode.  This latter package
   will build successfully only when the build compiler is configured for
   full Unicode range WIDECHAR. 

 o Use do-cm3-core.sh to build (and install) a core cm3 system, i.e.
   the compiler with some useful base libraries.

 o Use upgrade.sh to build and install a new compiler version from
   sources. This may be difficult, since packages have to be built and
   shipped in the correct order, and once you've shipped something
   wrong, you may be stuck.

 o Use install-cm3-compiler.sh to install the actual compiler
   (front-end and back-end) from the workspace.

Each of the do-cm3-*.sh scripts takes an action as an argument, which
translates into options to the cm3 command(s) executed by the script,
according to the following table:

   do-cm3-*.sh argument:                cm3 command(s) and options:

   <no argument>, build, buildlocal     cm3 -build -override ...
   buildglobal, buildship               cm3 -build ...; cm3 -ship ...
   ship                                 cm3 -ship ...
   clean, cleanlocal                    cm3 -clean -override ...
```

<sub>⏱️ 3m 39s</sub>

### 💬 Copilot

Created `.github/copilot-instructions.md`. Here's what it covers:

- **Build commands** — all `do-cm3-*.sh` scripts with their action arguments, single-package builds, direct `cm3` invocation flags
- **Testing** — how to run a single test vs the full suite, test category layout
- **Compiler pipeline** — frontend → M3CG IR → middle → backend (C/GCC/LLVM) → linker
- **Major collections** — m3-sys, m3-libs, m3-comm, m3-ui, etc. with what lives where
- **Quake build system** — key m3makefile functions and how `m3overrides` enables local workspace builds
- **File/naming conventions** — `.i3`/`.m3`/`.ig`/`.mg`, `Module()` vs `module()` semantics, package structure
- **Key dependencies** — m3core, libm3, m3middle as the critical shared layers

Is there anything you'd like to adjust — for example, more detail on bootstrapping, the LLVM backends, or any specific subsystem?

<details>
<summary>75 lines</summary>

```
#!/bin/sh

#set -e
#set -x

if [ -n "$ROOT" -a -d "$ROOT" ] ; then
  sysinfo="$ROOT/scripts/sysinfo.sh"
  root="${ROOT}"; export root
else
  root=`pwd`
  while [ -n "$root" -a ! -f "$root/scripts/sysinfo.sh" ] ; do
    root=`dirname $root`
  done
  sysinfo="$root/scripts/sysinfo.sh"
  if [ ! -f "$sysinfo" ] ; then
    echo "scripts/sysinfo.sh not found" 1>&2
    exit 1
  fi
  export root
fi

. "$sysinfo"
. "$root/scripts/pkginfo.sh"
. "$root/scripts/pkgcmds.sh"

USAGE="
  `basename $0` [ generic_options ] [ generic_cmd ]

  builds a new compiler from a new set of sources, using an existing compiler
  possibly an old compiler

  generic_options:
${GEN_OPTS}"
  
show_usage $@

OPTIONS=`extract_options $@`

EXE=""
if [ "${TARGET}" = "NT386" \
    -o "${TARGET}" = "I386_CYGWIN"  -o "${TARGET}" = "I386_NT"  -o "${TARGET}" = "I386_MINGW" \
    -o "${TARGET}" = "AMD64_CYGWIN" -o "${TARGET}" = "AMD64_NT" -o "${TARGET}" = "AMD64_MINGW" ]; then
  EXE=".exe"
fi

install_compiler() {
  M3CONFIG="${INSTALLROOT}/bin/cm3.cfg" "${root}/m3-sys/cm3/${TARGET}/cm3${EXE}" --version || exit 1
  if [ "x${GCC_BACKEND}" = xyes ]; then
    "${root}/m3-sys/m3cc/${TARGET}/cm3cg${EXE}" --help -version >/dev/null || exit 1
  fi
  mkdir -p "${INSTALLROOT}/bin" || exit 1
  cp "${root}/m3-sys/cm3/${TARGET}/cm3${EXE}" "${INSTALLROOT}/bin/cm3${EXE}" || exit 1
  if [ "x${GCC_BACKEND}" = xyes ]; then
    cp "${root}/m3-sys/m3cc/${TARGET}/cm3cg${EXE}" "${INSTALLROOT}/bin/cm3cg${EXE}" || exit 1
  fi
  install_config || exit 1
}

# delete lingering cm3cg in case old compiler/config uses it
for a in cm3cg gcc/m3cgc1; do
    for b in "" .exe; do
        rm "$root/m3-sys/m3cc/${TARGET}/$a$b" || true
    done
done

# Build the compiler with the installed version of the runtime;
# do _not_ compile m3core and libm3 here.
# Start with the front end.
P="sysutils set m3middle m3objfile m3linker m3back \
   m3front m3quake cm3 mklib m3cggen"

  "$root/scripts/do-pkg.sh" "$@" "build" m3cc || exit 1
fi

# Install the compiler binaries all together (cm3, cm3cg, config).
install_compiler || exit 1

# Rebuild with the new compiler.
# No need for m3cc since it is written in C (ie no compiler change).

P="m3core libm3 ${P}"
"$root/scripts/do-pkg.sh" "$@" "realclean" ${P} || exit 1
"$root/scripts/do-pkg.sh" "$@" "buildship" ${P} || exit 1

# Do another compiler upgrade.
install_compiler || exit 1
```

```
#!/bin/sh

if [ -n "$ROOT" -a -d "$ROOT" ] ; then
  sysinfo="$ROOT/scripts/sysinfo.sh"
  root="${ROOT}"; export root
else
  root=`pwd`
  while [ -n "$root" -a ! -f "$root/scripts/sysinfo.sh" ] ; do
    root=`dirname $root`
  done
  sysinfo="$root/scripts/sysinfo.sh"
  if [ ! -f "$sysinfo" ] ; then
    echo "scripts/sysinfo.sh not found" 1>&2
    exit 1
  fi
  export root
fi

. "$sysinfo"

CONFIG="${INSTALLROOT}/bin/config"
FRONTEND="${INSTALLROOT}/bin/cm3"
BACKEND="${INSTALLROOT}/bin/cm3cg"
FRONTEND_SRC="${ROOT}/m3-sys/cm3/${TARGET}/cm3"
BACKEND_SRC="${ROOT}/m3-sys/m3cc/${TARGET}/cm3cg"
CONFIG_SRC="${ROOT}/m3-sys/cminstall/src/config"

usage()
{
  echo ""
  echo "install-cm3-compiler.sh [ -n ] backup | newversion | upgrade"
  echo "install-cm3-compiler.sh [ -n ] restore <version_number>"
  echo ""
  echo "  backup"
  echo "    will make copies of cm3 front-end and back-end with the cm3"
  echo "    version number as suffix, e.g."
  echo "    ${FRONTEND} --> ${FRONTEND}-x.y.z"
  echo "    ${BACKEND} --> ${BACKEND}-x.y.z"
  echo "    ${CONFIG} --> ${CONFIG}-x.y.z"
  echo ""
  echo "  restore <version_number>"
  echo "    will restore copies with suffixed version number as current"
  echo "    version, e.g."
  echo "    ${FRONTEND}-x.y.z --> ${FRONTEND}"
  echo "    ${BACKEND}-x.y.z --> ${BACKEND}"
  echo "    ${CONFIG}-x.y.z --> ${CONFIG}"
  echo ""
  echo "  newversion"
  echo "    will install the version from the current workspace with"
  echo "    version number suffixes, e.g."
  echo "    ${FRONTEND_SRC} --> ${FRONTEND}-x.y.z"
  echo "    ${BACKEND_SRC} --> ${BACKEND}-x.y.z"
  echo "    ${CONFIG} --> ${CONFIG}-x.y.z"
  echo ""
  echo "  upgrade"
  echo "    will backup the existing version, install new executables"
  echo "    with suffixes and restore them as the current version"
  echo ""
  echo "  Beware: This script relies on the cm3 executable to correctly"
  echo "  identify its version (cm3 -version). If it does not, things will"
  echo "  get messed up."
  echo ""
}

if [ "${TARGET}" = "NT386" \
        -o "${TARGET}" = "I386_CYGWIN" \
        -o "${TARGET}" = "I386_MINGW" ]; then
  ext=".exe"
else
  ext=""
fi

exit_if()
{
  if [ "${NOACTION}" = yes ] ; then
    echo "error ignored due to -n" 1>&2
  else
    exit "$1"
  fi
}

do_cp()
{
  echo cp "$1${ext}" "$2${ext}"
  if [ "${NOACTION}" != yes ] ; then
    if cp "$1${ext}" "$2${ext}"; then
      true
    else
      exit_if 1
    fi
  fi
}

cp_if()
{
  if [ ! -r "$1${ext}" ] ; then
    echo "cp_if: source does not exist: $1" 1>&2 
    exit_if 1
  fi
  if [ -r "$2${ext}" ] ; then
    # destination exists
    if cmp "$1${ext}" "$2${ext}" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
      echo "cp_if: $1 and $2 identical" 1>&2
      true
    else
      if [ -w "$2${ext}" ] ; then
        do_cp "$1" "$2"
      else
        echo "cp_if: cannot write $2" 1>&2
        exit_if 1
      fi
    fi
  else
    do_cp "$1" "$2"
  fi
}

getversion()
{
  if [ -x "$1${ext}" ] ; then
    if "$1" -version > /dev/null; then
      "$1" -version | grep version | awk '{print $5}'
    else
      echo "$1 is broken" 1>&2
      exit 2
    fi
  else
    echo "$1 is not executable" 1>&2
    exit 1
  fi
}

install_local_as_version()
{
  CM3VERSION=`getversion "${FRONTEND_SRC}"`
  cp_if "${FRONTEND_SRC}" "${FRONTEND}-${CM3VERSION}"
  if [ "${GCC_BACKEND}" = yes ] ; then
    cp_if "${BACKEND_SRC}" "${BACKEND}-${CM3VERSION}"
  fi
  echo mkdir -p "${CONFIG}-${CM3VERSION}"
       mkdir -p "${CONFIG}-${CM3VERSION}"
  echo cp "${CONFIG_SRC}"/* "${CONFIG}-${CM3VERSION}"
       cp "${CONFIG_SRC}"/* "${CONFIG}-${CM3VERSION}"
}

backup_old()
{
  OLDCM3VERSION=`getversion "${FRONTEND}"`
  cp_if "${FRONTEND}" "${FRONTEND}-${OLDCM3VERSION}"
  if [ "${GCC_BACKEND}" = yes ] ; then
    cp_if "${BACKEND}" "${BACKEND}-${OLDCM3VERSION}"
  fi
  echo mkdir -p "${CONFIG}"
       mkdir -p "${CONFIG}"
  echo mkdir -p "${CONFIG}-${OLDCM3VERSION}"
       mkdir -p "${CONFIG}-${OLDCM3VERSION}"
  echo cp "${CONFIG}"/* "${CONFIG}-${OLDCM3VERSION}"
       cp "${CONFIG}"/* "${CONFIG}-${OLDCM3VERSION}"
}

rm_curent()
{
  if [ "${NOACTION}" != yes ] ; then
    rm -f "${FRONTEND}${ext}"
    if [ "${GCC_BACKEND}" = yes ] ; then
      rm -f "${BACKEND}${ext}"
    fi
    echo rm -rf "${CONFIG}"
         rm -rf "${CONFIG}"
    echo mkdir -p "${CONFIG}"
         mkdir -p "${CONFIG}"
  fi
}

cp_version()
{
  FE="${FRONTEND}-${CM3VERSION}"
  cp_if "${FE}" "${FRONTEND}"
  if [ "${GCC_BACKEND}" = yes ] ; then
    BE="${BACKEND}-${CM3VERSION}"
    cp_if "${BE}" "${BACKEND}"
  fi
  echo mkdir -p "${CONFIG}"
       mkdir -p "${CONFIG}"
  echo mkdir -p "${CONFIG}-${CM3VERSION}"
       mkdir -p "${CONFIG}-${CM3VERSION}"
  echo cp "${CONFIG}-${CM3VERSION}"/* "${CONFIG}"
       cp "${CONFIG}-${CM3VERSION}"/* "${CONFIG}"
}

upgrade()
{
  backup_old
  install_local_as_version
  FE="${FRONTEND}-${CM3VERSION}"
  if "${FE}" -version > /dev/null; then
    true
  else
    echo "${FE} is broken" 1>&2
    exit 2
  fi
  if [ "${GCC_BACKEND}" = yes ] ; then
    BE="${BACKEND}-${CM3VERSION}"
    if "${BE}" --version > /dev/null; then
      true
    else
      echo "${BE} is broken" 1>&2
      exit 2
    fi
  fi
  rm_curent
  cp_version
}

if [ "x${1}" = "x-n" ] ; then
  NOACTION=yes
  shift
fi

if [ "x${1}" = "xupgrade" ] ; then
  upgrade
elif [ "x${1}" = "xrestore" ] ; then
  if [ -z "$2" ] ; then
    echo "please specify a version" 1>&2 
    exit 1
  fi
  CM3VERSION="$2"
  cp_version
elif [ "x${1}" = "xnewversion" ] ; then
  install_local_as_version
elif [ "x${1}" = "xbackup" ] ; then
  backup_old
elif [ "x${1}" = "x" ] ; then
  usage
else
  echo "unknown command: $1" 1>&2
  exit 1
fi

exit 0
```

```
#!/bin/sh

if [ "$SYSINFO_DONE" != "yes" ] ; then

#-----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# mark that we have run (or are about to)

SYSINFO_DONE="yes"

#-----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# determine $root

if [ -n "$ROOT" -a -d "$ROOT" ] ; then
  sysinfo="$ROOT/scripts/sysinfo.sh"
  root="${ROOT}"; export root
else
  root=`pwd`
  while [ -n "$root" -a ! -f "$root/scripts/sysinfo.sh" ] ; do
    root=`dirname $root`
  done
  sysinfo="$root/scripts/sysinfo.sh"
  if [ ! -f "$sysinfo" ] ; then
    echo "scripts/sysinfo.sh not found" 1>&2
    exit 1
  fi
  export root
fi

#-----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# output functions

debug() {
  if [ -n "$CM3_DEBUG" ] ; then
    echo "$*"
  fi
}

header() {
  echo ""
  echo '----------------------------------------------------------------------------'
  echo $@
  echo '----------------------------------------------------------------------------'
  echo ""
}

#-----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Utility function to find first occurrence of executable file in
# $PATH.
# Arguments are filename and default pathname.
# Check for argument count and protect against passing a path as a
# filename. Try to not mangle pathnames with spaces.
 
find_exe() {
  if [ $# -eq 2 -a `basename "$1"` = "$1" ] ; then
    file="$1"
    default="$2"
    IFS=:
    for path in $PATH ; do
      if [ -f "$path/$file" -a -x "$path/$file" ]; then
       echo "$path"
       return 0
      fi
    done
    echo "$default"
  else
    echo
    return 1
  fi
}

#-----------------------------------------------------------------------------

qgrep() {
  egrep $@ >/dev/null 2>/dev/null
}

#-----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# abstraction functions

cygpath() {
  echo "$2"
}

strip_exe() {
  if [ -x /usr/ccs/bin/strip ]; then
    /usr/ccs/bin/strip $@
  else
    strip $@
  fi
}

#-----------------------------------------------------------------------------

find_in_list() {
    a="x`eval echo \\$$1`"
    if [ "$a" = "x" ]; then
        for a in $2; do
            for b in $a ${a}.exe; do
                if type $b >/dev/null 2>/dev/null; then
                    eval $1=$b
                    export $1
                    return
                fi
            done
        done
        echo "none of $2 found"
        exit 1
    fi
}

#-----------------------------------------------------------------------------
build_platform() {
  if [ -z "${BUILD_PLATFORM}" ]; then
    if [ -x ${ROOT}/m3-sys/m3cc/gcc/config.guess ]; then
      BUILD_PLATFORM=`${ROOT}/m3-sys/m3cc/gcc/config.guess`
    else
      BUILD_PLATFORM="`uname -p`-unknown-`uname -s``uname -r`"
    fi
  fi
  export BUILD_PLATFORM
```

```
% Darwin has no m3gdb support and -gstabs and -gstabs+ cause

% Plain -g causes cm3cg to access violate attempting to generate Dwarf symbols.

    return not stale(x, x)

proc configure_assembler() is
  if defined("SYSTEM_ASM")
    return
  end
  SYSTEM_ASM = "/usr/libexec/gcc/darwin/" & DarwinArch & "/as"

  % NOTE: Some versions of m3cg are incompatible with LLVM assembler that gcc -x assembler

    end

    %SYSTEM_ASM = "as -arch " & DarwinArch & " -force_cpusubtype_ALL"
  end
  %SYSTEM_ASM = SYSTEM_CC_ASM & " -v -c -x assembler"
end
```

```
#!/bin/sh

if [ -n "$ROOT" -a -d "$ROOT" ] ; then
  sysinfo="$ROOT/scripts/sysinfo.sh"
  root="${ROOT}"; export root
else
  root=`pwd`
  while [ -n "$root" -a ! -f "$root/scripts/sysinfo.sh" ] ; do
    root=`dirname $root`
  done
  sysinfo="$root/scripts/sysinfo.sh"
  if [ ! -f "$sysinfo" ] ; then
    echo "scripts/sysinfo.sh not found" 1>&2
    exit 1
  fi
  export root
fi

. "$sysinfo"
. "$ROOT/scripts/pkginfo.sh"
. "$ROOT/scripts/pkgcmds.sh"

set -e
set -x

for f in ${ROOT}/m3-sys/cminstall/src/config/*; do
  rm -f "${INSTALLROOT}/bin/`basename ${f}`" > /dev/null
done
mkdir -p "${INSTALLROOT}/bin/config"
for f in ${ROOT}/m3-sys/cminstall/src/config/*; do
  [ -f ${f} ] && cp "${f}" "${INSTALLROOT}/bin/config"
done
(
  echo "INSTALL_ROOT = path() & \"/..\""
  echo "include(path() & \"/config/${TARGET}\")"
) > "${INSTALLROOT}/bin/cm3.cfg"
```

```
#!/bin/sh

#set -e
#set -x

if [ -n "$ROOT" -a -d "$ROOT" ] ; then
  sysinfo="$ROOT/scripts/sysinfo.sh"
  root="${ROOT}"; export root
else
  root=`pwd`
  while [ -n "$root" -a ! -f "$root/scripts/sysinfo.sh" ] ; do
    root=`dirname $root`
  done
  sysinfo="$root/scripts/sysinfo.sh"
  if [ ! -f "$sysinfo" ] ; then
    echo "scripts/sysinfo.sh not found" 1>&2
    exit 1
  fi
  export root
fi

. "$sysinfo"
. "$root/scripts/pkginfo.sh"
. "$root/scripts/pkgcmds.sh"

USAGE="
  `basename $0` [ generic_options ] [ generic_cmd ]

  builds a new compiler from a new set of sources, using an existing compiler
  possibly an old compiler

  generic_options:
${GEN_OPTS}"
  
show_usage $@

OPTIONS=`extract_options $@`

EXE=""
if [ "${TARGET}" = "NT386" \
    -o "${TARGET}" = "I386_CYGWIN"  -o "${TARGET}" = "I386_NT"  -o "${TARGET}" = "I386_MINGW" \
    -o "${TARGET}" = "AMD64_CYGWIN" -o "${TARGET}" = "AMD64_NT" -o "${TARGET}" = "AMD64_MINGW" ]; then
  EXE=".exe"
fi

install_compiler() {
  M3CONFIG="${INSTALLROOT}/bin/cm3.cfg" "${root}/m3-sys/cm3/${TARGET}/cm3${EXE}" --version || exit 1
  if [ "x${GCC_BACKEND}" = xyes ]; then
    "${root}/m3-sys/m3cc/${TARGET}/cm3cg${EXE}" --help -version >/dev/null || exit 1
  fi
  mkdir -p "${INSTALLROOT}/bin" || exit 1
  cp "${root}/m3-sys/cm3/${TARGET}/cm3${EXE}" "${INSTALLROOT}/bin/cm3${EXE}" || exit 1
  if [ "x${GCC_BACKEND}" = xyes ]; then
    cp "${root}/m3-sys/m3cc/${TARGET}/cm3cg${EXE}" "${INSTALLROOT}/bin/cm3cg${EXE}" || exit 1
  fi
  install_config || exit 1
}

# delete lingering cm3cg in case old compiler/config uses it
for a in cm3cg gcc/m3cgc1; do
    for b in "" .exe; do
        rm "$root/m3-sys/m3cc/${TARGET}/$a$b" || true
    done
done

# Build the compiler with the installed version of the runtime;
# do _not_ compile m3core and libm3 here.
# Start with the front end.
P="sysutils set m3middle m3objfile m3linker m3back \
   m3front m3quake cm3 mklib m3cggen"
"$root/scripts/do-pkg.sh" "$@" "realclean" ${P} || exit 1
"$root/scripts/do-pkg.sh" "$@" "buildship" ${P} || exit 1

if [ "x${GCC_BACKEND}" = xyes ]; then
  # Continue with the backend, if needed. Deliberately don't ship it!
  # "$root/m3-sys/m3cggen/${TARGET}/m3cggen" > "$root/m3-sys/m3cc/gcc/gcc/m3cg/m3cg.h"
  "$root/scripts/do-pkg.sh" "$@" "build" m3cc || exit 1
fi

# Install the compiler binaries all together (cm3, cm3cg, config).
install_compiler || exit 1

# Rebuild with the new compiler.
# No need for m3cc since it is written in C (ie no compiler change).

P="m3core libm3 ${P}"
"$root/scripts/do-pkg.sh" "$@" "realclean" ${P} || exit 1
"$root/scripts/do-pkg.sh" "$@" "buildship" ${P} || exit 1

# Do another compiler upgrade.
install_compiler || exit 1
```

```
map_action() {
  skip=true
  while [ -n "$1" -a "$skip" = "true" ] ; do
    case "$1" in
      -*) shift;;
      *) skip=false
    esac
  done
  if [ -z "$1" ] ; then
    ACTION="${BUILDLOCAL}"
  elif [ "$1" = "build" -o "$1" = "buildlocal" ] ; then
    ACTION="${BUILDLOCAL}"
  elif [ "$1" = "buildglobal" -o "$1" = "buildship" ] ; then
    ACTION="${BUILDGLOBAL} && ${SHIP}"
  elif [ "$1" = "ship" ] ; then
    ACTION="${SHIP}"
  elif [ "$1" = "clean" -o "$1" = "cleanlocal" ] ; then
    ACTION="${CLEANLOCAL}"
  elif [ "$1" = "cleanglobal" ] ; then
    ACTION="${CLEANGLOBAL}"
  elif [ "$1" = "realclean" ] ; then
    ACTION="${REALCLEAN}"
  else
    if [ "${IGNORE_MISS}" = "yes" ] ; then
      ACTION="${BUILDLOCAL}"
    else
      echo "unknown action: $1" 1>&2
      exit 1
    fi
  fi
  echo "${ACTION}"
}

add_action_opts() {
  skip=true
  while [ -n "$1" -a "$skip" = "true" ] ; do
    case "$1" in
      -*) shift;;
      *) skip=false
    esac
  done
  ARGS="";
  if [ "$1" = "clean" -o "$1" = "cleanlocal" ] ; then
    ARGS="-k"
  elif [ "$1" = "cleanglobal" ] ; then
    ARGS="-k"
  elif [ "$1" = "realclean" ] ; then
    ARGS="-k"
  fi
  echo "${ARGS}"
}

extract_options() {
  RES=""
  while [ -n "$1" ] ; do
    case "$1" in
      -*) RES="${RES} $1";;
    esac
    shift
  done
  echo "$RES"
}

get_args() {
  skip=true
  while [ -n "$1" -a "$skip" = "true" ] ; do
    case "$1" in
      -*) shift;;
      *) skip=false
    esac
  done
  if [ "$1" = "build" -o "$1" = "buildlocal" ] ; then
    shift
  elif [ "$1" = "buildglobal" -o "$1" = "buildship" ] ; then
    shift
  elif [ "$1" = "ship" ] ; then
    shift
  elif [ "$1" = "clean" -o "$1" = "cleanlocal" ] ; then
    shift
  elif [ "$1" = "cleanglobal" ] ; then
    shift
  elif [ "$1" = "realclean" ] ; then
    shift
  fi
  ARGS=""
  while [ -n "$1" ] ; do
    case "$1" in
      -*) echo "encountered option after command: $1" 1>&2;;
      *) ARGS="${ARGS} $1";;
    esac
    shift
  done
  echo "$ARGS"
}

  buildglobal | buildship     build a package without overrides and ship it
  ship                        ship a package
```

```
    local p = path()

                  (p & SL & TARGET),
                  (p & SL & "cm3.exe.config"),

        end
    end

        if defined("ROOT")

        end
        if not equal($CM3_ROOT, "")

        error("Neither the variable ROOT nor environment variables ROOT or CM3_ROOT is defined.")

    CM3SetSourceRoot()

    Result = CM3ConfigInclude(ROOT & SL & "m3-sys" & SL & "cminstall" & SL & "src" & SL & "config" & SL & TARGET)

        return Result
    end

    %
    % Give up.
    %
    error("unable to find a configuration file for (" & INSTALL_ROOT & ", " & ROOT & ", " & TARGET & ")")
```

<sub>⏱️ 12m 42s</sub>

### 💬 Copilot

Now I have a clear picture. Let me explain the approach, then execute it.

**The situation:**
- Machine: ARM64 Darwin (Apple Silicon)  
- Existing `~/cm3`: AMD64_DARWIN cm3 running under Rosetta
- Goal: native ARM64_DARWIN cm3 at `~/cm3-ARM64_DARWIN`

**The strategy:** CM3 uses a C backend — the Modula-3 compiler generates C code, which `clang` then compiles. With `TARGET=ARM64_DARWIN`, the config passes `-arch arm64` to clang, so the AMD64 cm3 (via Rosetta) can produce native ARM64 binaries. We use `buildlocal` (`cm3 -build -override`) to build everything from workspace sources so we don't need pre-installed ARM64 libraries.

```
if not defined ("M3TESTS")

  foreach f in _FloatPieces{TARGET}
```

```
UNSAFE MODULE ExtendedFloat;

(* This module implements the operations on IEEE quad precision reals 
   that do not depend on the operating system. *)

IMPORT ExtendedRep AS Rep;
IMPORT DragonT, Word, Ctypes, Convert;

(* Users needing scalb or sqrt should consult QuadMath.i3 in libm3 *)
PROCEDURE Scalb (x : T; n: INTEGER) : T = <* NOWARN *>
  BEGIN
    <* ASSERT FALSE *>
  END Scalb;

PROCEDURE Sqrt (x: T): T = <* NOWARN *>
  BEGIN
    <* ASSERT FALSE *>
  END Sqrt;

PROCEDURE Logb (x: T): T =
  CONST Log_of_zero = Rep.T {sign := 1, exponent := 16_7FFF,
                             significand0 := 0, significand1 := 0,
                             significand2 := 0, significand3 := 0};
  VAR ans: T;                             
  BEGIN
    CASE Class (x) OF
    | IEEEClass.SignalingNaN, 
      IEEEClass.QuietNaN =>
        RETURN x;
    | IEEEClass.Infinity => 
        RETURN ABS (x);
    | IEEEClass.Zero =>
        LOOPHOLE (ans, Rep.T) := Log_of_zero;
        RETURN ans;
    | IEEEClass.Normal =>
        RETURN FLOAT (LOOPHOLE (x, Rep.T).exponent - 16383, T);
    | IEEEClass.Denormal =>
        RETURN -16382.0X0;
    END;
  END Logb;

(* See the file COPYRIGHT for a full description.                            *)
(*                                                                           *)
(* Last modified on Mon Jun 21 12:17:47 PDT 1993 by mcjones                  *)
(*      modified on Fri May  7 16:08:10 PDT 1993 by muller                   *)

MODULE ExtendedFloat;

(* This module implements the operations on IEEE extended precision reals 
   that do not depend on the operating system. 
   We assume that EXTENDED = LONGREAL. *)

IMPORT LongFloat, FloatMode;

PROCEDURE Scalb (x: T; n: INTEGER): T RAISES {FloatMode.Trap} =
  BEGIN
    RETURN FLOAT (LongFloat.Scalb (FLOAT (x, LONGREAL), n), T);
  END Scalb;

PROCEDURE Logb (x: T): T RAISES {FloatMode.Trap} =
  BEGIN
    RETURN FLOAT (LongFloat.Logb (FLOAT (x, LONGREAL)), T);
  END Logb;

PROCEDURE ILogb (x: T): INTEGER =
  BEGIN
    RETURN LongFloat.ILogb (FLOAT (x, LONGREAL));
  END ILogb;
```

```
(* Copyright (C) 2026 Peter McKinna. All rights reserved. *)
(* See file COPYRIGHT-BSD for details. *)

INTERFACE ExtendedRep;

(* This interface describes the layout of IEEE quad precision reals
   on little endian machines *)

TYPE
  T = RECORD 
    significand3 : BITS 32 FOR [-16_7fffffff-1 .. 16_7fffffff] := 0;
    significand2 : BITS 32 FOR [-16_7fffffff-1 .. 16_7fffffff] := 0;
    significand1 : BITS 32 FOR [-16_7fffffff-1 .. 16_7fffffff] := 0;
    significand0 : BITS 16 FOR [0..16_FFFF]                    := 0;
    exponent     : BITS 15 FOR [0..16_7FFF]                    := 0;
    sign         : BITS  1 FOR [0..1]                          := 0;
  END;

CONST
  NegInf = T { sign := 1, exponent := 16_7FFF };
  PosInf = T { sign := 0, exponent := 16_7FFF };
  Nan    = T { sign := 0, exponent := 16_7FFF, significand0 := 1 };

END ExtendedRep.
```

<sub>⏱️ 31m 47s</sub>

### 💬 Copilot

Now I understand the issue completely. ARM64 doesn't have x87 80-bit extended precision — `EXTENDED = LONGREAL = 64-bit`. Both `float/IEEE/m3makefile` and `float/IEEE-le/m3makefile` select `ext128` (80/128-bit extended) for all non-NT targets, but ARM64 needs `ext64`. Let me fix both files:

```
        (* DefineIfNotDefined: overridable from command line with -D *)
```

<sub>⏱️ 36m 39s</sub>

### 💬 Copilot

Now I understand the issue. The AMD64 cm3 binary (running under Rosetta) calls `uname` which returns `x86_64`, so it pre-defines `TARGET=AMD64_DARWIN` before the config file is even read. The `if not defined("TARGET")` in cm3.cfg is therefore always false, and M3CONFIG alone can't change the TARGET for actual builds.

The fix is to pass `-D TARGET=ARM64_DARWIN` explicitly on the cm3 command line.

---

The root cause is clear: `-D TARGET=ARM64_DARWIN` needs to be on the `cm3` command line — the `-D` flags are applied before `DefineIfNotDefined`, so they take precedence.

```
PROCEDURE ProcessDefine (arg: TEXT;  wr: Wr.T)
  RAISES {Wr.Failure, Thread.Alerted} =
  VAR len := Text.Length (arg);  eq: INTEGER;  sym, val: TEXT;
  BEGIN
    IF (len <= 2) THEN
      Msg.UsageError ("missing argument to \"-D\" option");
      RETURN;
    END;

    eq := Text.FindChar (arg, '=');
    IF (eq < 0) THEN
      (* -Dsymbol ==>  symbol = TRUE *)
      EVAL defs.put(Text.Sub (arg, 2), "TRUE");
      IF wr # NIL THEN
        Out (wr, Text.Sub (arg, 2), " = TRUE");
      END;
      RETURN;
    END;

    sym := Text.Sub (arg, 2, eq-2);
    val := Text.Sub (arg, eq+1);
    len := Text.Length (val);

    EVAL defs.put(sym, val);
```

```
proc configure_c_compiler() is

  if defined("SYSTEM_CC")
    return
  end

  %
  % older compiler doesn't like -m32 or -arch
  %
  % gcc -c -m32 -x c /dev/null
  % cc1: error: invalid option ‘m32’
  %
  % fPIC is not usually needed here.
  % It is the default for Apple gcc and left
  % here in case user is using a self-built FSF gcc.
  %
  % g++ 1.c used to compile successfully as C++, on MacOSX 10.5.8.
  % On MacOS X 10.10.4 Yosemite it errors. -x c++ fixes it.
  % But do not use that with linking, otherwise all the object files are interpreted as C++.
  %
  % Clang assembler gives warnings for -fPIC, which appears meaningless (review for arm/arm64).
  %
  %SYSTEM_CC = "gcc -g -fPIC"
  SYSTEM_CC = "g++ -g -fPIC"
  SYSTEM_CC = SYSTEM_CC & " -Wall"
  SYSTEM_CC = SYSTEM_CC & " -Werror"
  SYSTEM_CC = SYSTEM_CC & " -Wno-return-type"
  SYSTEM_CC = SYSTEM_CC & " -Wno-missing-braces"
  %SYSTEM_CC = SYSTEM_CC & " -Wextra"
  %SYSTEM_CC = SYSTEM_CC & " -Wno-missing-field-initializers"
  %SYSTEM_CC = SYSTEM_CC & " -Wno-unused-parameter"
  % Usocket.c:31: warning: comparison of unsigned expression < 0 is always false
  SYSTEM_CC_ASM = "g++"
  %SYSTEM_CC_ASM = "gcc"
  local m = " -m" & {"32BITS":"32","64BITS":"64"}{WORD_SIZE}
  local arch = " -arch " & DarwinArch
  if not equal(try_exec("@" & SYSTEM_CC & m & " -c -x c /dev/null -o /dev/null 2>&1 | fgrep \"cc1: error: invalid option \\\`32'\" >/dev/null"), 0)
    SYSTEM_CC = SYSTEM_CC & m
    SYSTEM_CC_ASM = SYSTEM_CC_ASM & m
  end
  if not equal(try_exec("@" & SYSTEM_CC & arch & " -c -x c /dev/null -o /dev/null 2>&1 | fgrep \"cc1: error: unrecognized command line option \\\\\"-arch\\\\\"\" >/dev/null"), 0)
    SYSTEM_CC = SYSTEM_CC & arch
    SYSTEM_CC_ASM = SYSTEM_CC_ASM & arch
  end
  SYSTEM_CC_LD = SYSTEM_CC
  SYSTEM_CC = SYSTEM_CC & " -x c++"
  configure_c_compiler_common()
  %write("SYSTEM_CC is " & SYSTEM_CC)
end

if not defined("SYSTEM_LIBTOOL")
    readonly SYSTEM_LIBTOOL = "/usr/bin/libtool"
end
```

$ ROOT=/Users/hosking/Downloads/cm3-d5.12.0
INST=$HOME/cm3-ARM64_DARWIN

# Install library packages (copy .a and .m3x files)
for pkg_path in \
  m3-libs/m3core:m3core \
  m3-libs/libm3:libm3 \
  m3-libs/set:set \
  m3-libs/sysutils:sysutils \
  m3-sys/m3middle:m3middle \

  m3-sys/m3quake:m3quake
do
  src_pkg="${pkg_path%%:*}"
  pkg_name="${pkg_path##*:}"
  src="$ROOT/$src_pkg/ARM64_DARWIN"
  dst="$INST/pkg/$pkg_name/ARM64_DARWIN"
  mkdir -p "$dst"
  cp -f "$src"/*.a "$src"/*.m3x "$dst"/ 2>/dev/null && echo "installed $pkg_name" || echo "FAILED $pkg_name"
done

<sub>⏱️ 54m 34s</sub>

### 💬 Copilot

All binaries are native ARM64. Here's a summary of everything that was done and the fixes required:

---

## Result

`~/cm3-ARM64_DARWIN/bin/cm3` is now a native ARM64 Mach-O executable (`host: ARM64_DARWIN`, `target: ARM64_DARWIN`).

## Fixes applied

**1. Source tree — float ext64/ext128 selection** (3 m3makefiles):
- `m3-libs/m3core/src/float/IEEE/m3makefile`
- `m3-libs/m3core/src/float/IEEE-le/m3makefile`  
- `m3-libs/libm3/src/random/IEEE/m3makefile`

Added `or equal (TARGET_ARCH, "ARM64")` to the ext64 condition — ARM64 has no x87 extended precision, so EXTENDED = LONGREAL = 64-bit.

**2. Build invocation** — must pass `-DTARGET=ARM64_DARWIN` on the `cm3` command line (via `BUILDARGS`/`SHIPARGS`). The AMD64 cm3 binary calls `uname` (returns `x86_64` under Rosetta) before reading cm3.cfg, pre-defining `TARGET=AMD64_DARWIN`. A `-D` flag overrides this.

**3. `~/cm3-ARM64_DARWIN/bin/config/ARM64_DARWIN`** — added:
```quake
configure_c_compiler()
SYSTEM_CC = SYSTEM_CC & " -include " & INSTALL_ROOT & "/include/m3_arm64_compat.h"
```
And created `~/cm3-ARM64_DARWIN/include/m3_arm64_compat.h` to define `Infinity`/`NaN`, since the pre-built AMD64 cm3 binary generates C code using the GCC extension `Infinity` without defining it, which clang on ARM64 rejects.

<sub>⏱️ 58m 35s</sub>

### 💬 Copilot

The issue is clear: M3C.m3 generates `typedef _Float128 EXTENDED;` for non-MSVC (including ARM64 Darwin), but Apple clang doesn't have `_Float128`. Also the Infinity/NaN redefinition since new cm3 defines those itself.

Two-part fix in the compat header:

<sub>⏱️ 58m 35s</sub>

```
/* ARM64 Darwin compatibility: define GCC extension 'Infinity' used by CM3 C backend */
#ifndef Infinity
#define Infinity (__builtin_inf())
#endif
#ifndef NaN
#define NaN (__builtin_nan(""))
#endif
```

```
168.        Addendum: Actually libunwind circa 2010 is mostly portable.
169.        Having a stack walker theoretically speeds up everything nicely.  If
170.        you are familiar with NT exception handling, all but x86 have a stack
171.        walker.  Not having a stack walker means that functions that have
172.        try/except/finally/raise incur a codegen cost even if there is never a
173.        raise -- for having the try.  Having a stack walker means "zero cost"
174.        for exception handling code that does not actually raise an exception.
175. 
176.        If there is NOT a stack walker, prologues/epilogues for functions that
177.        try/except/finally/raise call PushEFrame / PopEFrame, essentially to
178.        build a walkable parallel stack.
179. 
180.        If there is a stack walker, then raise can discover what PushEFrame /
181.        PopEFrame effectively recorded.

183.        NT/x86 has a highly optimized equivalent of PushEFrame / PopEFrame, not
184.        currently used by Modula-3.
```

```
(* See file COPYRIGHT-BSD for details. *)

INTERFACE ExtendedRep;

(* This interface describes the layout of IEEE quad precision reals
   on little endian machines *)

TYPE
  T = RECORD 
    significand3 : BITS 32 FOR [-16_7fffffff-1 .. 16_7fffffff] := 0;
    significand2 : BITS 32 FOR [-16_7fffffff-1 .. 16_7fffffff] := 0;
    significand1 : BITS 32 FOR [-16_7fffffff-1 .. 16_7fffffff] := 0;
    significand0 : BITS 16 FOR [0..16_FFFF]                    := 0;
    exponent     : BITS 15 FOR [0..16_7FFF]                    := 0;
    sign         : BITS  1 FOR [0..1]                          := 0;
  END;

CONST
  NegInf = T { sign := 1, exponent := 16_7FFF };
  PosInf = T { sign := 0, exponent := 16_7FFF };
  Nan    = T { sign := 0, exponent := 16_7FFF, significand0 := 1 };

END ExtendedRep.
```

<sub>⏱️ 70m 37s</sub>

### 💬 Copilot

Now I understand the root cause: the AMD64 cm3 (pre-built) had `typedef /*long*/ double EXTENDED;` (EXTENDED=64-bit), which is why stage 1 worked. Our new ARM64 cm3 was compiled from source that has `typedef _Float128 EXTENDED;` (128-bit), breaking stage 2.

The fix requires two source changes: `Target.m3` (make EXTENDED=64 for ARM64) and `M3C.m3` (emit `double` not `_Float128` for ARM64), then re-run stage 1 with the AMD64 cm3:

```
readonly TARGET = "ARM64_DARWIN"

readonly DarwinArch = "arm64"

include("ARM64.common")
include("Darwin.common")

M3_PARALLEL_BACK = 20

% The CM3 C backend generates code that uses _Float128 (a GCC/GNU extension)
% for the EXTENDED float type, and calls *q() quad-precision math functions.
% Apple clang on ARM64 Darwin lacks these; inject a compat header that maps
% them to their double equivalents via -include.
configure_c_compiler()
SYSTEM_CC = SYSTEM_CC & " -include " & INSTALL_ROOT & "/include/m3_arm64_compat.h"

SYSTEM_LIBS{"ODBC"} = ["-L/opt/homebrew/lib", "-liodbc", "-liodbcinst"]

SYSTEM_LIBS{"OPENGL"} = [ "-Wl,-dylib_file," & LIBGL_DYLIB & ":" & LIBGL_DYLIB,
```

$ SRC=/Users/hosking/Downloads/cm3-d5.12.0
INST=~/cm3-ARM64_DARWIN

# Package map: source-path → install-pkg-name
install_pkg() {
  local srcdir="$1" pkgname="$2"
  local destdir="$INST/pkg/$pkgname/ARM64_DARWIN"
  mkdir -p "$destdir"
  # Copy .a and .m3x (interface export) files
  cp -f "$srcdir"/ARM64_DARWIN/*.a "$destdir"/ 2>/dev/null
  cp -f "$srcdir"/ARM64_DARWIN/*.m3x "$destdir"/ 2>/dev/null
  # Copy public .i3 headers to pkg dir
  cp -f "$srcdir"/ARM64_DARWIN/*.i3 "$destdir"/ 2>/dev/null
  echo "$pkgname: $(ls $destdir/*.a 2>/dev/null | wc -l | tr -d ' ') .a, $(ls $destdir/*.m3x 2>/dev/null | wc -l | tr -d ' ') .m3x"
}

install_pkg $SRC/m3-libs/m3core      m3core
install_pkg $SRC/m3-libs/libm3       libm3
install_pkg $SRC/m3-libs/set         set

<sub>⏱️ 218m 31s</sub>

### 💬 Copilot

Here's a concise summary of all changes needed:

---

## Changes to get from stage 1 → stage 2 (and beyond)

The core problem: the current CM3 source assumes EXTENDED = 128-bit (`_Float128`, a GCC extension), but Apple clang on ARM64 has no `_Float128` and no quad-precision math functions.

### Source tree changes

**`m3-sys/m3middle/src/Target.m3`**
- Extended the EXTENDED=64-bit condition from `IF OS_name = "WIN32"` to also cover ARM64 targets
- Without this, the running cm3 had `Target.Extended.size = 128` baked in, causing a `LOOPHOLE` size mismatch (128 ≠ 64) when compiling `IEEESpecial.m3`

**`m3-sys/m3back/src/M3C.m3`** (the C backend code generator)
- `typedef _Float128 EXTENDED` → `typedef double EXTENDED` for `__aarch64__` (Apple clang lacks `_Float128`)
- Added `#ifndef`/`#endif` guards around `#define Infinity INFINITY` and `#define NaN NAN` (prevent redefinition conflicts with the compat header)
- Changed `#ifdef _WIN32` → `#if defined(_WIN32) || defined(__aarch64__)` in all four `m3_round`/`m3_trunc`/`m3_floor`/`m3_ceil` helpers — avoids calling non-existent `llroundq`/`truncq`/`floorq`/`ceilq` on Apple clang

**`m3-libs/m3core/src/float/IEEE/m3makefile`**  
**`m3-libs/m3core/src/float/IEEE-le/m3makefile`**  
**`m3-libs/libm3/src/random/IEEE/m3makefile`**
- Added ARM64 to the condition selecting `ext64` (64-bit EXTENDED representation) instead of `ext128`

### Installed config changes (`~/cm3/`)

**`include/m3_arm64_compat.h`** *(injected via `-include` in `SYSTEM_CC`)*
- `#define _Float128 double` — makes generated `typedef _Float128 EXTENDED` compile
- Macro aliases `truncq`/`floorq`/`ceilq`/`llroundq` → `trunc`/`floor`/`ceil`/`llround`
- `#ifndef` guards on `Infinity`/`NaN` definitions

**`bin/config/ARM64_DARWIN`**
- `M3_PARALLEL_BACK = 1` — the AMD64 cm3 running under Rosetta 2 deadlocks in `pthread_create` when trying to spawn 20 parallel clang threads; setting this to 1 forces sequential compilation

<sub>⏱️ 220m 9s</sub>

### 👤 User

What would cause pthread deadlocks under Rosetta 2 emulation?

---

<sub>⏱️ 220m 24s</sub>

### 💬 Copilot

This is an interesting systems question. Here's what's likely happening:

## Why `pthread_create` deadlocks under Rosetta 2

### What Rosetta 2 does
Rosetta 2 translates AMD64 instructions to ARM64 at runtime using two mechanisms:
- **AOT (Ahead-of-Time)**: translates the binary on first launch, caches result
- **JIT**: translates code paths not covered by AOT at runtime

### The likely culprit: the Rosetta runtime lock

Rosetta 2 maintains internal state for the JIT translator. When a translated AMD64 binary calls `pthread_create`, Rosetta must:
1. Set up the new thread in the translated environment
2. Ensure the JIT translator is available for that thread
3. Register the thread with Rosetta's runtime

This involves **Rosetta-internal locks**. The deadlock pattern seen in the sample was:

```
cm3 → Thread.Fork → ThreadPThread__thread_create → pthread_create → ??? (Rosetta runtime)
```

The `???` at address `0x7ff89e8d4a24` is Rosetta's own translated runtime code — it was **stuck holding or waiting on a lock inside Rosetta's JIT/thread management code**.

### Why 20 threads specifically triggers it

CM3's `Builder__ForceAllPromisesInParallel` tries to `pthread_create` 20 threads **simultaneously** (one per clang invocation). Rosetta's internal thread registration likely uses a **non-reentrant lock** or has a **bounded thread pool** for JIT state. Spawning 20 threads at once from translated code overwhelms this.

### Why native ARM64 cm3 has no problem

The native ARM64 cm3 (stage 2+) calls `pthread_create` directly — no Rosetta translation layer, no JIT lock, no deadlock. `M3_PARALLEL_BACK = 1` is only needed for the AMD64 (Rosetta) stage 1 build.

### You could probably raise it safely for Rosetta builds

The safe fix for a future stage 1 would be a small value like `M3_PARALLEL_BACK = 2` or `4` rather than `1` — fewer simultaneous `pthread_create` calls are less likely to exhaust Rosetta's internal thread registration capacity. But `1` is guaranteed safe.

<sub>⏱️ 243m 6s</sub>

### 💬 Copilot

**Short answer: No — ARM64_DARWIN has no stack walker.** It falls back to the `ex_frame` mechanism.

Here's what the code shows:

### What ARM64_DARWIN actually uses

The `m3makefile` only enables the real stack walker (`ex_stack` + libunwind) for a single target:
```
readonly HAS_STACK_WALKER = {
  "AMD64_LINUX" : TRUE,
}
```

ARM64_DARWIN is not in that table, so it always falls through to `ex_frame`. And `ex_frame/RTStackC.c` is the **stub implementation** — every function just calls `abort()`:

```c
void RTStack__CurFrame(...)  { abort(); }
void RTStack__PrevFrame(...) { abort(); }
void RTStack__Unwind(...)    { abort(); }
```

`common/RTMachine.i3` (which ARM64_DARWIN inherits since there's no platform-specific override) declares `Has_stack_walker = FALSE`.

### What `ex_frame` does instead

Exception handling still *works* — the CM3 C backend generates a **linked list of exception frames** at every try/except/finally boundary (pushed/popped via `setjmp`). `RTExFrame.m3` walks this linked list when raising an exception. It's entirely independent of the native call stack — no DWARF unwinding needed.

### The irony

macOS ARM64 has an *excellent* native unwinder. Apple's libunwind is baked into `libSystem.B.dylib` — no `-lunwind` link flag needed, just `#include \<libunwind.h\>`. The compact unwind info and DWARF tables emitted by clang are first-class. AMD64_LINUX had to link against an external libunwind (`-L/usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu`); Darwin has it for free.

### What it would take to add one

1. Create `m3-libs/m3core/src/runtime/ARM64_DARWIN/RTMachine.i3` with `Has_stack_walker = TRUE` and a `FrameInfo` record matching the libunwind cursor layout (essentially copy AMD64_LINUX's)
2. Create `ARM64_DARWIN/RTStackC.c` implementing `RTStack__CurFrame`/`PrevFrame`/`Unwind` using `unw_step()`/`unw_get_reg()` — again very close to AMD64_LINUX
3. Add `"ARM64_DARWIN" : TRUE` to `HAS_STACK_WALKER` in the m3makefile
4. Add `SYSTEM_LIBS{"UNWIND"} = []` (empty — it's in libSystem already) to the ARM64_DARWIN config
5. Implement a personality function (`__m3_personality_v0`) for the C++ EH ABI

The AMD64_LINUX implementation is a good template — it's the only one that's been modernised to use libunwind properly.

```
102.    known. */
103. 
104. char* RTStack__ProcName (Frame *f)
105. {
106.   int res;
107.   char *name;
108.   long name_len = 50;
109.   unw_word_t ofp;
110. 
111.   name = (char *) malloc(name_len);
112.   //there is a small mem leak here but as it is only called
113.   //during debugex of the stack unwinder it should be fine.
114. 
115.   res = unw_get_proc_name(f->cursor, name, name_len, &ofp);
116.   if (res == 0) {
117.     return name;
118.   } else {
119.     return 0;
120.   }
121. }
122. 
123. /*---------------------------------------------------------------------------*/
124. /* PROCEDURE GetThreadFrame (VAR f: Frame;  start: ADDRESS;  len: INTEGER);
125.    Return in "f" the frame of the thread whose machine state is in bytes
126.    [start .. start+len).  Returns with f.pc=NIL on failure. */
127. 
128. void RTStack__GetThreadFrame (Frame *f, char *start, int len)
129. {
130.   // not implemented 
131.   abort();
132. }
133. 
134. /*---------------------------------------------------------------------------*/
135. /* PROCEDURE CurrentFrame (VAR(*OUT*) f: Frame)
136.  * returns the frame that corresponds to its caller. */
137. 
138. void RTStack__CurFrame (Frame *f)
139. {
140.   unw_context_t *uc;
141.   unw_cursor_t *cursor;
142.   unw_word_t ip, sp = 0;
143. 
144.   //we alloc in m3 otherwise a serious memory leak 
145.   //uc = (unw_context_t *) malloc(sizeof(unw_context_t));
146.   //cursor = (unw_cursor_t *) malloc(sizeof(unw_cursor_t));
147.   uc = (unw_context_t *) RTException__AllocBuf(sizeof(unw_context_t));
148.   cursor = (unw_cursor_t *) RTException__AllocBuf(sizeof(unw_cursor_t));
149. 
150.   f->lock = FrameLock;
151.   unw_getcontext(uc);
152.   unw_init_local(cursor, uc);
153.   unw_get_reg(cursor, UNW_REG_IP, &ip);
154.   unw_get_reg(cursor, UNW_REG_SP, &sp);
155.   
156.   f->cursor = cursor;
157.   f->pc = ip;
158.   f->sp = sp;
159.   RTStack__GetProcInfo(f);
160. 
161.   if (f->lock != FrameLock) abort ();
162. }
163. 
164. /*---------------------------------------------------------------------------*/
165. /* PROCEDURE PreviousFrame (READONLY callee: Frame;  VAR(*OUT*)caller: Frame)
166.    Return the stack frame that called "callee".  Returns with pc = NIL if
167.    "callee" is the first frame on the stack or its predecessor is ill-formed.
168.    */
169. 
170. void RTStack__PrevFrame (Frame* callee, Frame* caller)
171. {
172.   unw_word_t ip, sp = 0;
173.   int res;
174. 
175.   if (!callee->cursor) abort();
176. 
177.   if (callee->lock != FrameLock) abort ();
178.   *caller = *callee;
179. 
180.   res = unw_step(caller->cursor);
181.   if (res > 0) {
182.     unw_get_reg(caller->cursor, UNW_REG_IP, &ip);
183.     unw_get_reg(caller->cursor, UNW_REG_SP, &sp);
184.     
185.     caller->pc = ip;
186.     caller->sp = sp;
187.     RTStack__GetProcInfo(caller);
188. 
189.   } else {
190.     caller->pc = 0;
191.     caller->sp = 0;
192.   }
193.   if (caller->lock != FrameLock) abort ();
194. }
195. 
196. /*---------------------------------------------------------------------------*/
197. /* PROCEDURE Unwind (READONLY f: Frame);
198.    Restore the machine state back to the frame "f".  All callee-saved
199.    registers must be restored to the state they were in when frame "f"
200.    made its last call. */
201. 
202. void RTStack__Unwind (Frame *target)
203. {
204.   int res;
205. 
206.   if (!target->cursor) abort();
207.   if (target->lock != FrameLock) abort ();
208.   
209.   //set the IP to landingPad 
210.   unw_set_reg(target->cursor, UNW_REG_IP, target->landingPad);
211.   
212.   //set the eh register zero to return the exception object
213.   unw_set_reg(target->cursor,
214. 	      __builtin_eh_return_data_regno(EHObjRegNo),
215. 	      target->exceptionRef);
216.  
217.   //set the eh register one to the tTypeIndex for gcc
218.   unw_set_reg(target->cursor,
219. 	      __builtin_eh_return_data_regno(EHTypeRegNo),
220. 	      target->tTypeIndex);
221. 
222.   res = unw_resume(target->cursor);
223.   //success means unreachable from here
224.   if (res < 0) {
225.     printf("RTStack__Unwind - unw_resume error\n");
226.     abort();
227.   }
228. }
229. 
230. /*
231. //a test of generating a backtrace with libunwind.
232. //
233. void show_backtrace (void) {
234.   unw_cursor_t cursor; unw_context_t uc;
235.   unw_word_t ip, sp;
236. 
237.   int ret;
238.   char name[50];
239.   size_t name_len = 50;
240.   unw_word_t ofp;
241. 
242.   unw_getcontext(&uc);
243.   unw_init_local(&cursor, &uc);
244.   while (unw_step(&cursor) > 0) {
245.     unw_get_reg(&cursor, UNW_REG_IP, &ip);
246.     unw_get_reg(&cursor, UNW_REG_SP, &sp);
247.     printf ("ip = %lx, sp = %lx\n", (long) ip, (long) sp);
248. 
249.     ret = unw_get_proc_name(&cursor, name, name_len, &ofp);
250.     printf("name %s\n",name);
251.   }
252. }
253. */
254. 
255. #ifdef __cplusplus
256. } /* extern "C" */
257. #endif
258.
```

```
1. (* Copyright (C) 1993, Digital Equipment Corporation           *)
2. (* All rights reserved.                                        *)
3. (* See the file COPYRIGHT for a full description.              *)
4. 
5. UNSAFE MODULE RTExStack EXPORTS RTException;
6. 
7. IMPORT RT0, RTOS, RTError, RTIO, RTStack, RTParams, RTEHScan;
8. IMPORT RTProcedureSRC;
9. FROM RT0 IMPORT RaiseActivation;
10. (*
11. IMPORT Cstring;
12. *)
13. 
14. 
15. VAR
16.   DEBUG := FALSE;
17. 
18. EXCEPTION
19.   OUCH; (* to keep the compiler from complaining *)
20. 
21. TYPE
22.   CharArr = REF ARRAY OF CHAR;
23. 
24. (* The unwinder needs to alloc buffers for the context and the cursor.
25.    Called from the unwinder. *)
26. PROCEDURE AllocBuf(size : INTEGER) : ADDRESS =
27.   VAR arr : CharArr;
28.   BEGIN
29.     arr := NEW(CharArr,size);
30.     RETURN ADR(arr[0]);
31.   END AllocBuf;
32. 
33. PROCEDURE Raise (VAR act: RaiseActivation) RAISES ANY =
34.   VAR
35.     here, f: RTStack.Frame;
36.     excRef : REF RaiseActivation;
37.     scan : BOOLEAN;
38.   BEGIN
39.     IF DEBUG THEN
40.       PutExcept ("RAISE", act);
41.       PrintStack (act.exception.uid);
42.     END;
43. 
44.     RTStack.CurrentFrame (here);
45.     RTStack.PreviousFrame (here, f); (* skip self *)
46.     LOOP
47.       IF (f.pc = NIL) THEN
48.         (* we're at the end of the stack (or we got lost along the way!) *)
49.         InvokeBackstop (act, raises := FALSE);
50.       END;
51. 
52.       IF f.lsda # NIL THEN
53.         (* scan the dwarf eh scopes found by the unwinder *)
54.         scan := RTEHScan.ScanEHTable(f, act.exception.uid);
55.         IF scan THEN
56.           excRef := NEW(REF RaiseActivation);
57.           excRef^ := act;
58.           ResumeRaise (excRef^)
59.         END;
60.       END;
61. 
62.       (* try the previous frame *)
63.       RTStack.PreviousFrame (f, f);
64.     END; (* loop *)
65.   END Raise;
66. 
67. PROCEDURE ResumeRaise (VAR a: RaiseActivation) RAISES ANY =
68.   VAR
69.     here, f: RTStack.Frame;
70.     scan : BOOLEAN;
71.   BEGIN
72.     IF DEBUG THEN
73.       PutExcept ("RERAISE", a);
74.       PrintStack (a.exception.uid);
75.     END;
76. 
77.     RTStack.CurrentFrame (here);
78.     RTStack.PreviousFrame (here, f); (* skip self *)
79.     LOOP
80.       IF (f.pc = NIL) THEN
81.         (* we're at the end of the stack (most likely unhandled exception) *)
82.         InvokeBackstop (a, raises := FALSE);
83.       END;
84. 
85.       IF f.lsda # NIL THEN
86.         (* scan the dwarf eh scopes found by the unwinder *)
87.         scan := RTEHScan.ScanEHTable(f, a.exception.uid);
88.         IF scan THEN
89.           (* landingpad set in scan *)
90.           f.excRef := ADR(a);
91.           RTStack.Unwind (f);
92.           RTError.MsgPC (LOOPHOLE (f.pc, INTEGER), "Unwind returned!");
93.           RAISE OUCH;
94.         END;
95.       END;
96. 
97.       (* try the previous frame *)
98.       RTStack.PreviousFrame (f, f);
99.     END;
100.   END ResumeRaise;
101. 
102. 
103. (*----------------------------------------------------------- diagnostics ---*)
104. 
105. (*
106. VAR NoName := ARRAY [0..15] OF CHAR {'s','t','a','t','i','c',' ',
107.                                      'p','r','o','c','e','d','u','r','e'};
108. *)
109. 
110. PROCEDURE DumpStack () =
111.   BEGIN
112.     PrintStack(0);
113.   END DumpStack;
114. 
115. PROCEDURE PrintStack (uid : INTEGER) =
116.   CONST CallInstructionSize = 8; (* was 4 - should be gotten from Target *)
117.   VAR
118.     here, f: RTStack.Frame;
119.     name: RTProcedureSRC.Name;
120.     scan : BOOLEAN;
121.   BEGIN
122.     RTOS.LockHeap (); (* disable thread switching... (you wish!) *)
123. 
124.     RTIO.PutText ("------------------------- STACK DUMP ---------------------------\n");
125.     RTIO.PutText ("----PC----      ----SP----      --------Procedure--------\n");
126. 
127.     RTStack.CurrentFrame (here);
128.     RTStack.PreviousFrame (here, f); (* skip self *)
129. 
130.     WHILE (f.pc # NIL) DO
131. 
132.       IF f.lsda # NIL THEN
133.         IF uid # 0 THEN
134.           (* scan the dwarf eh scopes found by the unwinder *)
135.           scan := RTEHScan.ScanEHTable(f, uid);
136.           IF scan THEN
137.             (* print the exception stuff. Fixme. Would have to modify
138.                ScanEHTable to take a parameter to dump its debug info. *)
139.           END;
140.         END;
141.       END;
142. 
143.       (* print the procedure's frame *)
144.       (* This is only approximate. The pc will be the one after the call that
145.          results in the chain leading to crash (which prints this trace).
146.          And call instructions can vary in size. *)
147.       RTIO.PutAddr (f.pc - CallInstructionSize, 10);
148.       RTIO.PutText ("  ");
149.       RTIO.PutAddr (f.sp, 10);
150. 
151.       name := RTStack.ProcName (f);
152.       RTIO.PutText ("  [");
153.       IF (name # NIL)
154.         (* not sure why they were checking for "static procedure" probably
155.            an artifact of an old architecture/os *)
156.         (* AND Cstring.memcmp (name, ADR(NoName), NUMBER(NoName)) # 0 *) THEN
157.         RTIO.PutString (name);
158.       END;
159.       RTIO.PutText ("]\n");
160. 
161.       (* try the previous frame *)
162.       RTStack.PreviousFrame (f, f);
163.     END;
164. 
165.     RTIO.PutText ("----------------------------------------------------------------\n");
166.     RTIO.Flush ();
167. 
168.     RTOS.UnlockHeap (); (* re-enable thread switching *)
169.   END PrintStack;
170. 
171. PROCEDURE PutExcept (tag: TEXT;  READONLY a: RaiseActivation) =
172.   BEGIN
173.     RTIO.PutText ("---> ");   RTIO.PutText (tag);
174.     RTIO.PutText (":  en=");  RTIO.PutAddr (a.exception);
175.     RTIO.PutText (" uid=");   RTIO.PutHex (a.exception.uid);
176.     RTIO.Flush ();
177.     RTIO.PutText (" ");       RTIO.PutString (a.exception.name);
178.     RTIO.PutText ("  arg=");  RTIO.PutAddr (a.arg);
179.     RTIO.PutText ("\n  module: ");  RTIO.PutAddr (a.module);
180.     IF (a.module # NIL) AND (a.module.file # NIL) THEN
181.       RTIO.PutText ("  ");          RTIO.PutString (a.module.file);
182.     END;
183.     RTIO.PutText ("\n  line: ");    RTIO.PutInt (a.line);
184.     RTIO.PutText ("   pc: ");       RTIO.PutAddr (a.pc);
185.     RTIO.PutText ("   info0: ");    RTIO.PutAddr (a.info0);
186.     RTIO.PutText ("   info1: ");    RTIO.PutAddr (a.info1);
187.     IF (a.un_except # NIL) THEN
188.       RTIO.PutText ("\n  unhandled: ");
189.       RTIO.PutText (" ");             RTIO.PutString (a.un_except.name);
190.       RTIO.PutText ("  arg=");        RTIO.PutAddr (a.un_arg);
191.     END;
192.     RTIO.PutText ("\n");
193.   END PutExcept;
194. 
195. BEGIN
196.   DEBUG := RTParams.IsPresent ("debugex");
197.   <*ASSERT RTStack.Has_walker*>
198. END RTExStack.
199.
```

```
readonly TARGET = "ARM64_DARWIN"

readonly DarwinArch = "arm64"

include("ARM64.common")
include("Darwin.common")

% Set to 1 to avoid pthread_create deadlock under Rosetta 2 (AMD64->ARM64 translation).
% The Rosetta-translated cm3 binary hangs when spawning multiple POSIX threads.
% Native ARM64 cm3 can safely increase this if desired.
M3_PARALLEL_BACK = 1

% The CM3 C backend generates code that uses _Float128 (a GCC/GNU extension)
% for the EXTENDED float type, and calls *q() quad-precision math functions.
% Apple clang on ARM64 Darwin lacks these; inject a compat header that maps
% them to their double equivalents via -include.
configure_c_compiler()
SYSTEM_CC = SYSTEM_CC & " -include " & INSTALL_ROOT & "/include/m3_arm64_compat.h"
```

```
#ifndef __LIBUNWIND__
#define __LIBUNWIND__

#include <__libunwind_config.h>

#include <stdint.h>
#include <stddef.h>

#ifdef __APPLE__
  #if __clang__
    #if __has_include(<Availability.h>)
      #include <Availability.h>
    #endif
  #elif __ENVIRONMENT_MAC_OS_X_VERSION_MIN_REQUIRED__ >= 1050
    #include <Availability.h>
  #endif

  #ifdef __arm__
     #define LIBUNWIND_AVAIL __attribute__((unavailable))
  #elif defined(__OSX_AVAILABLE_STARTING)
    #define LIBUNWIND_AVAIL __OSX_AVAILABLE_STARTING(__MAC_10_6, __IPHONE_5_0)
  #else
    #include <AvailabilityMacros.h>
    #ifdef AVAILABLE_MAC_OS_X_VERSION_10_6_AND_LATER
      #define LIBUNWIND_AVAIL AVAILABLE_MAC_OS_X_VERSION_10_6_AND_LATER
    #else
      #define LIBUNWIND_AVAIL __attribute__((unavailable))
    #endif
  #endif
#else
  #define LIBUNWIND_AVAIL
#endif

#if __has_include(<ptrauth.h>)
#include <ptrauth.h>
#endif

#if defined(__APPLE__) && __has_feature(ptrauth_qualifier)
#define _LIBUNWIND_PTRAUTH(__key, __address_discriminated, __discriminator)    \
  __ptrauth(__key, __address_discriminated,                                    \
            __builtin_ptrauth_string_discriminator(__discriminator))
// This work around is required to support divergence in spelling
// developed during the ptrauth upstreaming process.
#if __has_feature(ptrauth_restricted_intptr_qualifier)
#define _LIBUNWIND_PTRAUTH_RESTRICTED_INTPTR_WRAPPER(...)                      \
    __ptrauth_restricted_intptr(__VA_ARGS__)
#else
#define _LIBUNWIND_PTRAUTH_RESTRICTED_INTPTR_WRAPPER(...)                      \
    __ptrauth(__VA_ARGS__)
#endif
#define _LIBUNWIND_PTRAUTH_RESTRICTED_INTPTR(__key, __address_discriminated,   \
                                             __discriminator)                  \
  _LIBUNWIND_PTRAUTH_RESTRICTED_INTPTR_WRAPPER(                                \
      __key, __address_discriminated,                                          \
      __builtin_ptrauth_string_discriminator(__discriminator))
#else
#define _LIBUNWIND_PTRAUTH(__key, __address_discriminated, __discriminator)
#define _LIBUNWIND_PTRAUTH_RESTRICTED_INTPTR(__key, __address_discriminated,   \
                                             __discriminator)
#endif

#if defined(_WIN32) && defined(__SEH__)
  #define LIBUNWIND_CURSOR_ALIGNMENT_ATTR __attribute__((__aligned__(16)))
#else
  #define LIBUNWIND_CURSOR_ALIGNMENT_ATTR
#endif

/* error codes */
enum {
  UNW_ESUCCESS      = 0,     /* no error */
  UNW_EUNSPEC       = -6540, /* unspecified (general) error */
  UNW_ENOMEM        = -6541, /* out of memory */
  UNW_EBADREG       = -6542, /* bad register number */
  UNW_EREADONLYREG  = -6543, /* attempt to write read-only register */
  UNW_ESTOPUNWIND   = -6544, /* stop unwinding */
  UNW_EINVALIDIP    = -6545, /* invalid IP */
  UNW_EBADFRAME     = -6546, /* bad frame */
  UNW_EINVAL        = -6547, /* unsupported operation or bad value */
  UNW_EBADVERSION   = -6548, /* unwind info has unsupported version */
  UNW_ENOINFO       = -6549  /* no unwind info found */
#if defined(_LIBUNWIND_TARGET_AARCH64) && !defined(_LIBUNWIND_IS_NATIVE_ONLY)
  , UNW_ECROSSRASIGNING = -6550 /* cross unwind with return address signing */
#endif
```

```
1. (* Copyright (C) 2022 Peter McKinna. All rights reserved. *)

4. UNSAFE MODULE RTEHScan;
5. 
6. IMPORT RTStack,RTError,RTIO,RTParams,Word;
7. 
8. (*
9.   Scan the gcc except table embedded in the code stream to find
10.   an exception handling address and match the exception type uid.
11. 
12.   Inspired by and borrowed from cxa_personality.cpp in the llvm project
13.   libcxxabi. Included below is their description for the gcc_except_table
14.   which may help understanding the code. Be aware that it describes c++
15.   and uses its terminology which Modula-3 does not support. eg throw, catch
16.   It also describes the layout for SJLJ exceptions which is not supported
17.   currently.
18. 
19. 
20.     Exception Handling Table Layout:
21. 
22. +-----------------+--------+
23. | lpStartEncoding | (char) |
24. +---------+-------+--------+---------------+-----------------------+
25. | lpStart | (encoded with lpStartEncoding) | defaults to funcStart |
26. +---------+-----+--------+-----------------+---------------+-------+
27. | ttypeEncoding | (char) | Encoding of the type_info table |
28. +---------------+-+------+----+----------------------------+----------------+
29. | classInfoOffset | (ULEB128) | Offset to type_info table, defaults to null |
30. +-----------------++--------+-+----------------------------+----------------+
31. | callSiteEncoding | (char) | Encoding for Call Site Table |
32. +------------------+--+-----+-----+------------------------+--------------------------+
33. | callSiteTableLength | (ULEB128) | Call Site Table length, used to find Action table |
34. +---------------------+-----------+---------------------------------------------------+
35. #ifndef __USING_SJLJ_EXCEPTIONS__
36. +---------------------+-----------+------------------------------------------------+
37. | Beginning of Call Site Table            The current ip lies within the           |
38. | ...                                     (start, length) range of one of these    |
39. |                                         call sites. There may be action needed.  |
40. | +-------------+---------------------------------+------------------------------+ |
41. | | start       | (encoded with callSiteEncoding) | offset relative to funcStart | |
42. | | length      | (encoded with callSiteEncoding) | length of code fragment      | |
43. | | landingPad  | (encoded with callSiteEncoding) | offset relative to lpStart   | |
44. | | actionEntry | (ULEB128)                       | Action Table Index 1-based   | |
45. | |             |                                 | actionEntry == 0 -> cleanup  | |
46. | +-------------+---------------------------------+------------------------------+ |
47. | ...                                                                              |
48. +----------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
49. #else  // __USING_SJLJ_EXCEPTIONS__
50. +---------------------+-----------+------------------------------------------------+
51. | Beginning of Call Site Table            The current ip is a 1-based index into   |
52. | ...                                     this table.  Or it is -1 meaning no      |
53. |                                         action is needed.  Or it is 0 meaning    |
54. |                                         terminate.                               |
55. | +-------------+---------------------------------+------------------------------+ |
56. | | landingPad  | (ULEB128)                       | offset relative to lpStart   | |
57. | | actionEntry | (ULEB128)                       | Action Table Index 1-based   | |
58. | |             |                                 | actionEntry == 0 -> cleanup  | |
59. | +-------------+---------------------------------+------------------------------+ |
60. | ...                                                                              |
```

MODULE Main;

IMPORT IO;

EXCEPTION Boom(TEXT);

PROCEDURE Inner() RAISES {Boom} =
  BEGIN
    RAISE Boom("from Inner");
  END Inner;

PROCEDURE Middle() RAISES {Boom} =
  BEGIN
    Inner();
  END Middle;

PROCEDURE Outer() =
  BEGIN
    TRY
      Middle();
    EXCEPT
      Boom(msg) => IO.Put("Caught: " & msg & "\n");
    END;
  END Outer;

BEGIN
  Outer();
  IO.Put("Done\n");
END Main.
EOF

```
% See file COPYRIGHT-CMASS for details.
%

%-------------------------------------------------------------------
% defined by cm3, but not the other MxConfig users
if not defined("CR") CR = "\n" end
if not defined("EOL") EOL = "\n" end
if not defined("M3_PROFILING") M3_PROFILING = FALSE end
if not defined("SL") SL = "/" end
%-------------------------------------------------------------------

readonly TARGET_OS = "DARWIN"

% Darwin has no m3gdb support and -gstabs and -gstabs+ cause
% assembler errors on Mac OSX 10.10.4 Yosemite.
% Plain -g causes cm3cg to access violate attempting to generate Dwarf symbols.

m3back_debug = " "

if defined("HasCBackend")
  if HasCBackend()
    if not defined ("M3_BACKEND_MODE")
      M3_BACKEND_MODE = "3" % This should really be C.
    end
  end
end

proc FileExists(x) is
    return not stale(x, x)
end

IsX86 = equal(TARGET, "I386_DARWIN") or equal(TARGET, "AMD64_DARWIN")

proc configure_assembler() is
  if defined("SYSTEM_ASM")
    return
  end
  SYSTEM_ASM = "/usr/libexec/gcc/darwin/" & DarwinArch & "/as"

  % NOTE: Some versions of m3cg are incompatible with LLVM assembler that gcc -x assembler
  % might run. Workaround is to run as instead of gcc -x assembler.
  % See http://gcc.gnu.org/bugzilla/show_bug.cgi?id=67183
  % http://llvm.org/bugs/show_bug.cgi?id=24428

  % NOTE: Do all as versions accept -arch? It'd be nice, but I doubt it. i.e. old PowerPC
  % Does cm3cg record an architecture in the .s for as to dispatch on? Ditto.

  if not FileExists(SYSTEM_ASM)
    if IsX86
      configure_c_compiler ()
      SYSTEM_ASM = SYSTEM_CC_ASM & " -c -x assembler"
    else
      SYSTEM_ASM = "as"
    end
    %workaround and maybe faster:
    %SYSTEM_ASM = "as -arch " & DarwinArch & " -force_cpusubtype_ALL"
  end
  %SYSTEM_ASM = SYSTEM_CC_ASM & " -v -c -x assembler"
end

% TODO remove duplication (with cm3cfg.common, included later)
proc configure_c_compiler_common() is

  % Add these flags if they do not indicate errors.

  foreach a in [ "fno-reorder-blocks",
                 "funwind-tables" ]
    if not equal(try_exec("@" & SYSTEM_CC & " -" & a & " -c -x c /dev/null -o /dev/null 2>&1 | fgrep " & a & " >/dev/null"), 0)
      SYSTEM_CC = SYSTEM_CC & " -" & a
    end
  end
end

proc configure_c_compiler() is

  if defined("SYSTEM_CC")
    return
  end

  %
  % older compiler doesn't like -m32 or -arch
  %
  % gcc -c -m32 -x c /dev/null
  % cc1: error: invalid option ‘m32’
  %
  % fPIC is not usually needed here.
  % It is the default for Apple gcc and left
  % here in case user is using a self-built FSF gcc.
  %
  % g++ 1.c used to compile successfully as C++, on MacOSX 10.5.8.
  % On MacOS X 10.10.4 Yosemite it errors. -x c++ fixes it.
  % But do not use that with linking, otherwise all the object files are interpreted as C++.
  %
  % Clang assembler gives warnings for -fPIC, which appears meaningless (review for arm/arm64).
  %
  %SYSTEM_CC = "gcc -g -fPIC"
  SYSTEM_CC = "g++ -g -fPIC"
  SYSTEM_CC = SYSTEM_CC & " -Wall"
  SYSTEM_CC = SYSTEM_CC & " -Werror"
```

<sub>⏱️ 2498m 42s</sub>

### 💬 Copilot

That confirms it. `start_try`, `end_try`, `invoke_direct`, `invoke_indirect`, and `landing_pad` are **all stubs in M3C.m3**. They emit no C code whatsoever for exception table generation. The C backend relies entirely on the setjmp-based linked-list mechanism in `RTExFrame.m3`.

This means:

### Why the test program hangs

`RTExStack.Raise` loops calling `RTStack.PreviousFrame(f, f)`, checking `f.lsda # NIL` on each frame. Since M3C generates plain C calls (not C++ invocations), clang never emits `.gcc_except_table` LSDA sections. Every frame has `lsda = 0`. The loop walks off the end of the stack and keeps going forever.

### What's actually required

For `ex_stack` to work, `m3back` would need to generate something like:

```c
// For every call inside a TRY block:
try { result = SomeM3Proc(args); } catch (...) { goto handler_label; }
```

...or use `__attribute__((cleanup(...)))` on local frame structures. That causes clang to emit the LSDA `.gcc_except_table` that `RTEHScan.ScanEHTable` scans. Then `unw_resume()` can jump to the landing pad.

This requires:
1. **`m3back/M3C.m3`**: `invoke_direct`/`invoke_indirect` wrap the call in a C++ `try`/`catch(...)` that jumps to the `handler` label; `start_try`/`end_try` and `landing_pad` emit the corresponding structure
2. **Rebuild everything** since every `.o` file compiled from M3-generated C would need to be recompiled to get EH tables
3. **Full bootstrap** because the recompiled `m3core` uses the new code generator which itself needs to be rebuilt

### What we should do

The runtime plumbing we just added (RTMachine.i3, RTStackC.c, m3makefile entries) is correct and will be needed. But we should revert `M3_USE_STACK_WALKER = TRUE` in the config for now — it's not functional without the backend changes.

<sub>⏱️ 2509m 19s</sub>

### 💬 Copilot

You're exactly right. Here's the full picture:

### What `M3C.m3` (the C backend) actually generates

`start_try`, `end_try`, `invoke_direct`, `invoke_indirect`, and `landing_pad` are **all stubs** — they emit only a debug comment, no C code. Exception handling in the C backend is entirely `setjmp`-based: `RTExFrame.m3` maintains a thread-local linked list of `setjmp` buffers pushed/popped around TRY blocks. No DWARF EH tables are emitted.

This is why the test hung: `RTExStack.Raise` loops through frames checking `f.lsda # NIL`, but since `m3back` never emits anything that causes clang to generate `.gcc_except_table` sections, every frame has `lsda = 0`, and the loop walks off the end of the stack forever.

### What needs to happen for real `ex_stack` support

1. **`m3back/M3C.m3`**: `invoke_direct`/`invoke_indirect` must wrap the call in `try { } catch (...) { goto handler; }` (C++); `start_try`/`end_try` and `landing_pad` must emit corresponding structure so clang generates LSDA tables
2. **Full rebuild of everything** — all `.o` files need recompilation with EH-generating code
3. **Full bootstrap** — because `m3core` itself is compiled through this same backend

### Current state

The infrastructure is all in place and committed to source:
- `ARM64_DARWIN/RTMachine.i3` — `Has_stack_walker = TRUE`, correct `FrameInfo` layout  
- `ARM64_DARWIN/RTStackC.c` — complete libunwind implementation (macOS `libSystem` has it for free)
- `runtime/m3makefile` — `"ARM64_DARWIN" : TRUE` in `HAS_STACK_WALKER`
- `ARM64_DARWIN` config — `SYSTEM_LIBS{"UNWIND"} = []` defined; `M3_USE_STACK_WALKER` commented out until the backend catches up

Exception handling is working correctly via `ex_frame` (setjmp) as before.

```
364. PROCEDURE EmitExit1 () =
365.   VAR i: INTEGER;

367.     (* unwind as far as possible *)
368.     i := tos - 1;

370.       WITH z = stack[i] DO
371.         CASE z.kind OF
372.         | Kind.zTRYELSE =>
373.             CG.Load_intt (Exit_exception);
374.             CG.Store_int (Target.Integer.cg_type, z.info);
375.             CG.Jump (z.stopBody);
376.             EXIT;
377.         | Kind.zFINALLY, Kind.zFINALLYPROC =>
378.             CG.Load_intt (Exit_exception);
379.             CG.Store_int (Target.Integer.cg_type, z.info);
380.             CG.Jump (z.stopBody);
381.             EXIT;
382.         | Kind.zLOCK =>
383.             SetLock (FALSE, z.info, 0);
384.         | Kind.zEXIT =>
385.             CG.Jump (z.stopBody);
386.             EXIT;
387.         | Kind.zTRY =>
388.             (* ignore *)
389.         | Kind.zRAISES, Kind.zPROC =>
390.             Error.Msg ("INTERNAL ERROR: EXIT not in loop");
391.             <* ASSERT FALSE *>
392.             (* EXIT; *)
393.         END;
394.       END;
395.       DEC (i);
396.     END;
397.   END EmitExit1;

399. PROCEDURE EmitExit2 () =
400.   VAR i: INTEGER;
401.   BEGIN
402.     (* unwind as far as possible *)
403.     i := tos - 1;
404.     WHILE (i >= 0) DO
405.       WITH z = stack[i] DO
406.         CASE z.kind OF
407.         | Kind.zTRYELSE, Kind.zFINALLY =>

410.             CG.Store_int (Target.Integer.cg_type,

412.             CG.Jump (z.stop);
413.             EXIT;
414.         | Kind.zFINALLYPROC =>
415.             PopFrame (z.info);
416.             CallFinallyHandler (z.info, z.handler, z.h_level);
417.         | Kind.zLOCK =>
418.             PopFrame (z.info);
419.             SetLock (FALSE, z.info, M3RT.EF4_mutex);
420.         | Kind.zEXIT =>
```

```
45. PROCEDURE Parse (body: Stmt.T;  ): Stmt.T =
46.   TYPE TK = Token.T;
47.   VAR p := NEW (P);
48.   BEGIN
49.     StmtRep.Init (p);
50.     p.body := body;
51.     Scanner.Match (TK.tFINALLY);
52.     p.forigin := Scanner.offset;
53.     IF Target.Has_stack_walker THEN
54.       p.viaProc := FALSE;
55.       p.scope   := NIL;
56.       p.finally := Stmt.Parse ();
57.     ELSE
58.       p.handler := NEW (HandlerProc, self := p);
59.       ProcBody.Push (p.handler);
60.       p.scope := Scope.PushNew (TRUE, M3ID.NoID);
61.       p.finally := Stmt.Parse ();
62.       Scope.PopNew ();
63.       ProcBody.Pop ();
64.     END;
65.     Scanner.Match (TK.tEND);
66.     RETURN p;
67.   END Parse;
68. 
69. PROCEDURE Check (p: P;  VAR cs: Stmt.CheckState) =
70.   VAR zz: Scope.T;  oc: Stmt.Outcomes;  name: INTEGER;
71.   BEGIN
72.     Jmpbufs.CheckTry (cs.jmpbufs, p.jmpbufs);
73.     Marker.PushFinally (CG.No_label, CG.No_label, CG.No_label, NIL);
74.     Stmt.TypeCheck (p.body, cs);
75.     Marker.Pop ();
76.     TryStmt.PushHandler (NIL, 0, FALSE);
77.     IF Target.Has_stack_walker THEN
78.       Stmt.TypeCheck (p.finally, cs);
79.     ELSE
80.       oc := Stmt.GetOutcome (p.finally);
81.       IF (Stmt.Outcome.Exits IN oc) OR (Stmt.Outcome.Returns IN oc) THEN
82.         p.viaProc := FALSE;
83.         Stmt.TypeCheck (p.finally, cs);
84.       ELSE
85.         p.viaProc := TRUE;
86.         name := p.forigin MOD 10000;
87.         p.handler.name := HandlerName (name);
88.         IF (name = last_name) THEN
89.           INC (next_uid);
90.           p.handler.name := p.handler.name & "_" & Fmt.Int (next_uid);
91.         ELSE
92.           last_name := name;
93.           next_uid := 0;
94.         END;
95.         zz := Scope.Push (p.scope);
96.           p.handler.jmpbufs := Jmpbufs.CheckProcPush (cs.jmpbufs,
97.                                                       M3ID.Add (p.handler.name));
98.           Scope.TypeCheck (p.scope, cs);
99.           Stmt.TypeCheck (p.finally, cs);
100.           Jmpbufs.CheckProcPop (cs.jmpbufs, p.handler.jmpbufs);
101.         Scope.Pop (zz);
102.       END;
103.     END;
104.     TryStmt.PopHandler ();
105.   END Check;
```
