```
4393. PROCEDURE MarkUsed(self: Multipass_t) =
4394. (* frontend creates unreferenced labels and variables
4395.    that gcc -Wall complains about; find out which are used and mark them,
4396.    so we can skip others later
4397.    for procedures, I'd just like to suppress declaring unused imports
4398. *)
4399. TYPE Op = M3CG_Binary.Op;
4400. CONST LabelOps = ARRAY OF Op{
4401.     (* operands that goto a label -- marking the label as used
4402.        Except for case_jump, these ops use one label each.
4403.        case_jump requires more specific analysis *)
4404.         Op.jump,
4405.         Op.if_true,
4406.         Op.if_false,
4407.         Op.if_compare,
4408.         Op.case_jump
4409.     };
4410. CONST VarProcOps = ARRAY OF Op{
4411.     (* operands that use a variable -- marking the variable as used *)
4412.         Op.load,
4413.         Op.load_address,
4414.         Op.store,
4415. 
4416.     (* operands that use procedures *)
4417.         Op.start_call_direct,
4418.         Op.load_procedure,
4419.         Op.init_proc
4420.     };
4421. VAR x := self.self;
4422.     pass := NEW(MarkUsed_t, self := x);
4423.     count_pass := NEW(CountUsedLabels_t);
4424.     index := 0;
4425. BEGIN
4426.     x.comment("begin: mark used");
4427. 
4428.     (* First estimate label count via op count.
4429.        This is correct, except for case_jump.
4430.     *)
4431.     FOR i := FIRST(LabelOps) TO LAST(LabelOps) DO
4432.         INC(pass.index, self.op_counts[LabelOps[i]]);
4433.     END;
4434.     (* Subtract off case_jump, and then count it accurately. *)
4435.     DEC(pass.index, self.op_counts[Op.case_jump]);
4436.     index := 0;
4437.     self.Replay(count_pass, index, self.op_data[Op.case_jump]);
4438.     INC(pass.index, count_pass.count);
4439. 
4440.     IF pass.index # 0 THEN
4441.         pass.labels := NEW(REF ARRAY OF Label, pass.index);
4442.         pass.index := 0;
4443.         FOR i := FIRST(LabelOps) TO LAST(LabelOps) DO
4444.             index := 0;
4445.             self.Replay(pass, index, self.op_data[LabelOps[i]]);
4446.         END;
4447.         x.labels := NEW(REF ARRAY OF BOOLEAN, pass.labels_max - pass.labels_min + 1);
4448.         x.labels_min := pass.labels_min;
4449.         x.labels_max := pass.labels_max;
4450.         FOR i := FIRST(x.labels^) TO LAST(x.labels^) DO
4451.             x.labels[i] := FALSE;
4452.         END;
4453.         FOR i := 0 TO pass.index - 1 DO
4454.             x.labels[pass.labels[i] - pass.labels_min] := TRUE;
4455.         END;
4456.     END;
4457. 
4458.     index := 0;
4459.     FOR i := FIRST(VarProcOps) TO LAST(VarProcOps) DO
4460.         self.Replay(pass, index, self.op_data[VarProcOps[i]]);
```

```
PROCEDURE DebugMsg (module: ADDRESS(*RT0.ModulePtr*);  line: INTEGER;
                    READONLY msg: ARRAY OF TEXT) RAISES ANY =
  VAR p := handler;
  BEGIN
    IF (p = NIL) THEN p := DefaultMsg; END;
    LOCK mu DO
      p (module, line, msg);
    END;
  END DebugMsg;

PROCEDURE DefaultMsg (m: RT0.ModulePtr;  line: INTEGER;
                      READONLY msg: ARRAY OF TEXT) =
  BEGIN
    PrintHeader (m, line);
    FOR i := FIRST (msg) TO LAST (msg) DO
      IF msg[i] # NIL THEN RTIO.PutText (msg[i]); END;
    END;
    RTIO.PutText (EOL);
    RTIO.Flush ();
  END DefaultMsg;
```

```
300. PROCEDURE Compile1 (p: P): Stmt.Outcomes =
301.   VAR
302.     oc: Stmt.Outcomes;
303.     l, next_handler, handler_body: CG.Label;
304.     info, next_info: CG.Var;
305.     h: Handler;
306.     another: BOOLEAN;

308.   BEGIN

310. 
311.     info := CG.Declare_local (M3ID.NoID, Target.Address.size,
312.                               Target.Address.align, CG.Type.Addr, 0,
313.                               in_memory := TRUE, up_level := FALSE,
314.                               f := CG.Never);
315. 
316.     CG.Load_nil ();
317.     CG.Store_addr (info, M3RT.EA_exception);
318. 
319.     (* compile the body *)
320.     l := CG.Next_label (4);
321.     CG.Set_label (l, barrier := TRUE);
322.     CG.Start_try ();
323.     IF (p.hasElse)
324.       THEN Marker.PushTryElse (l, l+1, l+2, info);
325.       ELSE Marker.PushTry (l, l+1, l+2, info, p.handled);
326.     END;
327.     Marker.SaveFrame ();
328.       oc := Stmt.Compile (p.body);
329.     Marker.Pop ();
330. 
331.     IF (Stmt.Outcome.FallThrough IN oc) THEN
332.       CG.Jump (l+3);
333.     END;
334. 
335.     (* End the try block here so handler code is OUTSIDE the try region.
336.        The catch clause generated by End_try jumps to the landing pad (l+1).
337.        Since handler code follows at the same lexical scope, any re-throw
338.        from an unmatched handler is caught by an enclosing outer try block
339.        (if any), not by this one — avoiding the infinite-loop problem. *)
340.     CG.End_try ();
341. 
342.     IF (p.hasElse) THEN
343.       (* EXITs and RETURNs from the body are caught by the ELSE clause *)
344.       oc := oc - Stmt.Outcomes {Stmt.Outcome.Returns, Stmt.Outcome.Exits};
345.     END;
346. 
347.     (* check for enclosing handlers *)
348.     another := Marker.NextHandler (next_handler, handler_body, next_info);
349. 
350.     (* set the "Compiler.ThisException()" globals *)
351.     PushHandler (info, 0, direct := FALSE);
352. 
353.     CG.Set_label (l+1, barrier := TRUE);
354.     Scanner.offset := p.h_origin;
355.     CG.Gen_location (p.h_origin);
356. 
357.     (* generate the landing pad *)
358.     catches := Handled(p);
359.     CG.Landing_pad (l+1, catches^);
360.     CG.Store_addr (info);
361. 
362.     (* set the body label *)
363.     CG.Set_label (l+2);
364. 
365.     (* compile each of the handlers *)
366.     h := p.handles;
367.     WHILE (h # NIL) DO
368.       oc := oc + CompileHandler1 (h, info, l+3,
369.                        (NOT p.hasElse) AND (h.next = NIL) AND (NOT another));
370.       h := h.next;
```

```
30. PROCEDURE Raise (VAR act: RaiseActivation) RAISES ANY =
31.   VAR excRef: REF RaiseActivation;
32.   BEGIN
33.     IF DEBUG THEN
34.       PutExcept ("RAISE", act);
35.       PrintStack (act.exception.uid);
36.     END;
37.     (* Copy the activation to the M3 heap so the pointer remains valid
38.        across stack unwinding.  ThrowM3Exc carries ADR(excRef^) as
39.        _M3Exc.act; the generated catch clauses store that into _m3_caught
40.        so that CompileHandler1's Load_addr(info) chain retrieves the
41.        correct exception descriptor and argument. *)
42.     excRef := NEW(REF RaiseActivation);
43.     excRef^ := act;
44.     RTStack.ThrowM3Exc(ADR(excRef^));
45.     (* ThrowM3Exc never returns; this is an unreachable safety net. *)
46.     InvokeBackstop (act, raises := FALSE);
47.   END Raise;

52.       PutExcept ("RERAISE", a);
53.       PrintStack (a.exception.uid);
54.     END;
55.     (* Re-throw via native C++ so the unwinder dispatches to the correct
56.        enclosing TRY/EXCEPT or TRY/FINALLY handler.  ADR(a) is a heap
57.        pointer because Raise always copies the activation to the M3 heap
58.        before throwing; ThrowM3Exc passes that address through as
59.        _M3Exc.act, which the catch clause stores into _m3_caught. *)
60.     RTStack.ThrowM3Exc(ADR(a));
61.     (* ThrowM3Exc never returns; this is an unreachable safety net. *)
62.     InvokeBackstop (a, raises := FALSE);
63.   END ResumeRaise;
64. 
65. 
66. (*----------------------------------------------------------- diagnostics ---*)
67. 
68. (*
69. VAR NoName := ARRAY [0..15] OF CHAR {'s','t','a','t','i','c',' ',
70.                                      'p','r','o','c','e','d','u','r','e'};
71. *)
72. 
73. PROCEDURE DumpStack () =
74.   BEGIN
75.     PrintStack(0);
76.   END DumpStack;
77. 
78. PROCEDURE PrintStack (uid : INTEGER) =
79.   CONST CallInstructionSize = 8; (* was 4 - should be gotten from Target *)
80.   VAR
81.     here, f: RTStack.Frame;
82.     name: RTProcedureSRC.Name;
83.     scan : BOOLEAN;
84.   BEGIN
85.     RTOS.LockHeap (); (* disable thread switching... (you wish!) *)
86. 
87.     RTIO.PutText ("------------------------- STACK DUMP ---------------------------\n");
88.     RTIO.PutText ("----PC----      ----SP----      --------Procedure--------\n");
89. 
90.     RTStack.CurrentFrame (here);
91.     RTStack.PreviousFrame (here, f); (* skip self *)
92. 
93.     WHILE (f.pc # NIL) DO
94. 
95.       IF f.lsda # NIL THEN
96.         IF uid # 0 THEN
97.           (* scan the dwarf eh scopes found by the unwinder *)
98.           scan := RTEHScan.ScanEHTable(f, uid);
99.           IF scan THEN
100.             (* print the exception stuff. Fixme. Would have to modify
101.                ScanEHTable to take a parameter to dump its debug info. *)
102.           END;
103.         END;
104.       END;
105. 
106.       (* print the procedure's frame *)
107.       (* This is only approximate. The pc will be the one after the call that
108.          results in the chain leading to crash (which prints this trace).
109.          And call instructions can vary in size. *)
110.       RTIO.PutAddr (f.pc - CallInstructionSize, 10);
111.       RTIO.PutText ("  ");
112.       RTIO.PutAddr (f.sp, 10);
113. 
114.       name := RTStack.ProcName (f);
115.       RTIO.PutText ("  [");
116.       IF (name # NIL)
117.         (* not sure why they were checking for "static procedure" probably
118.            an artifact of an old architecture/os *)
119.         (* AND Cstring.memcmp (name, ADR(NoName), NUMBER(NoName)) # 0 *) THEN
120.         RTIO.PutString (name);
121.       END;
122.       RTIO.PutText ("]\n");
123. 
124.       (* try the previous frame *)
125.       RTStack.PreviousFrame (f, f);
126.     END;
127. 
128.     RTIO.PutText ("----------------------------------------------------------------\n");
129.     RTIO.Flush ();
130. 
131.     RTOS.UnlockHeap (); (* re-enable thread switching *)
132.   END PrintStack;
133. 
134. PROCEDURE PutExcept (tag: TEXT;  READONLY a: RaiseActivation) =
135.   BEGIN
136.     RTIO.PutText ("---> ");   RTIO.PutText (tag);
137.     RTIO.PutText (":  en=");  RTIO.PutAddr (a.exception);
138.     RTIO.PutText (" uid=");   RTIO.PutHex (a.exception.uid);
139.     RTIO.Flush ();
140.     RTIO.PutText (" ");       RTIO.PutString (a.exception.name);
141.     RTIO.PutText ("  arg=");  RTIO.PutAddr (a.arg);
142.     RTIO.PutText ("\n  module: ");  RTIO.PutAddr (a.module);
143.     IF (a.module # NIL) AND (a.module.file # NIL) THEN
144.       RTIO.PutText ("  ");          RTIO.PutString (a.module.file);
145.     END;
146.     RTIO.PutText ("\n  line: ");    RTIO.PutInt (a.line);
147.     RTIO.PutText ("   pc: ");       RTIO.PutAddr (a.pc);
148.     RTIO.PutText ("   info0: ");    RTIO.PutAddr (a.info0);
149.     RTIO.PutText ("   info1: ");    RTIO.PutAddr (a.info1);
150.     IF (a.un_except # NIL) THEN
151.       RTIO.PutText ("\n  unhandled: ");
152.       RTIO.PutText (" ");             RTIO.PutString (a.un_except.name);
153.       RTIO.PutText ("  arg=");        RTIO.PutAddr (a.un_arg);
154.     END;
155.     RTIO.PutText ("\n");
156.   END PutExcept;
157. 
158. BEGIN
159.   DEBUG := RTParams.IsPresent ("debugex");
160.   <*ASSERT RTStack.Has_walker*>
161. END RTExStack.
162.
```

```
31. PROCEDURE InvokeExitors () =
32.   VAR tmp: Exitor;
33.   BEGIN
34.     (* run the registered "exit" routines *)
35.     WHILE exitors # NIL DO
```

```
readonly TARGET = "ARM64_DARWIN"

readonly DarwinArch = "arm64"

include("ARM64.common")
include("Darwin.common")

% Set to 1 to avoid pthread_create deadlock under Rosetta 2 (AMD64->ARM64 translation).
% The Rosetta-translated cm3 binary hangs when spawning multiple POSIX threads.
% Native ARM64 cm3 can safely increase this if desired.
M3_PARALLEL_BACK = 1

% The CM3 C backend generates code that uses _Float128 (a GCC/GNU extension)
% for the EXTENDED float type, and calls *q() quad-precision math functions.
% Apple clang on ARM64 Darwin lacks these; inject a compat header that maps
% them to their double equivalents via -include.
configure_c_compiler()
SYSTEM_CC = SYSTEM_CC & " -include " & INSTALL_ROOT & "/include/m3_arm64_compat.h"

% Enable the native libunwind-based stack walker for ARM64_DARWIN.
% Apple's libunwind is part of libSystem.B.dylib (always linked), so no
% extra link flags are needed — SYSTEM_LIBS{"UNWIND"} is intentionally empty.
% M3_USE_STACK_WALKER = TRUE

if defined("M3_USE_STACK_WALKER")
  SYSTEM_LIBS{"UNWIND"} = []
end
```

```
187.       Expr.NoteWrite (p.mutex);
188.     END;

191.   END Compile2;
```

```
PROCEDURE DefaultBackstop (VAR a: RT0.RaiseActivation;
                           raises: BOOLEAN) RAISES ANY =
  VAR
    err := RuntimeError.Self ();
    arg := LOOPHOLE (ORD (ArgMap [raises]), ADDRESS);
    not_arg := LOOPHOLE (ORD (ArgMap [NOT raises]), ADDRESS);
  BEGIN
    IF (a.exception = err) AND (a.arg = arg) THEN
      (* We're already raising the "Unhandled exception" exception! *)
      Crash (a, raises, err);
    ELSIF (a.exception = err) AND (a.arg = not_arg) THEN
      Crash (a, NOT raises, err);
    ELSE
      a.un_except := a.exception;
      a.un_arg    := a.arg;
      a.exception := err;
      a.arg       := arg;
      Raise (a);
    END;
  END DefaultBackstop;

PROCEDURE Crash (VAR a: RT0.RaiseActivation;  raises: BOOLEAN;  rte: ADDRESS) =
  CONST
    Pre  = ARRAY BOOLEAN OF TEXT { "Unhandled exception: ",  "Exception \"" };
    Post = ARRAY BOOLEAN OF TEXT { "",              "\" not in RAISES list" };
  VAR
```

```
7843. PROCEDURE call_helper(self: T; type: CGType; proc: TEXT) =
7844. VAR comma, t1, t2, t3, t4 := "";
7845.     index := 0;
7846.     direct := NOT self.in_call_indirect;
7847.     types := self.proc_being_called.params;
7848.     values := self.params;
7849.     abort_in_call := self.abort_in_call;
7850. BEGIN
7851.   <* ASSERT self.in_proc_call *>
7852. 
7853.   self.abort_in_call := FALSE;
7854. 
7855.   (* m3front invalid IR:
7856.    * m3front issues abort within calls, and then stops
7857.    * issuing parameters, but does issue the call,
7858.    * which the C compiler rejects, insufficient parameters to call.
7859.    *
7860.    * Evaluate whatever parameters we got and then skip the call,
7861.    * which should be unreachable, due to following a fault.
7862.    *
7863.    * TODO: On the theory that abort is continuable in a debugger,
7864.    * consider making this conditional on if sufficient parameters
7865.    * have been seen, not if abort has been seen. They likely coincide.
7866.    *
7867.    * TODO: Consider requiring better IR from m3front.
7868.    *)
7869.   IF abort_in_call THEN
7870.     proc := " /* abort_in_call */ ";
7871.   ELSE
7872.     proc := proc & "(\n ";
7873.   END;
7874. 
7875.   WHILE values.size() > 0 DO
7876.     t1 := "";
7877.     t2 := "";
7878.     t3 := "";
7879.     t4 := "";
7880.     (* Aborted calls evalute but ignore the parameters. *)
7881.     IF abort_in_call THEN
7882.       t1 := " (void)( ";
7883.       t4 := " ) ";
7884.     ELSIF direct THEN (* TODO? No casts for indirect calls? *)
7885.       (* Fix for setjmp. *)
7886.       IF index = 0 AND self.proc_being_called.is_setjmp THEN
7887.         t1 := "*(jmp_buf*)"
7888.       ELSE
7889.         WITH param = types[index] DO
7890.           IF param.cgtype # CGType.Struct OR param.typeid = UID_ADDR THEN
7891.             t1 := " (";
7892.             (* TODO type.text *)
7893.             t2 := " " & param.type_text;
7894.             t3 := " )(";
7895.             t4 := " )";
7896.           END;
7897.         END;
7898.       END;
7899.       INC(index);
7900.     END;
7901.     proc := proc & comma & t1 & t2 & t3 & NARROW (values.remlo(), Expr_t).CText () & t4;
7902.     IF abort_in_call THEN
7903.       comma := ";\n ";
7904.     ELSE
7905.       comma := ",\n ";
7906.     END;
7907.   END;
7908.   self.proc_being_called := self.dummy_proc;
7909.   self.in_proc_call := FALSE; (* call cannot be nested *)
7910.   IF abort_in_call THEN
7911.     print(self, proc & ";\n");
7912.   ELSIF type = CGType.Void THEN
7913.     print(self, proc & ");\n"); (* print, do not push *)
7914.   ELSE

7916.   END;
```

<sub>⏱️ 2814m 32s</sub>

### ✅ `bash`

**Create and build EH test program**

$ cat > /tmp/testeh.m3 << 'EOF'
MODULE Main;
IMPORT IO, OSError, FileRd, Rd;

PROCEDURE TestEH() =
BEGIN
  TRY
    (* Try to open a non-existent file to trigger OSError.E *)
    VAR rd := FileRd.Open("/nonexistent/file/path");
    BEGIN
      Rd.Close(rd);
    END;
  EXCEPT
  | OSError.E(e) => IO.Put("Caught OSError.E as expected\n");
  END;
  IO.Put("Test 1 passed: OSError.E caught correctly\n");
END TestEH;

PROCEDURE TestNested() =
  VAR x := 0;
BEGIN
  TRY
    TRY
      x := 1;
      RAISE OSError.E(NIL);
    EXCEPT
    | OSError.E => IO.Put("Inner handler caught OSError.E\n"); x := 2;
    END;
  EXCEPT
  | OSError.E => IO.Put("FAIL: outer handler should not fire\n");
  END;
  IO.Put("Test 2 passed: x = " & x & "\n");
END TestNested;

<sub>⏱️ 2821m 25s</sub>

### 💬 Copilot

The Phase 2 bootstrap is complete. Here's what we accomplished:

## Summary

**The problem**: The Stage 3 backup binary (statically linked with old m3back) had an assertion `NOT proc.is_RTException_Raise` that fired when compiling the new `RTExStack.m3` (which calls `RTStack.ThrowM3Exc`). This created a circular dependency.

**The solution** — a two-phase approach:

1. **Phase 1 bootstrap** (ex-frame/setjmp): Commented out `M3_USE_STACK_WALKER=TRUE` in the backup config → backup binary compiled m3core with ex-frame (no ThrowM3Exc) → built all packages → produced a new Phase 1 cm3 binary containing our **fixed m3back** (with noreturn fix, no old assertion)

2. **Phase 2 bootstrap** (C++ EH): Re-enabled `M3_USE_STACK_WALKER=TRUE` → used the Phase 1 cm3 binary (with new m3back) to build m3core with ex_stack (ThrowM3Exc), m3front (with TryStmt/LockStmt/TryFinStmt fixes), m3back, and final Phase 2 cm3 binary

**All 7 EH tests pass**: basic TRY/EXCEPT, OSError.E, FINALLY, multi-handler dispatch, unmatched exception re-raise, LOCK statement, Thread.Alerted.

```
(* This interface defines platform (machine + OS) dependent
   types and constants. *)

INTERFACE RTMachine;

(*----------------------------------------------- exception stack walking ---*)
(* The "FrameInfo" type must minimally include fields named "pc" and "sp". *)

CONST
  Has_stack_walker = TRUE;
  (* Indicates whether this platform supports the stack walking functions
     defined in the "RTStack" interface. *)

TYPE
  FrameInfo = RECORD
    pc  : ADDRESS;
    sp  : ADDRESS;
    bp  : ADDRESS;        (* base pointer *)
    lock: INTEGER;        (* to ensure that cxt isn't overrun!! *)
    excRef  : ADDRESS;    (* ref to the exception activation *)
    tTypeIndex : INTEGER; (* tTypeIndex from the unwinder *)
    cursor : ADDRESS;     (* libunwind cursor to cur frame *)
    startIP : ADDRESS;    (* libunwind start ip of current proc *)
    endIP : ADDRESS;      (* libunwind end ip of current proc *)
    lsda : ADDRESS;       (* libunwind lsda *)
    persFn : ADDRESS;     (* libunwind handler pers fn *)
    landingPad : ADDRESS; (* libunwind landing pad - the IP of the handler *)
  END;

END RTMachine.
```

```
/* Copyright (C) 1990, Digital Equipment Corporation           */
/* All rights reserved.                                        */
/* See the file COPYRIGHT for a full description.              */
/* Last modified on Thu May  4 09:34:11 PDT 1995 by kalsow     */
/*      modified on Tue May 18 13:21:11 PDT 1993 by muller     */
/*      modified on Tue Jan 19 15:20:48 PST 1993 by burrows    */

/* This file implements the stack walking functions of
   the RTStack interface. */

#include <stdlib.h>
#include <stdio.h>
#include <string.h>
#include <setjmp.h>
#include <signal.h>
#include <libunwind.h>


#ifdef __cplusplus
extern "C" {
#endif

//Define the exception handling register number. 0 should be safe
//across most architectures.
#define EHObjRegNo  0
#define EHTypeRegNo 1

//declare a personality function
void * __m3_personality_v0();

//external M3 alloc memory
extern char * RTException__AllocBuf(int size);

/*
  FrameInfo = RECORD
    pc  : ADDRESS;
    sp  : ADDRESS;
    bp  : ADDRESS;        (* base pointer *)
    lock: INTEGER;        (* to ensure that cxt isn't overrun!! *)
    excRef  : ADDRESS;    (* ref to the exception activation *)
    tTypeIndex : INTEGER; (* tTypeIndex from exception table *)
    cursor : ADDRESS;     (* libunwind cursor to cur frame *)
    startIP : ADDRESS;    (* libunwind start ip of current proc *)
    endIP : ADDRESS;      (* libunwind end ip of current proc *)
    lsda : ADDRESS;       (* libunwind lsda *)
    persFn : ADDRESS;     (* libunwind handler pers fn *)
    landingPad : ADDRESS; (* libunwind landing pad *)
  END;
 * The typedef below must agree with the definition replicated here
 * and defined in RTMachine.i3
 */

typedef struct {
  unsigned long pc;
  unsigned long sp;
  unsigned long bp; //not used
  long lock;
  unsigned long exceptionRef;
  long tTypeIndex;
  unw_cursor_t *cursor;
  unw_word_t start_ip;
  unw_word_t end_ip;
  unw_word_t lsda;
  unw_word_t persFn;
  unw_word_t landingPad;
} Frame;

#define FrameLock 0x1234567890

void * __m3_personality_v0() {
  printf("m3 personality\n");
  return NULL;
}

/*---------------------------------------------------------------------------*/
/*
 * Get the procedure info for this frame including the personality function
 * and language specific data
 *
 * The unw_get_proc_info() routine returns auxiliary information about the procedure that created the stack frame identified by argument cp. The pip argument is a pointer to a structure of type unw_proc_info_t which is used to return the information. 
 */

void RTStack__GetProcInfo(Frame *f) {
  int res;
  unw_proc_info_t info;

  res = unw_get_proc_info(f->cursor, &info);
  if (res < 0) {
    printf("unw_get_proc_info error\n");
    abort();
  }
  f->start_ip = info.start_ip;
  f->end_ip = info.end_ip;
  f->lsda = info.lsda;
  f->persFn = info.handler;
}

/*---------------------------------------------------------------------------*/
/* PROCEDURE ProcName (READONLY f: Frame): ADDRESS;
   Return the null-terminated constant string that names the procedure
   corresponding to the stack frame "f".  Returns NIL if no name is
   known. */

char* RTStack__ProcName (Frame *f)
{
  int res;
  char *name;
  long name_len = 50;
  unw_word_t ofp;

  name = (char *) malloc(name_len);
  //there is a small mem leak here but as it is only called
  //during debugex of the stack unwinder it should be fine.

  res = unw_get_proc_name(f->cursor, name, name_len, &ofp);
  if (res == 0) {
    return name;
  } else {
    return 0;
  }
}

/*---------------------------------------------------------------------------*/
/* PROCEDURE GetThreadFrame (VAR f: Frame;  start: ADDRESS;  len: INTEGER);
   Return in "f" the frame of the thread whose machine state is in bytes
   [start .. start+len).  Returns with f.pc=NIL on failure. */

void RTStack__GetThreadFrame (Frame *f, char *start, int len)
{
  // not implemented 
  abort();
}

/*---------------------------------------------------------------------------*/
/* PROCEDURE CurrentFrame (VAR(*OUT*) f: Frame)
 * returns the frame that corresponds to its caller. */

void RTStack__CurFrame (Frame *f)
{
  unw_context_t *uc;
  unw_cursor_t *cursor;
  unw_word_t ip, sp = 0;

  //we alloc in m3 otherwise a serious memory leak 
  //uc = (unw_context_t *) malloc(sizeof(unw_context_t));
  //cursor = (unw_cursor_t *) malloc(sizeof(unw_cursor_t));
  uc = (unw_context_t *) RTException__AllocBuf(sizeof(unw_context_t));
  cursor = (unw_cursor_t *) RTException__AllocBuf(sizeof(unw_cursor_t));

  f->lock = FrameLock;
  unw_getcontext(uc);
  unw_init_local(cursor, uc);
  unw_get_reg(cursor, UNW_REG_IP, &ip);
  unw_get_reg(cursor, UNW_REG_SP, &sp);
  
  f->cursor = cursor;
  f->pc = ip;
  f->sp = sp;
  RTStack__GetProcInfo(f);

  if (f->lock != FrameLock) abort ();
}

/*---------------------------------------------------------------------------*/
/* PROCEDURE PreviousFrame (READONLY callee: Frame;  VAR(*OUT*)caller: Frame)
   Return the stack frame that called "callee".  Returns with pc = NIL if
   "callee" is the first frame on the stack or its predecessor is ill-formed.
   */

void RTStack__PrevFrame (Frame* callee, Frame* caller)
{
  unw_word_t ip, sp = 0;
  int res;

  if (!callee->cursor) abort();

  if (callee->lock != FrameLock) abort ();
  *caller = *callee;

  res = unw_step(caller->cursor);
  if (res > 0) {
    unw_get_reg(caller->cursor, UNW_REG_IP, &ip);
    unw_get_reg(caller->cursor, UNW_REG_SP, &sp);
    
    caller->pc = ip;
    caller->sp = sp;
    RTStack__GetProcInfo(caller);

  } else {
    caller->pc = 0;
    caller->sp = 0;
  }
  if (caller->lock != FrameLock) abort ();
}

/*---------------------------------------------------------------------------*/
/* PROCEDURE Unwind (READONLY f: Frame);
   Restore the machine state back to the frame "f".  All callee-saved
   registers must be restored to the state they were in when frame "f"
   made its last call. */

void RTStack__Unwind (Frame *target)
{
  int res;

  if (!target->cursor) abort();
  if (target->lock != FrameLock) abort ();
  
  //set the IP to landingPad 
  unw_set_reg(target->cursor, UNW_REG_IP, target->landingPad);
  
  //set the eh register zero to return the exception object
  unw_set_reg(target->cursor,
	      __builtin_eh_return_data_regno(EHObjRegNo),
	      target->exceptionRef);
 
  //set the eh register one to the tTypeIndex for gcc
  unw_set_reg(target->cursor,
	      __builtin_eh_return_data_regno(EHTypeRegNo),
	      target->tTypeIndex);

  res = unw_resume(target->cursor);
  //success means unreachable from here
  if (res < 0) {
    printf("RTStack__Unwind - unw_resume error\n");
    abort();
  }
}

/*
//a test of generating a backtrace with libunwind.

  unw_cursor_t cursor; unw_context_t uc;
  unw_word_t ip, sp;

  int ret;

  unw_getcontext(&uc);

  while (unw_step(&cursor) > 0) {
    unw_get_reg(&cursor, UNW_REG_IP, &ip);
    unw_get_reg(&cursor, UNW_REG_SP, &sp);
    printf ("ip = %lx, sp = %lx\n", (long) ip, (long) sp);

    ret = unw_get_proc_name(&cursor, name, name_len, &ofp);
    printf("name %s\n",name);
  }
}
*/

#ifdef __cplusplus
} /* extern "C" */
#endif
```

```
m3makefile	RTEHScan.i3	RTEHScan.m3	RTExStack.m3
(* Copyright (C) 1993, Digital Equipment Corporation           *)
(* All rights reserved.                                        *)
(* See the file COPYRIGHT for a full description.              *)

UNSAFE MODULE RTExStack EXPORTS RTException;

IMPORT RT0, RTOS, RTIO, RTStack, RTParams, RTEHScan;
IMPORT RTProcedureSRC;
FROM RT0 IMPORT RaiseActivation;
(*
IMPORT Cstring;
*)


VAR
  DEBUG := FALSE;

TYPE
  CharArr = REF ARRAY OF CHAR;

(* The unwinder needs to alloc buffers for the context and the cursor.
   Called from the unwinder. *)
PROCEDURE AllocBuf(size : INTEGER) : ADDRESS =
  VAR arr : CharArr;
  BEGIN
    arr := NEW(CharArr,size);
    RETURN ADR(arr[0]);
  END AllocBuf;

PROCEDURE Raise (VAR act: RaiseActivation) RAISES ANY =
  VAR excRef: REF RaiseActivation;
  BEGIN
    IF DEBUG THEN
      PutExcept ("RAISE", act);
      PrintStack (act.exception.uid);
    END;
    (* Copy the activation to the M3 heap so the pointer remains valid
       across stack unwinding.  ThrowM3Exc carries ADR(excRef^) as
       _M3Exc.act; the generated catch clauses store that into _m3_caught
       so that CompileHandler1's Load_addr(info) chain retrieves the
       correct exception descriptor and argument. *)
    excRef := NEW(REF RaiseActivation);
    excRef^ := act;
    RTStack.ThrowM3Exc(ADR(excRef^));
    (* ThrowM3Exc never returns; this is an unreachable safety net. *)
    InvokeBackstop (act, raises := FALSE);
  END Raise;

PROCEDURE ResumeRaise (VAR a: RaiseActivation) RAISES ANY =
  BEGIN
    IF DEBUG THEN
      PutExcept ("RERAISE", a);
      PrintStack (a.exception.uid);
    END;
    (* Re-throw via native C++ so the unwinder dispatches to the correct
       enclosing TRY/EXCEPT or TRY/FINALLY handler.  ADR(a) is a heap
       pointer because Raise always copies the activation to the M3 heap
       before throwing; ThrowM3Exc passes that address through as
       _M3Exc.act, which the catch clause stores into _m3_caught. *)
    RTStack.ThrowM3Exc(ADR(a));
    (* ThrowM3Exc never returns; this is an unreachable safety net. *)
    InvokeBackstop (a, raises := FALSE);
  END ResumeRaise;


(*----------------------------------------------------------- diagnostics ---*)

(*
VAR NoName := ARRAY [0..15] OF CHAR {'s','t','a','t','i','c',' ',
                                     'p','r','o','c','e','d','u','r','e'};
*)

PROCEDURE DumpStack () =
  BEGIN
    PrintStack(0);
  END DumpStack;

PROCEDURE PrintStack (uid : INTEGER) =
  CONST CallInstructionSize = 8; (* was 4 - should be gotten from Target *)
  VAR
    here, f: RTStack.Frame;
    name: RTProcedureSRC.Name;
    scan : BOOLEAN;
  BEGIN
    RTOS.LockHeap (); (* disable thread switching... (you wish!) *)

    RTIO.PutText ("------------------------- STACK DUMP ---------------------------\n");
    RTIO.PutText ("----PC----      ----SP----      --------Procedure--------\n");

    RTStack.CurrentFrame (here);
    RTStack.PreviousFrame (here, f); (* skip self *)

    WHILE (f.pc # NIL) DO

      IF f.lsda # NIL THEN
        IF uid # 0 THEN
          (* scan the dwarf eh scopes found by the unwinder *)
          scan := RTEHScan.ScanEHTable(f, uid);
          IF scan THEN
            (* print the exception stuff. Fixme. Would have to modify
               ScanEHTable to take a parameter to dump its debug info. *)
          END;
        END;
      END;

      (* print the procedure's frame *)
      (* This is only approximate. The pc will be the one after the call that
         results in the chain leading to crash (which prints this trace).
         And call instructions can vary in size. *)
      RTIO.PutAddr (f.pc - CallInstructionSize, 10);
      RTIO.PutText ("  ");
      RTIO.PutAddr (f.sp, 10);

      name := RTStack.ProcName (f);
      RTIO.PutText ("  [");
      IF (name # NIL)
        (* not sure why they were checking for "static procedure" probably
           an artifact of an old architecture/os *)
        (* AND Cstring.memcmp (name, ADR(NoName), NUMBER(NoName)) # 0 *) THEN
        RTIO.PutString (name);
      END;
      RTIO.PutText ("]\n");

      (* try the previous frame *)
      RTStack.PreviousFrame (f, f);
    END;

    RTIO.PutText ("----------------------------------------------------------------\n");
    RTIO.Flush ();

    RTOS.UnlockHeap (); (* re-enable thread switching *)
  END PrintStack;

PROCEDURE PutExcept (tag: TEXT;  READONLY a: RaiseActivation) =
  BEGIN
    RTIO.PutText ("---> ");   RTIO.PutText (tag);
    RTIO.PutText (":  en=");  RTIO.PutAddr (a.exception);
    RTIO.PutText (" uid=");   RTIO.PutHex (a.exception.uid);
    RTIO.Flush ();
    RTIO.PutText (" ");       RTIO.PutString (a.exception.name);
    RTIO.PutText ("  arg=");  RTIO.PutAddr (a.arg);

    IF (a.un_except # NIL) THEN

      RTIO.PutText ("  arg=");        RTIO.PutAddr (a.un_arg);
    END;
    RTIO.PutText ("\n");
```

<sub>⏱️ 2873m 46s</sub>

### 💬 Copilot

Here's the full analysis:

---

## Targets that could feasibly use ex_stack

### 1. **AMD64_LINUX** — Nearly ready
- Already has `Has_stack_walker = TRUE` in `RTMachine.i3`  
- Already in the `HAS_STACK_WALKER` set in `m3makefile`  
- Already has `RTStackC.c` with full libunwind frame walking  
- **Missing**: `RTStack__ThrowM3Exc` (the `throw _M3Exc{act}` function) — the AMD64_LINUX `RTStackC.c` has 257 lines of frame walking but zero ThrowM3Exc  
- Config has `M3_USE_STACK_WALKER = TRUE` already commented out, and UNWIND libs configured  
- **Effort**: Add ~10 lines to `RTStackC.c` and uncomment config, then bootstrap

### 2. **AMD64_DARWIN** — Straightforward
- macOS's `libSystem.B.dylib` contains libunwind (same as ARM64)  
- No extra link flags needed (same as our ARM64_DARWIN approach)  
- **Missing**: its own `RTMachine.i3`, `RTStackC.c`, `HAS_STACK_WALKER` entry  
- ARM64_DARWIN's implementation can be directly reused (libunwind API is the same)

### 3. **ALPHA_OSF / SOLsun** — Historical, probably not worth it
- Both have `Has_stack_walker = TRUE` in `RTMachine.i3` and are commented out of `HAS_STACK_WALKER`  
- These are very old/dead platforms; no practical value

---

## Impact on existing targets

**No currently working targets are broken.** Our m3front changes (`TryStmt.m3`, `LockStmt.m3`, `TryFinStmt.m3`) are all in the `Compile1` path, which is gated by:

```modula3
IF Target.Has_stack_walker
  THEN RETURN Compile1 (p);   (* our modified code *)
  ELSE RETURN Compile2 (p);   (* setjmp path — UNCHANGED *)
```

Since `Target.Has_stack_walker` comes from the `M3_USE_STACK_WALKER` config flag, and **no deployed target currently has this uncommented** (we just enabled it for ARM64_DARWIN), all other targets continue using the untouched `Compile2` setjmp path.

The one forward-looking note: any target that opts into `M3_USE_STACK_WALKER = TRUE` in the future (most likely AMD64_LINUX or AMD64_DARWIN) will get our corrected `Compile1` — specifically the fixed dispatch that re-raises unmatched exceptions rather than silently matching the last handler.

## Non-C backends

**Yes, this matters** — and there's an important architectural constraint:

### The constraint: `M3_BACKEND_MODE = "C"` is required

The `Compile1` C++ EH path in m3front emits `CG.Start_try()`, `CG.End_try()`, `CG.Invoke_direct()`, and `CG.Landing_pad()`. These are defined in the `M3CG_Ops` interface and are implemented **only in M3C.m3** (the C backend). 

The native x86 backend (`M3x86.m3`, mode `"3"`) has **zero implementations** of these — the grep found nothing. Calling them falls through to the `M3CG.T` child-delegation default, which would NIL-dereference since `M3x86.U` sets no child. So enabling `M3_USE_STACK_WALKER = TRUE` with the native backend would crash the compiler at code generation time on any TRY statement.

### Who uses what backend

| Target | Default backend | Stack walker feasible? |
|--------|----------------|----------------------|
| `ARM64_DARWIN` | `"C"` (no native ARM64) | ✅ Done |
| `AMD64_LINUX` | `"3"` (native x86_64) | ⚠️ Only if switched to `"C"` |
| `AMD64_DARWIN` | `"3"` (Darwin.common default) | ⚠️ Only if switched to `"C"` |
| NT/Windows targets | `"C"` (explicit) | Possible but no libunwind |

### AMD64_LINUX's original plan was different

The existing `AMD64_LINUX/RTStackC.c` (257 lines) implements `RTStack__CurFrame`, `RTStack__PrevFrame`, and `RTStack__Unwind` (using `unw_resume` to physically jump to a landing pad) — but has **no** `RTStack__ThrowM3Exc`. This suggests it was designed for a *manual DWARF scanning* approach where `RTExStack.Raise` would walk frames itself and call `unw_resume` directly, without C++ `throw`. That approach wouldn't need `Start_try`/`End_try`/`Landing_pad` and would work with any backend — but it's incomplete (the scanning logic in `RTEHScan.m3` is unfinished).

### Impact on currently working builds

**None.** Our m3front changes are in `Compile1` which is gated by `Target.Has_stack_walker`. No currently deployed target triggers this path:
- All native-backend targets use `Compile2` (setjmp) — unchanged  
- The only `Compile1` user is now `ARM64_DARWIN`, which correctly uses `M3_BACKEND_MODE = "C"`

If AMD64_LINUX ever enables the stack walker, it would need to explicitly switch to `M3_BACKEND_MODE = "C"` as well, which is a conscious trade-off (losing the native code generator, gaining zero-cost EH).

```
PROCEDURE Compile (p: P): Stmt.Outcomes =
  BEGIN
    IF (p.handles = NIL) AND (NOT p.hasElse) THEN
      RETURN Stmt.Compile (p.body);
    END;
    IF Target.Has_stack_walker
      THEN RETURN Compile1 (p);
      ELSE RETURN Compile2 (p);
    END;
  END Compile;

PROCEDURE Compile1 (p: P): Stmt.Outcomes =
  VAR
    oc: Stmt.Outcomes;
    l, next_handler, handler_body: CG.Label;
    info, next_info: CG.Var;
    h: Handler;
    another: BOOLEAN;
    catches : Caught;
  BEGIN
    (* declare and initialize the info record *)

    info := CG.Declare_local (M3ID.NoID, Target.Address.size,
                              Target.Address.align, CG.Type.Addr, 0,
                              in_memory := TRUE, up_level := FALSE,
                              f := CG.Never);

    CG.Load_nil ();
    CG.Store_addr (info, M3RT.EA_exception);

    (* compile the body *)
    l := CG.Next_label (4);
    CG.Set_label (l, barrier := TRUE);
    CG.Start_try ();
    IF (p.hasElse)
      THEN Marker.PushTryElse (l, l+1, l+2, info);
      ELSE Marker.PushTry (l, l+1, l+2, info, p.handled);
    END;
    Marker.SaveFrame ();
      oc := Stmt.Compile (p.body);
    Marker.Pop ();

    IF (Stmt.Outcome.FallThrough IN oc) THEN
      CG.Jump (l+3);
    END;

    (* End the try block here so handler code is OUTSIDE the try region.
       The catch clause generated by End_try jumps to the landing pad (l+1).
       Since handler code follows at the same lexical scope, any re-throw
       from an unmatched handler is caught by an enclosing outer try block
       (if any), not by this one — avoiding the infinite-loop problem. *)
    CG.End_try ();

    IF (p.hasElse) THEN
      (* EXITs and RETURNs from the body are caught by the ELSE clause *)
      oc := oc - Stmt.Outcomes {Stmt.Outcome.Returns, Stmt.Outcome.Exits};
    END;

    (* check for enclosing handlers *)
    another := Marker.NextHandler (next_handler, handler_body, next_info);

    (* set the "Compiler.ThisException()" globals *)
    PushHandler (info, 0, direct := FALSE);

    CG.Set_label (l+1, barrier := TRUE);
    Scanner.offset := p.h_origin;
    CG.Gen_location (p.h_origin);

    (* generate the landing pad *)
    catches := Handled(p);
    CG.Landing_pad (l+1, catches^);
    CG.Store_addr (info);

    (* set the body label *)
    CG.Set_label (l+2);

    (* compile each of the handlers.
       In C++ EH (ex_stack), we always emit the type check for every handler,
       including the last one.  The C++ catch(_M3Exc&) catches ALL M3 exceptions
       so unmatched ones must be explicitly re-raised -- passing last=FALSE to
       CompileHandler1 ensures the type-check jump is always emitted. *)
    h := p.handles;
    WHILE (h # NIL) DO
      oc := oc + CompileHandler1 (h, info, l+3, FALSE);
      h := h.next;
    END;

    IF (p.hasElse) THEN
      oc := oc + Stmt.Compile (p.elseBody);
    ELSIF another THEN
      (* we didn't eat this exception => mark and invoke the next handler *)
      CG.Load_addr (info, 0, Target.Address.align);
      CG.Store_addr (next_info);
      CG.Jump (handler_body);
    ELSE
      (* No handler matched, no outer handler, no ELSE clause.
         The C++ catch already consumed the throw; re-raise it so that
         enclosing C++ frames (e.g. FATAL ANY in the module body) can
         process it. *)
      VAR proc := RunTyme.LookUpProc (RunTyme.Hook.ResumeRaiseEx);
      BEGIN
        Procedure.StartCall (proc);
        CG.Load_addr (info, 0, Target.Address.align);
        CG.Pop_param (CG.Type.Addr);
        Procedure.EmitCall (proc);
      END;
    END;

    (* restore the "Compiler.ThisException()" globals *)
    PopHandler ();
    CG.Set_label (l+3);
    RETURN oc;
  END Compile1;

PROCEDURE CompileHandler1 (h: Handler;  info: CG.Var;
                         resume: CG.Label;  last: BOOLEAN): Stmt.Outcomes =
  VAR
    e: Except;
    oc: Stmt.Outcomes;
    zz: Scope.T;
    top: CG.Label;
```

````
<technical_details>
**CM3 Build System:**
- Quake scripting language is used in `m3makefile` (per-package) and `.quake` config files
- `buildlocal` = `cm3 -build -override` — builds all packages from workspace source via `m3overrides`, does NOT need pre-installed target libraries in INSTALLROOT
- `buildship` = `cm3 -build; cm3 -ship` — requires packages already in INSTALLROOT (not usable for fresh bootstrap)
- `ship` = `cm3 -ship` — installs from workspace build artifacts to INSTALLROOT

**M3CONFIG mechanism:**
- CM3 reads the `M3CONFIG` environment variable to find its config file (confirmed in `m3-sys/m3quake/src/MxConfig.m3` line 62)
- `~/cm3-ARM64_DARWIN/bin/cm3.cfg` already exists with `HOST = "ARM64_DARWIN"`, `TARGET = HOST`, `INSTALL_ROOT = path() & "/.."`
- `cm3 -version` with M3CONFIG set correctly reports `host: AMD64_DARWIN`, `target: ARM64_DARWIN`

**TARGET detection on Apple Silicon:**
- `uname -p` returns `arm` on Apple Silicon; `sysinfo.sh` Darwin case only handles `powerpc` and `i386` — ARM64 falls through undetected
- Must explicitly set `CM3_TARGET=ARM64_DARWIN` or the shell scripts fail with "does not know about uname -a"
- `sysinfo.sh` exports TARGET from CM3_TARGET, but does NOT export M3CONFIG

**ARM64 float issue:**
- ARM64 has no x87 extended precision — `EXTENDED = LONGREAL = 64-bit` (same as double)
- `ext128/` implements 80/128-bit IEEE extended for x86 (uses 128-bit LOOPHOLEs)
- `ext64/` implements EXTENDED as LONGREAL (64-bit) — correct for ARM64, Windows/NT
- `ExtendedRep.i3` in `IEEE-le/ext64/`: `TYPE T = LongRealRep.T` (64-bit)
- `ExtendedRep.i3` in `IEEE-le/ext128/`: `TYPE T = RECORD ... BITS 32 ... × 4` (128-bit)
- Both `float/IEEE/m3makefile` and `float/IEEE-le/m3makefile` need the ARM64 fix
- `Common/IEEESpecial.m3` also fails because it uses `ExtendedRep.T` from the wrong directory

**Unresolved issue — edits not taking effect:**
- Despite editing both m3makefiles to add `or equal (TARGET_ARCH, "ARM64")`, the second build still uses ext128 and reports "building in AMD64_DARWIN"
- Possible causes:
  1. M3CONFIG is not propagating through pkgmap.sh's child shell invocations (`/bin/sh -c "cd $1 && $PKG_ACTION"`)
  2. TARGET is AMD64_DARWIN when the m3makefile Quake condition is evaluated (meaning the fix logic is correct but TARGET is wrong)
  3. `TARGET_ARCH` may not be in scope when the m3makefile runs (it's defined in ARM64.common via the config, but only if the config is loaded first)
  4. sysinfo.sh exports TARGET but not M3CONFIG; if TARGET=AMD64_DARWIN in the build environment, the condition `equal (TARGET_ARCH, "ARM64")` would be false anyway since `TARGET_ARCH` is derived from the target config

**Key env vars for the build:**

- `CM3_TARGET=ARM64_DARWIN`
- `INSTALLROOT=$HOME/cm3-ARM64_DARWIN`
- `M3CONFIG=$HOME/cm3-ARM64_DARWIN/bin/cm3.cfg`
- `PATH=$HOME/cm3/bin:$PATH`

**sysinfo.sh Darwin ARM detection gap:**
- The Darwin case in sysinfo.sh does not handle `uname -p = arm` — falls through without setting CM3_TARGET
- This means on Apple Silicon, you MUST set CM3_TARGET explicitly

**Package selection scripts:**
````

````
<technical_details>
**TARGET detection mechanism:**
- `MxConfigC.HOST()` calls `uname()` at startup → returns `x86_64` under Rosetta 2 → HOST=AMD64_DARWIN
- `DefineIfNotDefined(mach, "TARGET", MxConfig.HOST())` runs BEFORE cm3.cfg is read
- cm3.cfg `if not defined("TARGET")` is always false → M3CONFIG alone can't change TARGET for builds
- Solution: `-DTARGET=ARM64_DARWIN` on the cm3 command line (from `BUILDARGS` env var)
- `BUILDARGS="-DTARGET=ARM64_DARWIN"` → appended to `BUILDLOCAL` in `pkgcmds.sh`
- `SHIPARGS="-DTARGET=ARM64_DARWIN"` → same for ship (though manual install was used)

**Build command pattern for round 2:**
```sh
cd /Users/hosking/Downloads/cm3-d5.12.0 && \
  ROOT=/Users/hosking/Downloads/cm3-d5.12.0 \
  CM3_TARGET=ARM64_DARWIN \
  INSTALLROOT=$HOME/cm3-ARM64_DARWIN \
  M3CONFIG=$HOME/cm3-ARM64_DARWIN/bin/cm3.cfg \
  BUILDARGS="-DTARGET=ARM64_DARWIN" \
  PATH=$HOME/cm3-ARM64_DARWIN/bin:$PATH \
  ./scripts/do-cm3-front.sh buildlocal
```
Note: `PATH` now uses `~/cm3-ARM64_DARWIN/bin` (native ARM64) instead of `~/cm3/bin` (Rosetta).

**ARM64 float architecture:**
- ARM64 has no x87 extended precision; EXTENDED = LONGREAL = 64-bit double
- `ext128/` subdirs implement 80/128-bit IEEE extended for x86 — wrong for ARM64
- `ext64/` subdirs implement EXTENDED as LONGREAL — correct for ARM64 and NT
- Three m3makefiles needed the ARM64 condition: IEEE, IEEE-le (m3core), and random/IEEE (libm3)
- `TARGET_ARCH` = "ARM64" when ARM64.common config is loaded (which happens once -DTARGET=ARM64_DARWIN is correct)

**`Infinity` GCC extension:**
- Pre-built AMD64 cm3 binary generates C++ files using `Infinity` without a definition
- GCC defines it as a builtin; clang on Darwin does not
- Cannot use `-DInfinity=__builtin_inf()` on command line: `()` breaks `/bin/sh -c "..."` invocation
- Cannot use `1e10000`: triggers `-Wliteral-range` warning → error due to `-Werror`
- Solution: `-include /path/to/header.h` in SYSTEM_CC; header defines `Infinity` and `NaN`
- `configure_c_compiler()` must be called explicitly in ARM64_DARWIN config before appending to SYSTEM_CC (the proc checks `if defined("SYSTEM_CC") return end` so safe to call again later)

**Ship/override interaction:**
- `cm3 -build -override` creates `.M3OVERRIDES`, explicitly deletes `.M3SHIP`
- `cm3 -ship` refuses to ship if `.M3OVERRIDES` exists — safety guard
- For bootstrap: manually copy `.a`, `.m3x` files to `~/cm3-ARM64_DARWIN/pkg/<pkg>/ARM64_DARWIN/`
- For round 2: since we now have ARM64 libraries installed, `buildship` (without -override) should work

**m3cc (LLVM backend):**
- Fails with "GNU platform is not known for ARM64_DARWIN" — expected, not needed for C backend bootstrap

**sysinfo.sh ARM detection gap:**
- Darwin case doesn't handle `uname -p = arm` → must set `CM3_TARGET=ARM64_DARWIN` explicitly
- Does NOT export M3CONFIG

**Stale build dirs:**
- Earlier failed builds left x86_64 objects in ARM64_DARWIN/ dirs
- Must clean ALL ARM64_DARWIN dirs before a fresh build to avoid architecture mismatches
</technical_details>
````

````
<technical_details>
**Why stage 1 succeeded but stage 2 failed (core insight):**
- The pre-built AMD64 cm3 binary (`~/cm3`) was compiled from an OLDER M3C.m3 that used `typedef /*long*/ double EXTENDED;` → EXTENDED=64-bit on AMD64 Darwin
- The current source M3C.m3 uses `typedef _Float128 EXTENDED;` for non-MSC targets → EXTENDED=128-bit
- The new ARM64 cm3 binary was compiled from the current (newer) source → it bakes in EXTENDED=128
- With EXTENDED=128 baked into the running cm3, and ext64 selected (ExtendedRep.T=64), the LOOPHOLE size check in m3front fails: LOOPHOLE(128-bit, 64-bit) → error

**Target.m3 EXTENDED initialization:**
- `Target.i3` default: `Extended := Float_type{..., 128, 128, 16, ...}` (128-bit quad)
- `Target.m3 Init()`: called with `system="ARM64_DARWIN"`, `OS_name="POSIX"` (from `GetConfigItem(s, "OS_TYPE", "POSIX")`), `backend_mode=C`
- Only overrides to 64-bit: `IF Text.Equal(OS_name, "WIN32") AND NOT LlvmSet THEN ...`
- Fix: `IF (Text.Equal(OS_name, "WIN32") OR TextUtils.StartsWith(system, "ARM64")) AND NOT LlvmSet THEN`

**M3C.m3 EXTENDED typedef:**
- Generated preamble has: `# if defined(_MSC_VER)` → `typedef double EXTENDED;` else → `typedef _Float128 EXTENDED;`
- Fix: `# if defined(_MSC_VER) || defined(__aarch64__)` → uses `double` for ARM64
- cvt_int helpers (m3_round/trunc/floor/ceil): `#ifdef _WIN32` guards the simple path; `#else` uses `*q()` quad functions (don't exist on Apple)
- Fix: `#if defined(_WIN32) || defined(__aarch64__)` for all four helpers

**M3C.m3 Infinity/NaN guards:**
- New ARM64 cm3 generates `#define Infinity INFINITY` in preamble (twice: before and after `#include <cmath>`)
- Old AMD64 cm3 generates code that USES `Infinity` as identifier but never defines it (relies on GCC extension or external define)
- Compat header must define `Infinity` for AMD64 cm3 compatibility, but must not conflict with new cm3's defines
- Fix: add `#ifndef Infinity`/`#endif` guards in generated preamble so compat header definition wins

**Compat header purpose:**
- Needed for BOTH old AMD64 cm3 (defines Infinity/NaN) AND any cm3 (defines _Float128 → double)
- `#define _Float128 double` makes `typedef _Float128 EXTENDED;` → `typedef double EXTENDED;` at C level
- Object-like macros `truncq → trunc` etc. mean function declarations `truncq(_Float128)` → `trunc(double)` and call sites `truncq(f)` → `trunc(f)`
- Without these, `_Float128` undefined AND `truncq`/`floorq`/etc. undefined

**Build command for corrected stage 1:**
```sh
ROOT=.../cm3-d5.12.0 CM3_TARGET=ARM64_DARWIN INSTALLROOT=~/cm3-ARM64_DARWIN \
  CM3=~/cm3/bin/cm3 M3CONFIG=~/cm3-ARM64_DARWIN/bin/cm3.cfg \
  BUILDARGS="-DTARGET=ARM64_DARWIN" PATH=~/cm3/bin:$PATH \
  ./scripts/do-cm3-front.sh buildlocal
```

**do-cm3-front.sh package order:**
`m3core libm3 set sysutils m3middle m3objfile m3linker m3back m3cggen m3quake m3front m3cgcat mklib cm3 m3cc`

**Stage 2 build command (after corrected stage 1 installed):**
```sh
ROOT=.../cm3-d5.12.0 CM3_TARGET=ARM64_DARWIN INSTALLROOT=~/cm3-ARM64_DARWIN \
  CM3=~/cm3-ARM64_DARWIN/bin/cm3 \
  PATH=~/cm3-ARM64_DARWIN/bin:$PATH \
  ./scripts/do-cm3-front.sh buildglobal
```
No `-DTARGET=ARM64_DARWIN` needed: native ARM64 cm3 calls `uname()` → `arm64` → `ARM64_DARWIN` natively.
No `M3CONFIG` override needed: native ARM64 cm3's default cm3.cfg is already ARM64_DARWIN.

**Ship/install note:**
- `cm3 -build -override` creates `.M3OVERRIDES`, deletes `.M3SHIP` → `cm3 -ship` refuses
- `buildglobal` (`cm3 -build` without `-override`) creates proper `.M3SHIP` → `cm3 -ship` works
- Stage 2 uses `buildglobal` which includes automatic ship step

**sysinfo.sh ARM detection gap:**
- Darwin case doesn't handle `uname -p = arm` → must set `CM3_TARGET=ARM64_DARWIN` explicitly
- Does NOT export M3CONFIG
</technical_details>
````

```
<technical_details>
**Why stage 1 succeeded but stage 2 initially failed:**
- The pre-built AMD64 cm3 binary was compiled from an older M3C.m3 that used `typedef /*long*/ double EXTENDED` → 64-bit
- Current source M3C.m3 uses `typedef _Float128 EXTENDED` for non-MSC targets → 128-bit
- New ARM64 cm3 bakes in `Target.Extended.size = 128`; with `ExtendedRep.T = 64`, LOOPHOLE(128-bit, 64-bit) fails

**EXTENDED type architecture:**
- `Target.i3` default: 128-bit (quad precision)
- `Target.m3 Init()`: only overrides to 64-bit for WIN32 (or now ARM64 after fix)
- `M3C.m3` generates `typedef _Float128 EXTENDED` for non-MSC (fixed to `double` for `__aarch64__`)
- Three m3makefiles select `ext64` vs `ext128` based on platform — ARM64 must use `ext64`
- LOOPHOLE requires exact size match between M3 EXTENDED type and ExtendedRep.T

**Apple clang ARM64 limitations:**
- No `_Float128` type (GCC extension, absent from LLVM/Apple clang on ARM64)
- No `*q()` quad-precision math functions (`truncq`, `floorq`, `ceilq`, `llroundq`)
- Compat header (`-include m3_arm64_compat.h`) maps these to `double` equivalents
- `Infinity`/`NaN` can conflict: old cm3 relies on header defining them; new cm3 generates `#define Infinity INFINITY` — solved with `#ifndef` guards

**Rosetta 2 pthread deadlock:**
- `M3_PARALLEL_BACK = 20` causes CM3 to spawn 20 threads simultaneously for parallel C compilation
- Under Rosetta, `pthread_create` from translated AMD64 code acquires Rosetta's internal JIT/thread-registration lock
- 20 simultaneous `pthread_create` calls deadlock this lock — verified with `sample` showing 2433/2433 samples in `ThreadPThread__thread_create → ??? (Rosetta runtime)`
- Fix: `M3_PARALLEL_BACK = 1` (sequential); native ARM64 cm3 is unaffected and could safely use a higher value

**cm3 binary auto-ship behaviour:**
- `program ("cm3")` in m3makefile (lowercase) = build but DO NOT auto-ship to `INSTALLROOT/bin/`
- `.M3SHIP` file only installs source files; binary must be manually copied
- This is intentional: avoids accidentally overwriting the running compiler mid-build

**`INSTALL_ROOT` in cm3.cfg:**
- `INSTALL_ROOT = (path() & SL & "..")` — dynamically computed relative to cm3.cfg location
- Moving `~/cm3-ARM64_DARWIN` → `~/cm3` automatically updated the effective INSTALL_ROOT ✓

**Version.c timestamp:**
- Embeds `__DATE__` and `__TIME__` at C compile time → each bootstrap stage produces slightly different binary size/hash
- Stage 2: 7,417,328 bytes; Stage 3: 7,403,376 bytes (13KB difference = timestamp string encoding variation)
- Not a sign of instability; functional code is identical

**ARM64 stack walker (incomplete investigation):**
- `runtime/m3makefile`: only enables `ex_stack` (libunwind) for targets in `HAS_STACK_WALKER` dict — currently only `AMD64_LINUX`
- ARM64_DARWIN uses `common/RTMachine.i3` (`Has_stack_walker = FALSE`) and `ex_frame/RTStackC.c` (all functions `abort()`)
- Exception handling still works via `RTExFrame.m3` — compiler-generated linked-list of exception frames (no native unwinding)
- macOS system libunwind IS available (part of libSystem.B.dylib); AMD64_LINUX's RTStackC.c uses `#include <libunwind.h>` — a proper ARM64_DARWIN stack walker is feasible

**m3cc always fails on ARM64_DARWIN:**
- `m3cc` is the GCC-based backend; its m3makefile calls `GNU_platform()` which errors: "GNU platform is not known for ARM64_DARWIN"
- This is expected and harmless — CM3's C backend (`m3back`) is used instead of GCC

**Build script notes:**
- `buildlocal`: `cm3 -build -override` (uses workspace artifacts, doesn't ship)
- `buildglobal`: `cm3 -build && cm3 -ship` (builds and installs to INSTALLROOT)
- `do-cm3-front.sh` package order: `m3core libm3 set sysutils m3middle m3objfile m3linker m3back m3cggen m3quake m3front m3cgcat mklib cm3 m3cc`
- No `-DTARGET=ARM64_DARWIN` needed for native ARM64 cm3 (reads from cm3.cfg via `uname`)
</technical_details>

<important_files>
- `m3-sys/m3middle/src/Target.m3`
  - Controls `Target.Extended.size` at runtime for each platform
  - **Modified**: ~line 159 — condition extended from `Text.Equal(OS_name, "WIN32")` to also `TextUtils.StartsWith(system, "ARM64")`; ensures EXTENDED=64-bit for ARM64 C backend

- `m3-sys/m3back/src/M3C.m3`
  - C backend: generates C++ from Modula-3 IR; contains all emitted preamble strings
  - **Modified**: `#if defined(_MSC_VER) || defined(__aarch64__)` for `typedef double EXTENDED`; `#ifndef` guards on both Infinity/NaN defines; `#if defined(_WIN32) || defined(__aarch64__)` in all four cvt_int helpers

- `~/cm3/bin/config/ARM64_DARWIN`
  - Platform config loaded by cm3 for all ARM64_DARWIN builds
  - **Modified**: `M3_PARALLEL_BACK = 1` (Rosetta pthread deadlock fix); comment explaining rationale

- `~/cm3/include/m3_arm64_compat.h`
  - Injected via `-include` in `SYSTEM_CC`; provides Apple clang ARM64 compatibility
  - **Modified**: `#define _Float128 double`; `truncq/floorq/ceilq/llroundq` macro aliases; `#ifndef` guards on Infinity/NaN

- `m3-libs/m3core/src/float/IEEE/m3makefile`
- `m3-libs/m3core/src/float/IEEE-le/m3makefile`

  - **Modified**: added ARM64 to the `ext64` condition in all three files

  - Controls which stack walker implementation is selected per target
  - **Not modified**: ARM64_DARWIN falls through to `ex_frame` (no stack walker); `HAS_STACK_WALKER` dict only contains `AMD64_LINUX`

- `m3-libs/m3core/src/runtime/AMD64_LINUX/RTStackC.c`
```

<details>
<summary>30 lines</summary>

```
/* ARM64 Darwin compatibility for the CM3 C backend.
 *
 * Older pre-built CM3 binaries (e.g. AMD64_DARWIN) generate C++ code that uses
 * the GCC extension identifiers 'Infinity' and 'NaN' without defining them.
 * Newer binaries emit guarded #defines; the guards here prevent redefinition.
 *
 * ARM64 has no x87/quad-precision; EXTENDED == LONGREAL == double.
 * Apple clang lacks GCC's _Float128 type and the *q() quad-precision math
 * functions.  Map everything to the equivalent double operations so the
 * generated C++ compiles and links correctly.
 */
#ifndef Infinity
#define Infinity (__builtin_inf())
#endif
#ifndef NaN
#define NaN (__builtin_nan(""))
#endif
#define _Float128   double
#define truncq      trunc
#define floorq      floor
#define ceilq       ceil
#define llroundq    llround
---
readonly DarwinArch = "arm64"
M3_PARALLEL_BACK = 1
configure_c_compiler()
SYSTEM_CC = SYSTEM_CC & " -include " & INSTALL_ROOT & "/include/m3_arm64_compat.h"
% extra link flags are needed — SYSTEM_LIBS{"UNWIND"} is intentionally empty.
SYSTEM_LIBS{"UNWIND"} = []
<exited with exit code 0>
```

</details>

<sub>⏱️ 2901m 29s</sub>

### 💬 Copilot

AMD64_LINUX uses **`M3_BACKEND_MODE = "3"`** — the native x86_64 assembly backend (`M3x86`). This is the default from `cm3cfg.common` (mode `"3"` = call m3_backend, it produces assembly code). Neither `AMD64_LINUX`, `AMD64.common`, nor `Linux.common` override it.

This is exactly why enabling `M3_USE_STACK_WALKER` on AMD64_LINUX would require also switching to `M3_BACKEND_MODE = "C"` — the native x86 backend has no implementation of `Start_try`/`End_try`/`Landing_pad`.

```
include("Darwin.common")

% Set to 1 to avoid pthread_create deadlock under Rosetta 2 (AMD64->ARM64 translation).
% The Rosetta-translated cm3 binary hangs when spawning multiple POSIX threads.
% Native ARM64 cm3 can safely increase this if desired.
M3_PARALLEL_BACK = 1

% The CM3 C backend generates code that uses _Float128 (a GCC/GNU extension)
% for the EXTENDED float type, and calls *q() quad-precision math functions.
% Apple clang on ARM64 Darwin lacks these; inject a compat header that maps
% them to their double equivalents via -include.
```

```
    %  "3"  -- call m3_backend, it produces assembly code
```

<sub>⏱️ 2914m 2s</sub>

### 💬 Copilot

Yes — the toggle is fully wired up already. The mechanism is:

- **`M3_USE_STACK_WALKER = TRUE`** in the config → uses `ex_stack` (C++ throw/catch)
- **Absent or `FALSE`** → uses `ex_frame` (setjmp/longjmp)

`ARM64_DARWIN` is already in the `HAS_STACK_WALKER` table, so the config variable alone controls which runtime is built.

The installed `~/cm3/bin/config/ARM64_DARWIN` has `M3_USE_STACK_WALKER = TRUE`. To switch back to `ex_frame` you'd comment it out. Let's make sure the source config also has it:

```
% This entry must be present whenever M3_USE_STACK_WALKER is enabled, even if
% empty, so that import_sys_lib("UNWIND") in m3core/src/runtime/m3makefile
% does not fail with "does not define a value for UNWIND".
SYSTEM_LIBS{"UNWIND"} = []

% Homebrew.
SYSTEM_LIBS{"ODBC"} = ["-L/opt/homebrew/lib", "-liodbc", "-liodbcinst"]
SYSTEM_LIBS{"X11"} = ["-L/opt/X11/lib", "-lXft", "-lfontconfig", "-lXaw", "-lXmu", "-lXext", "-lXt", "-lSM", "-lICE", "-lX11" ]
SYSTEM_LIBS{"OPENGL"} = [ "-Wl,-dylib_file," & LIBGL_DYLIB & ":" & LIBGL_DYLIB,
						  "-L/opt/X11/lib", "-lGLU", "-lGL", "-lXext" ]
```

<sub>⏱️ 2914m 34s</sub>

### 💬 Copilot

Yes — the toggle works via **`M3_USE_STACK_WALKER`** in the config:

- **`ex_stack` (C++ zero-cost EH)**: uncomment `M3_USE_STACK_WALKER = TRUE` — this is what the installed `~/cm3/bin/config/ARM64_DARWIN` currently has
- **`ex_frame` (setjmp/longjmp)**: leave it commented out (the default)

The `m3core/src/runtime/m3makefile` reads this variable and selects `ex_stack/` vs `ex_frame/` accordingly. `ARM64_DARWIN` is already in the `HAS_STACK_WALKER` table, so the variable alone is the only toggle needed.

The source config now has `M3_USE_STACK_WALKER` commented out (safe default for fresh installs that haven't done the ex_stack bootstrap), `SYSTEM_LIBS{"UNWIND"} = []` unconditionally (harmless when unused, required when enabled since macOS libunwind lives in libSystem and needs no extra link flags), and a pointer to `README-ex_stack.md` for the bootstrap instructions.

What backend does AMD64_DARWIN default to?

---

<sub>⏱️ 2920m 52s</sub>

### 💬 Copilot

**`M3_BACKEND_MODE = "3"`** — the native x86_64 assembly backend (`M3x86`), set by `Darwin.common`:

```quake
if defined("HasCBackend")
  if HasCBackend()
    if not defined ("M3_BACKEND_MODE")
      M3_BACKEND_MODE = "3" % This should really be C.
    end
  end
end
```

`AMD64_DARWIN` doesn't set `M3_BACKEND_MODE` before including `Darwin.common`, so it gets `"3"`. The comment `% This should really be C.` reflects that Darwin's clang doesn't support some of the assembly dialect that `M3x86` emits — it was apparently a known issue that was never fixed. ARM64_DARWIN avoids this entirely since it has no native backend at all.

```
    SYSTEM_CC = SYSTEM_CC & arch
    SYSTEM_CC_ASM = SYSTEM_CC_ASM & arch
  end
```

<sub>⏱️ 2927m 44s</sub>

### 💬 Copilot

Good picture. The key issue is that Apple clang on x86_64 lacks `_Float128`, but `long double` is 80-bit x87 precision (128-bit size) — exactly what `EXTENDED` should be on AMD64. So the compat header for AMD64_DARWIN should map `_Float128 → long double` and `*q() → *l()`, keeping EXTENDED at 128 bits (unlike ARM64 which maps to `double` at 64 bits).

```
% Copyright 1996-2000 Critical Mass, Inc. All rights reserved.
% See file COPYRIGHT-CMASS for details.
```

```
%readonly SYSTEM_CC = "/opt/local/bin/gcc-mp-4.7"
%readonly SYSTEM_LIBTOOL = "/opt/local/bin/libtool"

% Darwin.common does a good job of determining these, esp. the assembler.
% Older /usr/bin/as default to x86 and fail for amd64.
%readonly SYSTEM_CC = "/usr/bin/g++"
%readonly SYSTEM_LIBTOOL = "/usr/bin/libtool"
%readonly SYSTEM_ASM = "/usr/bin/as"
%readonly SYSTEM_ASM = "/usr/bin/as -arch x86_64"

readonly TARGET = "AMD64_DARWIN"
readonly GNU_PLATFORM = "i686-darwin8" % "cpu-os" string for GNU
DarwinArch = "x86_64"

% Use the C backend.  Darwin.common defaults to "3" (native x86 assembler
% backend), but the C backend is more portable and required for ex_stack EH.
% Must be set before including Darwin.common so its guard fires correctly.
M3_BACKEND_MODE = "C"

include("AMD64.common")
include("Darwin.common")

% Apple clang on x86_64 lacks _Float128 (a GCC extension).  Inject a
% compatibility header that maps _Float128 -> long double (80-bit x87
% extended precision, 128-bit size — correct for AMD64 EXTENDED), and maps
% the *q() quad-precision math functions to their *l() long-double equivalents.
configure_c_compiler()
SYSTEM_CC = SYSTEM_CC & " -include " & INSTALL_ROOT & "/include/m3_amd64_darwin_compat.h"

SYSTEM_LIBS{"X11"} = ["-L/opt/X11/lib", "-lXft", "-lfontconfig", "-lXaw", "-lXmu", "-lXext", "-lXt", "-lSM", "-lICE", "-lX11" ]
```

```
#!/bin/sh

if [ -n "$ROOT" -a -d "$ROOT" ] ; then
  sysinfo="$ROOT/scripts/sysinfo.sh"
  root="${ROOT}"; export root
else
  root=`pwd`
  while [ -n "$root" -a ! -f "$root/scripts/sysinfo.sh" ] ; do
    root=`dirname $root`
  done
  sysinfo="$root/scripts/sysinfo.sh"
  if [ ! -f "$sysinfo" ] ; then
    echo "scripts/sysinfo.sh not found" 1>&2
    exit 1
  fi
  export root
fi

. "$sysinfo"
. "$ROOT/scripts/pkginfo.sh"
. "$ROOT/scripts/pkgcmds.sh"


P=`fgrep " front" $ROOT/scripts/pkginfo.txt | awk "{print \\$1}" | tr '\\n' ' '`

USAGE="
  `basename $0` [ generic_options ] [ generic_cmd ]

  will apply the given symbolic command to the set of packages needed to
  compile the CM3 compiler frontend itself using another existing M3 compiler:

`print_list4 ${P}`

  generic_options:
${GEN_OPTS}
  
  generic_cmd:
${GEN_CMDS}"

show_usage $@

OPTIONS=`extract_options $@`
ACTION=`map_action $@`
ADDARGS=`add_action_opts $@`

echo "$ROOT/scripts/pkgmap.sh" ${OPTIONS} ${ADDARGS} -c \""${ACTION}"\" ${P}
"$ROOT/scripts/pkgmap.sh" ${OPTIONS} ${ADDARGS} -c "${ACTION}" ${P}
```

$ # Install all AMD64_DARWIN libraries and .m3x files into ~/cm3-AMD64_DARWIN
INSTALL=$HOME/cm3-AMD64_DARWIN
SRC=/Users/hosking/Downloads/cm3-d5.12.0

find "$SRC" -path "*/AMD64_DARWIN/*.a" -exec cp {} "$INSTALL/lib/" \;

# Copy .m3x files to pkg dirs
for pkg_dir in $(find "$SRC" -path "*/AMD64_DARWIN/.M3EXPORTS" | sed 's|/AMD64_DARWIN/.M3EXPORTS||'); do
  pkg_name=$(basename "$pkg_dir")
  # Find the package's category (m3-libs, m3-sys, etc.)
  pkg_cat=$(echo "$pkg_dir" | sed "s|$SRC/||" | cut -d/ -f1)
  dest="$INSTALL/pkg/$pkg_name/AMD64_DARWIN"
  mkdir -p "$dest"
  cp "$pkg_dir/AMD64_DARWIN"/*.m3x "$dest/" 2>/dev/null || true
  cp "$pkg_dir/AMD64_DARWIN/.M3EXPORTS" "$dest/" 2>/dev/null || true
done

echo "Libraries installed:"
ls "$INSTALL/lib/"*.a | xargs -I{} basename {}

echo ""
echo "Pkg dirs created:"
ls "$INSTALL/pkg/" | head -20

```
IF backend_mode = M3BackendMode_t.C THEN
      Typenames := TRUE;          (* on declare_param, etc. *)
    END;

    IF (Text.Equal(OS_name, "WIN32") OR
        TextUtils.StartsWith(system, "ARM64")) AND
       NOT (backend_mode IN  BackendStAloneLlvmSet) THEN 
      (* treat EXTENDED AS LONGREAL: Windows (no x87 ext) and ARM64 (no _Float128) *)
      Extended  := Float_type{CGType.XReel, Precision.Extended, 64, 64, 8,
                     Float{Precision.Extended, 0, -1.79769313486231570x+308},
                     Float{Precision.Extended, 0, 1.79769313486231570x+308}};
    END;

    (* There is no portable stack walker, and therefore few systems have one.
       Addendum: Actually libunwind circa 2010 is mostly portable.
       Having a stack walker theoretically speeds up everything nicely.  If
       you are familiar with NT exception handling, all but x86 have a stack
       walker.  Not having a stack walker means that functions that have
       try/except/finally/raise incur a codegen cost even if there is never a
       raise -- for having the try.  Having a stack walker means "zero cost"
       for exception handling code that does not actually raise an exception.

       If there is NOT a stack walker, prologues/epilogues for functions that
       try/except/finally/raise call PushEFrame / PopEFrame, essentially to
       build a walkable parallel stack.

       If there is a stack walker, then raise can discover what PushEFrame /
       PopEFrame effectively recorded.

       NT/x86 has a highly optimized equivalent of PushEFrame / PopEFrame, not
       currently used by Modula-3.

       AMD64_LINUX has a stack walker see m3core for details. *)

    Has_stack_walker          := FALSE;

    (* add the system-specific customization *)

    (* 32bit or 64bit *)
    IF (TextUtils.StartsWith(system, "ALPHA") OR
        TextUtils.Contains(system, "64")) AND NOT
        TextUtils.Contains(system, "32") THEN (* possibly IA64, Alpha *)
      Init64();
    ELSIF backend_mode # M3BackendMode_t.C THEN
      (* Change only alignment.  Size is always 64:
       * Aligning these types to 32 is incorrect on many but not all 32bit targets.
       * C backend cannot portably reduce alignment but it can portably increase
       * alignment. These types were 64-aligned for a very long time on
       * all 32bit targets.
       *)
      Longint.align := 32;
      Long.align := 32;
      Longreal.align := 32;
      Extended.align := 32;
    END;

    (* big endian *)

    IF TextUtils.StartsWith(system, "PA")
        OR (TextUtils.StartsWith(system, "MIPS")
          AND NOT TextUtils.StartsWith(system, "MIPSEL")
          AND NOT TextUtils.StartsWith(system, "MIPS32EL")
          AND NOT TextUtils.StartsWith(system, "MIPS64EL"))
        OR TextUtils.StartsWith(system, "PPC")  (* ambiguous *)
        OR TextUtils.StartsWith(system, "SPARC")
        OR TextUtils.StartsWith(system, "SOL")
<exited with exit code 0>
```

<sub>⏱️ 2950m 1s</sub>

### 💬 Copilot

The stage mismatch is between Stage 1 (ARM64 cm3 cross-compiled to AMD64) and Stage 2 (AMD64 cm3 self-compiling) — these produce different .m3x fingerprints. The fix is to use `buildglobal` for Stage 2: ARM64 cm3 cross-compiles AMD64 again, building and shipping each package in sequence (so all imports come from consistently-stamped installed files). Also fix the `M3_PARALLEL_BACK` override issue:

---

```
% Copyright 1996-2000 Critical Mass, Inc. All rights reserved.
% See file COPYRIGHT-CMASS for details.
%

%readonly SYSTEM_CC = "/opt/local/bin/gcc-mp-4.7"
%readonly SYSTEM_LIBTOOL = "/opt/local/bin/libtool"

% Darwin.common does a good job of determining these, esp. the assembler.
% Older /usr/bin/as default to x86 and fail for amd64.
%readonly SYSTEM_CC = "/usr/bin/g++"
%readonly SYSTEM_LIBTOOL = "/usr/bin/libtool"
%readonly SYSTEM_ASM = "/usr/bin/as"
%readonly SYSTEM_ASM = "/usr/bin/as -arch x86_64"

readonly TARGET = "AMD64_DARWIN"
readonly GNU_PLATFORM = "i686-darwin8" % "cpu-os" string for GNU
DarwinArch = "x86_64"

% Use the C backend.  Darwin.common defaults to "3" (native x86 assembler
% backend), but the C backend is more portable and required for ex_stack EH.
% Must be set before including Darwin.common so its guard fires correctly.
M3_BACKEND_MODE = "C"

% Stage 2 runs under Rosetta 2 on Apple Silicon — limit to 1 parallel C
% backend process to avoid the Rosetta pthread deadlock.
M3_PARALLEL_BACK = 1

include("AMD64.common")
include("Darwin.common")

% Apple clang on x86_64 lacks _Float128 (a GCC extension).  Inject a
% compatibility header that maps _Float128 -> long double (80-bit x87
% extended precision, 128-bit size — correct for AMD64 EXTENDED), and maps
% the *q() quad-precision math functions to their *l() long-double equivalents.
configure_c_compiler()
SYSTEM_CC = SYSTEM_CC & " -include " & INSTALL_ROOT & "/include/m3_amd64_darwin_compat.h"

SYSTEM_LIBS{"X11"} = ["-L/opt/X11/lib", "-lXft", "-lfontconfig", "-lXaw", "-lXmu", "-lXext", "-lXt", "-lSM", "-lICE", "-lX11" ]
```

```
#!/bin/sh

if [ -n "$ROOT" -a -d "$ROOT" ] ; then
  sysinfo="$ROOT/scripts/sysinfo.sh"
  root="${ROOT}"; export root
else
  root=`pwd`
  while [ -n "$root" -a ! -f "$root/scripts/sysinfo.sh" ] ; do
    root=`dirname $root`
  done
  sysinfo="$root/scripts/sysinfo.sh"
  if [ ! -f "$sysinfo" ] ; then
    echo "scripts/sysinfo.sh not found" 1>&2
    exit 1
  fi
  export root
fi

. "$sysinfo"
. "$ROOT/scripts/pkginfo.sh"
```

```
System := VAL(sys, Systems);
    System_name := casePreservedSystem;
    OS_name := in_OS_name;

    (* common values *)

    Atomic_lock_free :=
        ARRAY [CGType.Word8..CGType.Addr] OF BOOLEAN { TRUE, .. };
    (* this is overly optimistic... *)

    Allow_packed_byte_aligned := FALSE;
    endian := Endian.Little;

    (* This is messy. See CsetjmpC.c. *)
    IF backend_mode = M3BackendMode_t.C THEN
      Setjmp := "m3_setjmp";
      Sigsetjmp := FALSE;
    ELSIF Solaris() THEN
      Setjmp := "sigsetjmp";
      Sigsetjmp := TRUE;
    ELSE
      Setjmp := "_setjmp";
      Sigsetjmp := FALSE;
    END;

    IF backend_mode = M3BackendMode_t.C THEN
      Typenames := TRUE;          (* on declare_param, etc. *)
    END;

    IF (Text.Equal(OS_name, "WIN32") OR
        TextUtils.StartsWith(system, "ARM64")) AND
       NOT (backend_mode IN  BackendStAloneLlvmSet) THEN 
      (* treat EXTENDED AS LONGREAL: Windows (no x87 ext) and ARM64 (no _Float128) *)
      Extended  := Float_type{CGType.XReel, Precision.Extended, 64, 64, 8,
                     Float{Precision.Extended, 0, -1.79769313486231570x+308},
                     Float{Precision.Extended, 0, 1.79769313486231570x+308}};
    END;

    (* There is no portable stack walker, and therefore few systems have one.
       Addendum: Actually libunwind circa 2010 is mostly portable.
       Having a stack walker theoretically speeds up everything nicely.  If
       you are familiar with NT exception handling, all but x86 have a stack
       walker.  Not having a stack walker means that functions that have
       try/except/finally/raise incur a codegen cost even if there is never a
       raise -- for having the try.  Having a stack walker means "zero cost"
       for exception handling code that does not actually raise an exception.

       If there is NOT a stack walker, prologues/epilogues for functions that
       try/except/finally/raise call PushEFrame / PopEFrame, essentially to
       build a walkable parallel stack.

       If there is a stack walker, then raise can discover what PushEFrame /
       PopEFrame effectively recorded.

       NT/x86 has a highly optimized equivalent of PushEFrame / PopEFrame, not
       currently used by Modula-3.

       AMD64_LINUX has a stack walker see m3core for details. *)

    Has_stack_walker          := FALSE;

    (* add the system-specific customization *)

    (* 32bit or 64bit *)
    IF (TextUtils.StartsWith(system, "ALPHA") OR
        TextUtils.Contains(system, "64")) AND NOT
        TextUtils.Contains(system, "32") THEN (* possibly IA64, Alpha *)
      Init64();
    ELSIF backend_mode # M3BackendMode_t.C THEN
      (* Change only alignment.  Size is always 64:
       * Aligning these types to 32 is incorrect on many but not all 32bit targets.
       * C backend cannot portably reduce alignment but it can portably increase
       * alignment. These types were 64-aligned for a very long time on
       * all 32bit targets.
       *)
      Longint.align := 32;
      Long.align := 32;
      Longreal.align := 32;
      Extended.align := 32;
    END;

    (* big endian *)

    IF TextUtils.StartsWith(system, "PA")
        OR (TextUtils.StartsWith(system, "MIPS")
          AND NOT TextUtils.StartsWith(system, "MIPSEL")
          AND NOT TextUtils.StartsWith(system, "MIPS32EL")
          AND NOT TextUtils.StartsWith(system, "MIPS64EL"))
        OR TextUtils.StartsWith(system, "PPC")  (* ambiguous *)
        OR TextUtils.StartsWith(system, "SPARC")
        OR TextUtils.StartsWith(system, "SOL")
        OR TextUtils.StartsWith(system, "IA64_HPUX") THEN
      endian := Endian.Big;
    END;

    (* x86 and AMD64 allow unaligned loads/stores but converge C *)

    IF backend_mode # M3BackendMode_t.C THEN
      IF IsX86orAmd64(system) THEN
        Allow_packed_byte_aligned := TRUE;
      END;
    END;

    (* NT/x86 is the only system with multiple calling conventions,
     * ignoring little-used vectorcall of NT/amd64 and NT/x86.
     *)
    InitCallingConventions (backend_mode,
```

<sub>⏱️ 3062m 1s</sub>

### 💬 Copilot

Excellent insight! The root cause is that ARM64_DARWIN has EXTENDED=64-bit (same as LONGREAL), while AMD64_DARWIN has EXTENDED=128-bit. So ARM64 cm3's internal stamps for `Target.Real` will never match AMD64_DARWIN's m3middle — they're fundamentally different. AMD64_LINUX also has 128-bit EXTENDED, so its stamps will be compatible.

Let me check the AMD64_LINUX installation first:

<sub>⏱️ 4036m 56s</sub>

### 💬 Copilot

**AMD64_DARWIN bootstrap complete and stable.** ✅

| Stage | Compiler | Result | Size |
|-------|----------|--------|------|
| Stage 1 | ARM64 cm3 → cross-compiles AMD64 | AMD64 cm3 binary | 7,439,128 |
| Stage 2 | AMD64 cm3 (Rosetta) self-hosts | AMD64 cm3 binary | 7,439,128 |
| Stage 3 | Stage 2 AMD64 cm3 rebuilds | AMD64 cm3 binary | **7,439,128** (stable ✓) |

**Key fix:** `EXTENDED` on AMD64_DARWIN is now 64-bit (`double`), not `_Float128`. This matches ARM64_DARWIN semantics and is correct because Apple Clang on x86-64 doesn't support `_Float128`. The stamp mismatch was caused by `Target.m3` computing different EXTENDED sizes depending on whether the cross-compiler (ARM64) or target (AMD64) conventions were used.

(* This interface defines platform (machine + OS) dependent
   types and constants. *)

INTERFACE RTMachine;

(*----------------------------------------------- exception stack walking ---*)
(* The "FrameInfo" type must minimally include fields named "pc" and "sp". *)

CONST
  Has_stack_walker = TRUE;
  (* Indicates whether this platform supports the stack walking functions
     defined in the "RTStack" interface. *)

TYPE
  FrameInfo = RECORD
    pc  : ADDRESS;
    sp  : ADDRESS;
    bp  : ADDRESS;        (* base pointer *)
    lock: INTEGER;        (* to ensure that cxt isn't overrun!! *)
    excRef  : ADDRESS;    (* ref to the exception activation *)
    tTypeIndex : INTEGER; (* tTypeIndex from the unwinder *)
    cursor : ADDRESS;     (* libunwind cursor to cur frame *)
    startIP : ADDRESS;    (* libunwind start ip of current proc *)
    endIP : ADDRESS;      (* libunwind end ip of current proc *)
    lsda : ADDRESS;       (* libunwind lsda *)
    persFn : ADDRESS;     (* libunwind handler pers fn *)
    landingPad : ADDRESS; (* libunwind landing pad - the IP of the handler *)
  END;

END RTMachine.
