/* Copyright (C) 1990, Digital Equipment Corporation           */
/* All rights reserved.                                        */
/* See the file COPYRIGHT for a full description.              */
/* Last modified on Thu May  4 09:34:11 PDT 1995 by kalsow     */
/*      modified on Tue May 18 13:21:11 PDT 1993 by muller     */
/*      modified on Tue Jan 19 15:20:48 PST 1993 by burrows    */

/* This file implements the stack walking functions of
   the RTStack interface. */

#include <stdlib.h>
#include <stdio.h>
#include <string.h>
#include <setjmp.h>
#include <signal.h>
#include <libunwind.h>


#ifdef __cplusplus
extern "C" {
#endif

//Define the exception handling register number. 0 should be safe
//across most architectures.
#define EHObjRegNo  0
#define EHTypeRegNo 1

//declare a personality function
void * __m3_personality_v0();

//external M3 alloc memory
extern char * RTException__AllocBuf(int size);

/*
  FrameInfo = RECORD
    pc  : ADDRESS;
    sp  : ADDRESS;
    bp  : ADDRESS;        (* base pointer *)
    lock: INTEGER;        (* to ensure that cxt isn't overrun!! *)
    excRef  : ADDRESS;    (* ref to the exception activation *)
    tTypeIndex : INTEGER; (* tTypeIndex from exception table *)
    cursor : ADDRESS;     (* libunwind cursor to cur frame *)
    startIP : ADDRESS;    (* libunwind start ip of current proc *)
    endIP : ADDRESS;      (* libunwind end ip of current proc *)
    lsda : ADDRESS;       (* libunwind lsda *)
    persFn : ADDRESS;     (* libunwind handler pers fn *)
    landingPad : ADDRESS; (* libunwind landing pad *)
  END;
 * The typedef below must agree with the definition replicated here
 * and defined in RTMachine.i3
 */

typedef struct {
  unsigned long pc;
  unsigned long sp;
  unsigned long bp; //not used
  long lock;
  unsigned long exceptionRef;
  long tTypeIndex;
  unw_cursor_t *cursor;
  unw_word_t start_ip;
  unw_word_t end_ip;
  unw_word_t lsda;
  unw_word_t persFn;
  unw_word_t landingPad;
} Frame;

#define FrameLock 0x1234567890

void * __m3_personality_v0() {
  printf("m3 personality\n");
  return NULL;
}

/*---------------------------------------------------------------------------*/
/*
 * Get the procedure info for this frame including the personality function
 * and language specific data
 *
 * The unw_get_proc_info() routine returns auxiliary information about the procedure that created the stack frame identified by argument cp. The pip argument is a pointer to a structure of type unw_proc_info_t which is used to return the information. 
 */

void RTStack__GetProcInfo(Frame *f) {
  int res;
  unw_proc_info_t info;

  res = unw_get_proc_info(f->cursor, &info);
  if (res < 0) {
    printf("unw_get_proc_info error\n");
    abort();
  }
  f->start_ip = info.start_ip;
  f->end_ip = info.end_ip;
  f->lsda = info.lsda;
  f->persFn = info.handler;
}

/*---------------------------------------------------------------------------*/
/* PROCEDURE ProcName (READONLY f: Frame): ADDRESS;
   Return the null-terminated constant string that names the procedure
   corresponding to the stack frame "f".  Returns NIL if no name is
   known. */

char* RTStack__ProcName (Frame *f)
{
  int res;
  char *name;
  long name_len = 50;
  unw_word_t ofp;

  name = (char *) malloc(name_len);
  //there is a small mem leak here but as it is only called
  //during debugex of the stack unwinder it should be fine.

  res = unw_get_proc_name(f->cursor, name, name_len, &ofp);
  if (res == 0) {
    return name;
  } else {
    return 0;
  }
}

/*---------------------------------------------------------------------------*/
/* PROCEDURE GetThreadFrame (VAR f: Frame;  start: ADDRESS;  len: INTEGER);
   Return in "f" the frame of the thread whose machine state is in bytes
   [start .. start+len).  Returns with f.pc=NIL on failure. */

void RTStack__GetThreadFrame (Frame *f, char *start, int len)
{
  // not implemented 
  abort();
}

/*---------------------------------------------------------------------------*/
/* PROCEDURE CurrentFrame (VAR(*OUT*) f: Frame)
 * returns the frame that corresponds to its caller. */

void RTStack__CurFrame (Frame *f)
{
  unw_context_t *uc;
  unw_cursor_t *cursor;
  unw_word_t ip, sp = 0;

  //we alloc in m3 otherwise a serious memory leak 
  //uc = (unw_context_t *) malloc(sizeof(unw_context_t));
  //cursor = (unw_cursor_t *) malloc(sizeof(unw_cursor_t));
  uc = (unw_context_t *) RTException__AllocBuf(sizeof(unw_context_t));
  cursor = (unw_cursor_t *) RTException__AllocBuf(sizeof(unw_cursor_t));

  f->lock = FrameLock;
  unw_getcontext(uc);
  unw_init_local(cursor, uc);
  unw_get_reg(cursor, UNW_REG_IP, &ip);
  unw_get_reg(cursor, UNW_REG_SP, &sp);
  
  f->cursor = cursor;
  f->pc = ip;
  f->sp = sp;
  RTStack__GetProcInfo(f);

  if (f->lock != FrameLock) abort ();
}

/*---------------------------------------------------------------------------*/
/* PROCEDURE PreviousFrame (READONLY callee: Frame;  VAR(*OUT*)caller: Frame)
   Return the stack frame that called "callee".  Returns with pc = NIL if
   "callee" is the first frame on the stack or its predecessor is ill-formed.
   */

void RTStack__PrevFrame (Frame* callee, Frame* caller)
{
  unw_word_t ip, sp = 0;
  int res;

  if (!callee->cursor) abort();

  if (callee->lock != FrameLock) abort ();
  *caller = *callee;

  res = unw_step(caller->cursor);
  if (res > 0) {
    unw_get_reg(caller->cursor, UNW_REG_IP, &ip);
    unw_get_reg(caller->cursor, UNW_REG_SP, &sp);
    
    caller->pc = ip;
    caller->sp = sp;
    RTStack__GetProcInfo(caller);

  } else {
    caller->pc = 0;
    caller->sp = 0;
  }
  if (caller->lock != FrameLock) abort ();
}

/*---------------------------------------------------------------------------*/
/* PROCEDURE Unwind (READONLY f: Frame);
   Restore the machine state back to the frame "f".  All callee-saved
   registers must be restored to the state they were in when frame "f"
   made its last call. */

void RTStack__Unwind (Frame *target)
{
  int res;

  if (!target->cursor) abort();
  if (target->lock != FrameLock) abort ();
  
  //set the IP to landingPad 
  unw_set_reg(target->cursor, UNW_REG_IP, target->landingPad);
  
  //set the eh register zero to return the exception object
  unw_set_reg(target->cursor,
	      __builtin_eh_return_data_regno(EHObjRegNo),
	      target->exceptionRef);
 
  //set the eh register one to the tTypeIndex for gcc
  unw_set_reg(target->cursor,
	      __builtin_eh_return_data_regno(EHTypeRegNo),
	      target->tTypeIndex);

  res = unw_resume(target->cursor);
  //success means unreachable from here
  if (res < 0) {
    printf("RTStack__Unwind - unw_resume error\n");
    abort();
  }
}

//a test of generating a backtrace with libunwind.

    ret = unw_get_proc_name(&cursor, name, name_len, &ofp);
    printf("name %s\n",name);
  }
}
*/

#ifdef __cplusplus
} /* extern "C" */
#endif

/* Copyright (C) 1990, Digital Equipment Corporation           */
/* All rights reserved.                                        */
/* See the file COPYRIGHT for a full description.              */

/* Stack walking functions for ARM64_DARWIN using Apple's libunwind.
   Apple's libunwind (part of libSystem.B.dylib) provides a compatible
   implementation of the nongnu libunwind API; no extra link flags needed. */

#include <stdlib.h>
#include <stdio.h>
#include <string.h>
#include <setjmp.h>
#include <signal.h>
#include <libunwind.h>


/* _M3Exc is the C++ exception type thrown by RTStack__ThrowM3Exc and caught
   by the "catch (_M3Exc& _m3exc)" clauses that M3C.m3 generates in each
   translation unit.  It must be a proper C++ struct (not inside extern "C")
   so that C++ EH type-matching works correctly.  The identical definition
   appears in the M3C.m3 preamble for generated translation units; ODR is
   satisfied because the layout is the same everywhere. */
#ifdef __cplusplus
struct _M3Exc { void* act; };
#endif

#ifdef __cplusplus
extern "C" {
#endif

/* Exception handling register numbers per the AArch64 DWARF ABI.
   Register 0 carries the exception object pointer; register 1 the
   selector (tTypeIndex).  __builtin_eh_return_data_regno() maps these
   abstract indices to the concrete DWARF register numbers for the target. */
#define EHObjRegNo  0
#define EHTypeRegNo 1

/* Personality function stub — the real dispatch is done in RTEHScan. */
void * __m3_personality_v0();

/* External M3 allocator — avoids a memory leak in CurFrame. */
extern char * RTException__AllocBuf(int size);

/*
  FrameInfo = RECORD
    pc  : ADDRESS;
    sp  : ADDRESS;
    bp  : ADDRESS;        (* base pointer — unused *)
    lock: INTEGER;        (* sentinel to detect cursor overrun *)
    excRef  : ADDRESS;    (* ref to the exception activation *)
    tTypeIndex : INTEGER; (* tTypeIndex from exception table *)
    cursor : ADDRESS;     (* libunwind cursor to cur frame *)
    startIP : ADDRESS;    (* libunwind start ip of current proc *)
    endIP : ADDRESS;      (* libunwind end ip of current proc *)
    lsda : ADDRESS;       (* libunwind lsda *)
    persFn : ADDRESS;     (* libunwind handler pers fn *)
    landingPad : ADDRESS; (* libunwind landing pad *)
  END;
 * The typedef below must agree with the definition above
 * and in RTMachine.i3.
 */

typedef struct {
  unsigned long pc;
  unsigned long sp;
  unsigned long bp;
  long lock;
  unsigned long exceptionRef;
  long tTypeIndex;
  unw_cursor_t *cursor;
  unw_word_t start_ip;
  unw_word_t end_ip;
  unw_word_t lsda;
  unw_word_t persFn;
  unw_word_t landingPad;
} Frame;

#define FrameLock 0x1234567890

void * __m3_personality_v0() {
  printf("m3 personality\n");
  return NULL;
}

/*---------------------------------------------------------------------------*/
/*
 * Populate proc_info fields (start_ip, end_ip, lsda, persFn) for the
 * frame identified by the libunwind cursor in *f.
 */

void RTStack__GetProcInfo(Frame *f) {
  int res;
  unw_proc_info_t info;

  res = unw_get_proc_info(f->cursor, &info);
  if (res < 0) {
    printf("unw_get_proc_info error\n");
    abort();
  }
  f->start_ip = info.start_ip;
  f->end_ip   = info.end_ip;
  f->lsda     = info.lsda;
  f->persFn   = info.handler;
}

/*---------------------------------------------------------------------------*/
/* PROCEDURE ProcName (READONLY f: Frame): ADDRESS;
   Return the null-terminated constant string that names the procedure
   corresponding to the stack frame "f".  Returns NIL if no name is
   known. */

char* RTStack__ProcName (Frame *f)
{
  int res;
  char *name;
  long name_len = 50;
  unw_word_t ofp;

  /* Small leak is acceptable — only called for debug/diagnostic output. */
  name = (char *) malloc(name_len);

  res = unw_get_proc_name(f->cursor, name, name_len, &ofp);
  if (res == 0) {
    return name;
  } else {
    return 0;
  }
}

/*---------------------------------------------------------------------------*/
/* PROCEDURE GetThreadFrame (VAR f: Frame;  start: ADDRESS;  len: INTEGER);
   Return in "f" the frame of the thread whose machine state is in bytes
   [start .. start+len).  Returns with f.pc=NIL on failure. */

void RTStack__GetThreadFrame (Frame *f, char *start, int len)
{
  /* Not implemented. */
  abort();
}

/*---------------------------------------------------------------------------*/
/* PROCEDURE CurrentFrame (VAR(*OUT*) f: Frame)
 * Returns the frame that corresponds to the caller of this function. */

void RTStack__CurFrame (Frame *f)
{
  unw_context_t *uc;
  unw_cursor_t *cursor;
  unw_word_t ip, sp = 0;

  /* Allocate from the M3 heap so the cursor lifetime is managed there. */
  uc     = (unw_context_t *) RTException__AllocBuf(sizeof(unw_context_t));
  cursor = (unw_cursor_t *)  RTException__AllocBuf(sizeof(unw_cursor_t));

  f->lock = FrameLock;
  unw_getcontext(uc);
  unw_init_local(cursor, uc);
  unw_get_reg(cursor, UNW_REG_IP, &ip);
  unw_get_reg(cursor, UNW_REG_SP, &sp);

  f->cursor = cursor;
  f->pc     = ip;
  f->sp     = sp;
  RTStack__GetProcInfo(f);

  if (f->lock != FrameLock) abort();
}

/*---------------------------------------------------------------------------*/
/* PROCEDURE PreviousFrame (READONLY callee: Frame;  VAR(*OUT*) caller: Frame)
   Return the stack frame that called "callee".  Returns with pc = NIL if
   "callee" is the first frame on the stack or its predecessor is ill-formed.
   */

void RTStack__PrevFrame (Frame* callee, Frame* caller)
{
  unw_word_t ip, sp = 0;
  int res;

  if (!callee->cursor)           abort();
  if (callee->lock != FrameLock) abort();

  *caller = *callee;

  res = unw_step(caller->cursor);
  if (res > 0) {
    unw_get_reg(caller->cursor, UNW_REG_IP, &ip);
    unw_get_reg(caller->cursor, UNW_REG_SP, &sp);

    caller->pc = ip;
    caller->sp = sp;
    RTStack__GetProcInfo(caller);
  } else {
    caller->pc = 0;
    caller->sp = 0;
  }

  if (caller->lock != FrameLock) abort();
}

/*---------------------------------------------------------------------------*/
/* PROCEDURE Unwind (READONLY f: Frame);
   Restore the machine state back to the frame "f".  All callee-saved
   registers must be restored to the state they were in when frame "f"
   made its last call. */

void RTStack__Unwind (Frame *target)
{
  int res;

  if (!target->cursor)           abort();
  if (target->lock != FrameLock) abort();

  /* Set IP to the landing pad computed by RTEHScan.ScanEHTable. */
  unw_set_reg(target->cursor, UNW_REG_IP, target->landingPad);

  /* Pass the exception object pointer in EH data register 0. */
  unw_set_reg(target->cursor,
              __builtin_eh_return_data_regno(EHObjRegNo),
              target->exceptionRef);

  /* Pass the tTypeIndex (exception selector) in EH data register 1. */
  unw_set_reg(target->cursor,
              __builtin_eh_return_data_regno(EHTypeRegNo),
              target->tTypeIndex);

  res = unw_resume(target->cursor);
  /* unw_resume only returns on error. */
  if (res < 0) {
    printf("RTStack__Unwind - unw_resume error\n");
    abort();
  }
}

#ifdef __cplusplus
} /* extern "C" */
#endif

#ifdef __cplusplus
/* RTStack__ThrowM3Exc is defined outside the extern "C" block so that the
   C++ compiler's exception-handling machinery is fully engaged (the throw
   expression needs C++ EH unwinding, not C abort semantics).  The
   extern "C" on the definition gives the symbol C linkage so that M3
   code can call it via the EXTERNAL pragma in RTStack.i3. */
extern "C" void RTStack__ThrowM3Exc(void* act) {
  throw _M3Exc{act};
}
#endif

<sub>⏱️ 4098m 57s</sub>

### 💬 Copilot

The picture is clear. The ARM64_DARWIN `RTStackC.c` and `RTMachine.i3` are **entirely architecture-independent** — they use the standard libunwind API which is identical on macOS for both arm64 and x86_64. The `M3C.m3` `_M3Exc`/throw machinery already works for AMD64_DARWIN (the C backend with `M3_BACKEND_MODE = "C"`).

The porting work is minimal — just create the `AMD64_DARWIN` runtime directory, add it to `HAS_STACK_WALKER`, and enable `M3_USE_STACK_WALKER` in the config. Let me do it:

% Copyright 1996-2000 Critical Mass, Inc. All rights reserved.
% See file COPYRIGHT-CMASS for details.
%

%readonly SYSTEM_CC = "/opt/local/bin/gcc-mp-4.7"
%readonly SYSTEM_LIBTOOL = "/opt/local/bin/libtool"

% Darwin.common does a good job of determining these, esp. the assembler.
% Older /usr/bin/as default to x86 and fail for amd64.
%readonly SYSTEM_CC = "/usr/bin/g++"
%readonly SYSTEM_LIBTOOL = "/usr/bin/libtool"
%readonly SYSTEM_ASM = "/usr/bin/as"
%readonly SYSTEM_ASM = "/usr/bin/as -arch x86_64"

readonly TARGET = "AMD64_DARWIN"
readonly GNU_PLATFORM = "i686-darwin8" % "cpu-os" string for GNU
DarwinArch = "x86_64"

% Use the C backend.  Darwin.common defaults to "3" (native x86 assembler
% backend), but the C backend is more portable and required for ex_stack EH.
% Must be set before including Darwin.common so its guard fires correctly.
M3_BACKEND_MODE = "C"

include("AMD64.common")
include("Darwin.common")

configure_c_compiler()

% Limit parallel C compilation to 1 to avoid pthread deadlock under Rosetta 2.
M3_PARALLEL_BACK = 1

% Uncomment to use C++ zero-cost exception handling (ex_stack) instead of
% the default setjmp/longjmp implementation (ex_frame).  Requires a full
% bootstrap to take effect (see README-ex_stack.md).

<technical_details>
**Backend mode "C" placement:**
- `M3_BACKEND_MODE = "C"` must be set BEFORE `include("Darwin.common")` in the platform config, because `Darwin.common` sets it to `"3"` inside `if not defined("M3_BACKEND_MODE")`. Setting it first prevents the "3" default from firing.
- It was previously set on line 1 of the installed `~/cm3/bin/cm3.cfg` — a historical artifact that has now been moved to the proper location (the platform config).

**ARM64_DARWIN ex_stack toggle:**
- Toggle is `M3_USE_STACK_WALKER = TRUE` in the platform config. Commented out = `ex_frame` (setjmp). Uncommented = `ex_stack` (C++ throw).
- Requires a full bootstrap to take effect (see README-ex_stack.md).
- `SYSTEM_LIBS{"UNWIND"} = []` must always be present (even when toggle is off) so that `import_sys_lib("UNWIND")` in m3core's m3makefile doesn't error if the variable is referenced. Actually re-check: `import_sys_lib("UNWIND")` is only called inside `if defined("M3_USE_STACK_WALKER") ... end`, so it might not be strictly necessary when commented out — but it's harmless and safe to leave unconditional.

**AMD64_DARWIN compat header strategy (critical distinction from ARM64_DARWIN):**
- ARM64_DARWIN: `_Float128 → double` (64-bit), because ARM64 has no extended precision at all. `Target.Extended.size = 64`, uses `ext64` in m3makefiles.
- AMD64_DARWIN: `_Float128 → long double` (128-bit storage, 80-bit x87 precision), because `long double` on x86_64 macOS with Apple clang IS the correct 80-bit extended type. `Target.Extended.size = 128` (unchanged default), uses `ext128` in m3makefiles. **No changes needed to Target.m3 or m3makefiles for AMD64_DARWIN.**
- The `*q()` functions map to `*l()` (long double variants): `truncq→truncl`, `floorq→floorl`, `ceilq→ceill`, `llroundq→llroundl`.

**AMD64_DARWIN cross-compilation from ARM64:**
- ARM64 cm3 (`~/cm3/bin/cm3`) will be used to cross-compile.
- `uname()` on ARM64 returns `arm64` → `HOST = ARM64_DARWIN`. Must pass `-DTARGET=AMD64_DARWIN` via `BUILDARGS` (same pattern as ARM64 Stage 1 bootstrap).
- `Darwin.common`'s `configure_c_compiler()` automatically adds `-arch x86_64` (via `DarwinArch = "x86_64"`) to `SYSTEM_CC`, so cross-compilation to x86_64 is handled automatically — no manual `-arch` flag needed.
- `M3_PARALLEL_BACK` can stay at 20 since the ARM64 cm3 running natively has no Rosetta deadlock issue.

**`~/cm3-AMD64_DARWIN/bin/cm3.cfg` still has stale line 1:**
- This file still has `M3_BACKEND_MODE = "C"` on line 1 (same issue that was fixed for `~/cm3/bin/cm3.cfg`). Needs cleanup — that line should be removed since it's now properly in the platform config.

**Source config AMD64_DARWIN not yet updated:**

The approach follows the standard CM3 multi-stage bootstrap: Stage 1 (ARM64 cm3 cross-compiles to AMD64), Stage 2 (ARM64 cm3 rebuilds and ships all packages consistently using `buildglobal`), Stage 3 (AMD64 cm3 self-hosts under Rosetta for stability verification).

<technical_details>
--
It's defined as a regular `proc` in `cm3cfg.common` (line ~193), NOT a built-in Quake function like `HasCBackend`. Old installations without this proc fail when m3core's IEEE float m3makefile calls it. Fix: sync `cm3cfg.common` from a current installation.

**AMD64_DARWIN compat header strategy (`_Float128 → long double`):**
On x86_64 macOS, `long double` IS 80-bit x87 extended precision with 128-bit size — exactly what CM3's `EXTENDED` type expects. This differs from ARM64 (where `_Float128 → double`, 64-bit). AMD64 uses `ext128` in m3makefiles, Target.Extended.size=128. No changes to Target.m3 needed for AMD64.

**Stage 1 manual install required:**
`buildlocal` uses `-override` which marks packages as "not shippable". Must manually copy `.a` and `.m3x` files from source tree AMD64_DARWIN dirs to `~/cm3-AMD64_DARWIN/lib/` and `pkg/*/AMD64_DARWIN/`.

**Version stamp mismatch between ARM64 cm3 and AMD64 cm3 for same target:**
Even when both target AMD64_DARWIN, ARM64 cm3 and AMD64 cm3 produce DIFFERENT `.m3x` files (different MD5 confirmed for `libm3middle.m3x`). This causes `bad version stamps` in the linker (MxMerge.m3) when Stage 2 `buildlocal` mixes Stage 1 (ARM64-cm3-produced) and Stage 2 (AMD64-cm3-produced) `.m3x` files.

**Fix: use `buildglobal` for Stage 2:**
`buildglobal` = `cm3 -build && cm3 -ship` for each package in sequence, no `-override`. ARM64 cm3 cross-compiles all packages, importing from the install root (which gets progressively updated as packages ship). All stamps come from ARM64 cm3 — fully consistent. No stamp gap. Stage 3 then uses the AMD64 cm3 to self-host, and all imports come from consistently-stamped Stage 2 packages.

**cm3 binary not auto-shipped:**
`program("cm3")` (lowercase) in m3makefile means build but don't ship. Must manually `cp m3-sys/cm3/AMD64_DARWIN/cm3 ~/cm3-AMD64_DARWIN/bin/cm3` after each stage.

**m3cc always fails:**
The GCC-based backend (`m3cc`) crashes with `libc++abi: terminating due to uncaught exception of type _M3Exc` when cm3 tries to build it. This is expected and known — ignore it.

**`cm3 -ship` creates symlinks:**
Unlike the manual install (which copied files), `cm3 -ship` creates symlinks in `lib/` pointing to `pkg/TARGET/libXXX.a`. This is the correct behavior.

<sub>⏱️ 4109m 46s</sub>

### ✅ `bash`

**Manually install Stage 1 artifacts to ~/cm3-AMD64_DARWIN**

$ cd /Users/hosking/Downloads/cm3-d5.12.0

# Install .a files
for pkg in m3-libs/m3core m3-libs/libm3 m3-libs/set m3-libs/sysutils \
           m3-sys/m3middle m3-sys/m3objfile m3-sys/m3linker m3-sys/m3back \
           m3-sys/m3cggen m3-sys/m3quake m3-sys/m3front m3-sys/m3cgcat \
           m3-sys/mklib m3-sys/cm3; do
  pname=$(basename $pkg)
  srcdir="$pkg/AMD64_DARWIN"
  if [ -d "$srcdir" ]; then
    # Install .a files
    find "$srcdir" -name "*.a" -exec cp {} ~/cm3-AMD64_DARWIN/lib/ \;
    # Install .m3x and .M3EXPORTS files to pkg dir
    destdir=~/cm3-AMD64_DARWIN/pkg/$pname/AMD64_DARWIN
    mkdir -p "$destdir"
    find "$srcdir" \( -name "*.m3x" -o -name ".M3EXPORTS" \) -exec cp {} "$destdir/" \;
    echo "  installed: $pname"
  fi
done

# Install cm3 binary
cp m3-sys/cm3/AMD64_DARWIN/cm3 ~/cm3-AMD64_DARWIN/bin/cm3
echo "Installed cm3 binary"
ls -la ~/cm3-AMD64_DARWIN/bin/cm3

311. ### Verification
312. 
313. A simple sanity test after Phase 2:
314. 
315. ```modula3
316. MODULE Main;
317. IMPORT IO, OSError, FileRd, Thread;
318. EXCEPTION LocalExc(TEXT);
319. 
320. BEGIN
321.   (* Basic raise/catch *)
322.   TRY RAISE LocalExc("hello") EXCEPT LocalExc(m) => IO.Put("caught: " & m & "\n") END;
323. 
324.   (* Cross-exception dispatch — must NOT catch wrong type *)
325.   TRY
326.     TRY RAISE LocalExc("x") EXCEPT OSError.E => IO.Put("FAIL\n") END;
327.   EXCEPT LocalExc => IO.Put("reraise ok\n") END;
328. 
329.   (* FINALLY must run even when an exception propagates through *)
330.   VAR ran := FALSE;
331.   BEGIN
332.     TRY TRY RAISE LocalExc("f") FINALLY ran := TRUE END EXCEPT LocalExc => END;
333.     IF ran THEN IO.Put("finally ok\n") ELSE IO.Put("FAIL\n") END;
334.   END;
335. 
336.   (* LOCK must release the mutex when an exception escapes *)
337.   VAR mu := NEW(MUTEX);
338.   BEGIN
339.     TRY LOCK mu DO RAISE LocalExc("lock") END EXCEPT LocalExc => IO.Put("lock ok\n") END;
340.   END;
341. 
342.   (* Thread.Alerted must be caught by the correct handler *)
343.   TRY
344.     Thread.Alert(Thread.Self()); Thread.AlertPause(0.0d0);
345.   EXCEPT Thread.Alerted => IO.Put("alerted ok\n") END;
346. END Main.
347. ```
348. 
349. ---
350.

352.

357. `RTStackC.c` already implements `RTStack__CurFrame`, `RTStack__PrevFrame`,
358. and `RTStack__Unwind` using `libunwind`.
359. 
360. However, `AMD64_LINUX` typically uses the native x86_64 code generator

/* ARM64 Darwin compatibility for the CM3 C backend.
 *
 * Older pre-built CM3 binaries (e.g. AMD64_DARWIN) generate C++ code that uses
 * the GCC extension identifiers 'Infinity' and 'NaN' without defining them.
 * Newer binaries emit guarded #defines; the guards here prevent redefinition.
 *
 * ARM64 has no x87/quad-precision; EXTENDED == LONGREAL == double.
 * Apple clang lacks GCC's _Float128 type and the *q() quad-precision math
 * functions.  Map everything to the equivalent double operations so the
 * generated C++ compiles and links correctly.
 */
#ifndef Infinity
#define Infinity (__builtin_inf())
#endif
#ifndef NaN
#define NaN (__builtin_nan(""))
#endif
#define _Float128   double
#define truncq      trunc
#define floorq      floor
#define ceilq       ceil
#define llroundq    llround

include("ARM64.common")
include("Darwin.common")

% Set to 1 to avoid pthread_create deadlock under Rosetta 2 (AMD64->ARM64 translation).
% The Rosetta-translated cm3 binary hangs when spawning multiple POSIX threads.
% Native ARM64 cm3 can safely increase this if desired.
M3_PARALLEL_BACK = 1

% The CM3 C backend generates code that uses _Float128 (a GCC/GNU extension)
% for the EXTENDED float type, and calls *q() quad-precision math functions.
% Apple clang on ARM64 Darwin lacks these; inject a compat header that maps
% them to their double equivalents via -include.
configure_c_compiler()
SYSTEM_CC = SYSTEM_CC & " -include " & INSTALL_ROOT & "/include/m3_arm64_compat.h"

% Enable the native libunwind-based stack walker for ARM64_DARWIN.
% Apple's libunwind is part of libSystem.B.dylib (always linked), so no
% extra link flags are needed — SYSTEM_LIBS{"UNWIND"} is intentionally empty.
M3_USE_STACK_WALKER = TRUE

% libunwind is always available in libSystem.B.dylib on macOS — no extra link flags needed.
SYSTEM_LIBS{"UNWIND"} = []

if defined("M3_USE_STACK_WALKER")
end

% Homebrew.
SYSTEM_LIBS{"ODBC"} = ["-L/opt/homebrew/lib", "-liodbc", "-liodbcinst"]
SYSTEM_LIBS{"X11"} = ["-L/opt/X11/lib", "-lXft", "-lfontconfig", "-lXaw", "-lXmu", "-lXext", "-lXt", "-lSM", "-lICE", "-lX11" ]
SYSTEM_LIBS{"OPENGL"} = [ "-Wl,-dylib_file," & LIBGL_DYLIB & ":" & LIBGL_DYLIB,
						  "-L/opt/X11/lib", "-lGLU", "-lGL", "-lXext" ]

1. # Porting CM3 to ARM64_DARWIN (Apple Silicon)
2. 
3. This document describes the work done to bootstrap a native ARM64_DARWIN
4. CM3 compiler on Apple Silicon Macs (M1/M2/M3/…), starting from an existing
5. AMD64_DARWIN installation running under Rosetta 2.
6. 
7. ---
8. 
9. ## Starting Point
10. 
11. CM3 was already installed at `~/cm3` as an AMD64_DARWIN binary.  On Apple
12. Silicon this binary runs transparently under Rosetta 2, which translates
13. x86_64 instructions to ARM64 at runtime.  The source tree at
14. `~/Downloads/cm3-d5.12.0` was available for cross-compilation.
15. 
16. The goal was a fully self-hosted native ARM64 CM3 compiler installed at
17. `~/cm3`.
18. 
19. ---
20. 
21. ## Issues Encountered and Fixed
22. 
23. ### 1. ARM64 target not auto-detected by build scripts
24. 
25. `scripts/sysinfo.sh` handles the Darwin case by inspecting `uname -p`.  It
26. handles `powerpc` and `i386` but has no branch for `arm` or `arm64`, so it
27. falls through without setting `CM3_TARGET`.  This causes the wrapper scripts
28. (`pkgmap.sh`, `do-cm3-front.sh`) to error with "does not know about uname -a".
29. 
30. **Fix**: Set `CM3_TARGET=ARM64_DARWIN` explicitly in the environment before
31. invoking any build script.
32. 
33. ### 2. CM3 target not overridable via `M3CONFIG` alone
34. 
35. The CM3 startup sequence in `m3-sys/m3quake/src/MxConfigC.m3` calls
36. `uname()` first and sets `HOST` to whatever the OS reports.  Under Rosetta,
37. `uname` returns `x86_64`, so `HOST = AMD64_DARWIN`.  The `DefineIfNotDefined`
38. call for `TARGET` runs before `cm3.cfg` is read, so the `if not
39. defined("TARGET")` guard in `cm3.cfg` is always false — `M3CONFIG` alone
40. cannot change `TARGET`.
41. 
42. **Fix**: Pass `-DTARGET=ARM64_DARWIN` explicitly on the `cm3` command line,
43. via the `BUILDARGS` environment variable that `pkgcmds.sh` appends to the
44. build command:
45. 
46. ```sh
47. export BUILDARGS="-DTARGET=ARM64_DARWIN"
48. ```
49. 
50. This is only required for the AMD64 cm3 cross-building for ARM64.  Once the
51. native ARM64 binary is in use, `uname()` returns `arm64` and `TARGET` is set
52. correctly from `cm3.cfg` without any override.
53. 
54. ### 3. `EXTENDED` float type: ARM64 has no x87 extended precision
55. 
56. The Modula-3 type `EXTENDED` historically maps to the x87 80-bit extended
57. precision type on x86.  CM3 implements this via one of two subdirectories:
58. 
59. - `ext128/` — 128-bit EXTENDED using GCC's `_Float128` type (x86, Linux)
60. - `ext64/` — EXTENDED = LONGREAL (64-bit double), correct for Windows and ARM64
61. 
62. ARM64 has no x87 unit and no hardware support for any precision beyond 64-bit
63. double.  The existing condition that selected `ext64` only covered Windows
64. (`TARGET_OS = "NT"`); all other targets including ARM64 fell into `ext128`.
65. 
66. Three `m3makefile` files needed the additional ARM64 condition:
67. 
68. #### `m3-libs/m3core/src/float/IEEE/m3makefile`
69. ```diff
70. -if equal (TARGET_OS, "NT") and not IsBackendLlvm ()
71. +if (equal (TARGET_OS, "NT") and not IsBackendLlvm ()) or equal (TARGET_ARCH, "ARM64")
72.    include_dir ("ext64")
73.  else
74.    include_dir ("ext128")
75. ```
76. 
77. #### `m3-libs/m3core/src/float/IEEE-le/m3makefile`
78. Same change (selects `ExtendedRep.i3`).
79. 
80. #### `m3-libs/libm3/src/random/IEEE/m3makefile`
81. Same change (selects random float implementation).
82. 
83. ### 4. `Target.Extended` size mismatch between compiler and runtime
84. 
85. `m3-sys/m3middle/src/Target.m3` sets `Target.Extended.size` at runtime when
86. the compiler initialises for a given target.  The default is 128 bits (quad
87. precision).  An override to 64 bits existed only for `WIN32`.  When the new
88. ARM64 cm3 binary compiled with `ext128` in m3core tried to use
89. `LOOPHOLE(EXTENDED, T)` where `T` is 64 bits, m3front detected the size
90. mismatch and errored.
91. 
92. **Fix** in `m3-sys/m3middle/src/Target.m3`:
93. 
94. ```diff
95. -    IF (Text.Equal(OS_name, "WIN32")) AND NOT LlvmSet THEN
96. +    IF (Text.Equal(OS_name, "WIN32") OR
97. +        TextUtils.StartsWith(system, "ARM64")) AND NOT LlvmSet THEN
98.        (* treat EXTENDED AS LONGREAL: Windows (no x87 ext) and ARM64 (no _Float128) *)
99.        Extended := Float_type{ ..., 64, 64, 8, ... };
100. ```
````

</details>

102. ### 5. Apple clang lacks `_Float128` and quad-precision math functions
103. 
104. `M3C.m3` generates a C++ preamble containing:
105. 
106. ```c
107. # if defined(_MSC_VER)
108. typedef double EXTENDED;
109. # else
110. typedef _Float128 EXTENDED;
111. # endif
112. ```
113. 
114. Apple clang (LLVM) on ARM64 does not support `_Float128` (a GCC extension).
115. It also lacks the quad-precision math functions `truncq`, `floorq`, `ceilq`,
116. and `llroundq`.  Additionally, the conversion helper functions
117. (`m3_round`, `m3_trunc`, `m3_floor`, `m3_ceil`) used `#ifdef _WIN32` to
118. select the simple `llround(f)` form, falling back to `llroundq(_Float128)`
119. on other platforms — which also doesn't exist on ARM64.
120. 
121. **Fix 1** in `m3-sys/m3back/src/M3C.m3` — add ARM64 to the `typedef double`
122. branch:
123. 
124. ```diff
125. -# if defined(_MSC_VER)
126. +# if defined(_MSC_VER) || defined(__aarch64__)
127.  typedef double EXTENDED;
128. ```
129. 
130. **Fix 2** in `m3-sys/m3back/src/M3C.m3` — add ARM64 to all four conversion
131. helper guards:
132. 
133. ```diff
134. -#if defined(_WIN32)
135. +#if defined(_WIN32) || defined(__aarch64__)
136.  static INT64 __stdcall m3_round(EXTENDED f) { return llround(f); }
137.  ...
138. ```
139. 
140. ### 6. `Infinity` and `NaN` identifier conflicts
141. 
142. Older pre-built AMD64 CM3 binaries generate C++ files that use `Infinity`
143. and `NaN` as identifiers without ever `#define`-ing them (relying on a GCC
144. built-in extension not present in Apple clang).  The newer CM3 binary built
145. from source generates explicit `#define Infinity INFINITY` in the preamble.
146. 
147. These two code paths collide when building with the compat header (see below):
148. the header defines `Infinity` for the old binary's benefit, then the new
149. binary's generated code tries to `#define` it again — a redefinition error.
150. 
151. **Fix** in `m3-sys/m3back/src/M3C.m3` — add `#ifndef` guards around both
152. occurrences of the preamble definitions:
153. 
154. ```diff
155. +#ifndef Infinity
156.  #define Infinity INFINITY
157. +#endif
158. +#ifndef NaN
159.  #define NaN NAN
160. +#endif
161. ```
162. 
163. ### 7. Compatibility header for Apple clang (installed artifact)
164. 
165. Because some of the above issues (missing `_Float128`, missing `*q()`
166. functions, and the `Infinity`/`NaN` identifiers for old binaries) arise at C
167. compile time in generated code, a compatibility header is injected into every
168. compilation via the `-include` flag in `SYSTEM_CC`.
169. 
170. **File**: `~/cm3/include/m3_arm64_compat.h`  
171. (This file is an installed artifact, not in the source tree.)
172. 
173. ```c
174. /* ARM64 Darwin compatibility for the CM3 C backend. */
175. #ifndef Infinity
176. #define Infinity (__builtin_inf())
177. #endif
178. #ifndef NaN
179. #define NaN (__builtin_nan(""))
180. #endif
181. #define _Float128   double
182. #define truncq      trunc
183. #define floorq      floor
184. #define ceilq       ceil
185. #define llroundq    llround
186. ```
187. 
188. **Config** (`~/cm3/bin/config/ARM64_DARWIN`):
189. 
190. ```quake
191. configure_c_compiler()
192. SYSTEM_CC = SYSTEM_CC & " -include " & INSTALL_ROOT & "/include/m3_arm64_compat.h"
193. ```
194. 
195. The `configure_c_compiler()` call must precede the append because it
196. early-returns if `SYSTEM_CC` is already defined — calling it first ensures
197. the base flags are set before we extend them.
198. 
199. **Note**: The source file that should be updated for future installs is
200. `m3-sys/cminstall/src/config/ARM64_DARWIN`.  The compat header should

229. ### 9. `cm3 -ship` does not overwrite the running cm3 binary
230. 
231. `program ("cm3")` in `m3-sys/cm3/src/m3makefile` (lowercase, not
232. `Program`) tells CM3 to build the binary but not auto-ship it.  The ship
233. step only installs interface and library files.  This is intentional — it
234. prevents accidentally overwriting the running compiler mid-bootstrap.
235. 
236. **Workaround**: After each bootstrap stage, manually copy the new binary:
237. 
238. ```sh
239. cp m3-sys/cm3/src/ARM64_DARWIN/cm3 ~/cm3/bin/cm3
240. ```
241. 
242. ---
243. 
244. ## Bootstrap Process
245. 
246. ### Prerequisites
247. 
248. - Apple Silicon Mac (M1/M2/M3/…)
249. - Existing AMD64_DARWIN CM3 installation at `~/cm3` (runs under Rosetta 2)
250. - CM3 source tree at `~/Downloads/cm3-d5.12.0` (or similar)
251. - Xcode Command Line Tools (provides `clang`, `ar`, etc.)
252. 
253. ### Stage 1 — Cross-compile for ARM64 using AMD64 cm3 under Rosetta
254. 
255. The AMD64 cm3 binary is told to target ARM64_DARWIN by pointing it at the
256. ARM64 config file via `M3CONFIG`, and passing `-DTARGET=ARM64_DARWIN` to
257. override the startup target detection.
258. 
259. ```sh
260. cd ~/Downloads/cm3-d5.12.0
261. 
262. export ROOT=$(pwd)
263. export CM3_TARGET=ARM64_DARWIN
264. export INSTALLROOT=$HOME/cm3-ARM64_DARWIN
265. export M3CONFIG=$HOME/cm3-ARM64_DARWIN/bin/cm3.cfg
266. export BUILDARGS="-DTARGET=ARM64_DARWIN"
267. export PATH=$HOME/cm3/bin:$PATH    # AMD64 cm3 under Rosetta
268. 
269. # Build all "front" packages (m3core through cm3)
270. ./scripts/do-cm3-front.sh buildlocal
271. 
272. # Ship libraries to ~/cm3-ARM64_DARWIN/
273. ./scripts/do-cm3-front.sh ship
274. 
275. # Manually install the cm3 binary (ship doesn't overwrite it)
276. cp m3-sys/cm3/src/ARM64_DARWIN/cm3 ~/cm3-ARM64_DARWIN/bin/cm3
277. ```
278. 
279. Verify:
280. ```sh
281. file ~/cm3-ARM64_DARWIN/bin/cm3
282. # → Mach-O 64-bit executable arm64
283. 
284. ~/cm3-ARM64_DARWIN/bin/cm3 -version
285. # → host: ARM64_DARWIN, target: ARM64_DARWIN
286. ```
287. 
288. ### Stage 2 — Self-hosted build using the new native ARM64 cm3
289. 
290. With the Stage 1 ARM64 binary in place, rebuild everything natively.  No
291. `M3CONFIG` override or `-DTARGET` flag is needed: the native binary calls
292. `uname()` → `arm64` → `ARM64_DARWIN` automatically.
293. 
294. ```sh
295. cd ~/Downloads/cm3-d5.12.0
296. 
297. # Clean stale x86_64 build artifacts
298. find . -name "ARM64_DARWIN" -type d | xargs rm -rf
299. 
300. export ROOT=$(pwd)
301. export CM3_TARGET=ARM64_DARWIN
302. export INSTALLROOT=$HOME/cm3-ARM64_DARWIN
303. export PATH=$HOME/cm3-ARM64_DARWIN/bin:$PATH   # native ARM64 cm3
304. 
305. ./scripts/do-cm3-front.sh buildglobal   # build + ship in one step
306. 
307. # Manually install the cm3 binary
308. cp m3-sys/cm3/src/ARM64_DARWIN/cm3 ~/cm3-ARM64_DARWIN/bin/cm3
309. ```
310. 
311. ### Stage 3 — Stability verification (optional)
312. 
313. Repeat Stage 2 identically to confirm the output is stable (the binary
314. should compile itself to produce a functionally identical result).
315. 
316. ```sh
317. find . -name "ARM64_DARWIN" -type d | xargs rm -rf
318. ./scripts/do-cm3-front.sh buildglobal
319. cp m3-sys/cm3/src/ARM64_DARWIN/cm3 ~/cm3-ARM64_DARWIN/bin/cm3
320. ```
321. 
322. The Stage 2 and Stage 3 binaries will differ slightly in size due to
323. embedded `__DATE__`/`__TIME__` strings in `Version.c`, but the executable
324. code is identical.
325. 
326. ### Promote to default installation
327. 
328. After verifying Stage 3:
329. 
330. ```sh
331. mv ~/cm3 ~/cm3-AMD64_DARWIN      # preserve Rosetta backup
332. mv ~/cm3-ARM64_DARWIN ~/cm3      # promote native ARM64
333. ```
334. 
335. `INSTALL_ROOT` in `cm3.cfg` is computed dynamically as `path() & "/.."`
336. relative to the config file, so renaming the directory automatically updates
337. all paths.
338.

340. 
341. ## Summary of Changes
342. 
343. | File | Change |
344. |------|--------|
345. | `m3-sys/m3middle/src/Target.m3` | `Target.Extended` set to 64-bit for ARM64 targets (was WIN32-only) |
346. | `m3-sys/m3back/src/M3C.m3` | `typedef double EXTENDED` for `__aarch64__`; `#ifndef` guards on `Infinity`/`NaN`; `#if … || defined(__aarch64__)` in all four `cvt_int` helpers |

350. | `m3-sys/cminstall/src/config/ARM64_DARWIN` | `M3_PARALLEL_BACK = 1`; call `configure_c_compiler()`; inject compat header via `SYSTEM_CC` |

367. `M3_BACKEND_MODE = "C"`) on Darwin, not the GCC backend.

````
1. # Native C++ Exception Handling for ARM64_DARWIN (`ex_stack`)
2. 
3. This document describes the native stack-unwinding exception handling
4. implementation added for `ARM64_DARWIN`, explains the changes made to the
5. compiler and runtime, and documents the bootstrap process required to
6. transition from the old `ex_frame` (setjmp/longjmp) implementation to the
7. new `ex_stack` (C++ throw/catch) implementation.
8. 
9. ---
10. 
11. ## Background
12. 
13. CM3 has historically used a portable "frame-linked" exception handling
14. mechanism (`ex_frame`) in which:
15. 
16. - Each `TRY` block pushes a `jmp_buf` onto a per-thread singly-linked list.
17. - `RAISE` walks that list, calling `longjmp` to jump to the matching handler.
18. - `m3front` compiles `TRY/EXCEPT` via `Compile2`, which emits `setjmp` calls
19.   and the associated frame setup/teardown.
20. 
21. This approach is fully portable but has non-trivial overhead on every `TRY`
22. entry (a `setjmp` call) and does not interact with C++ destructors or other
23. language runtimes sharing the same stack.
24. 
25. The `ex_stack` implementation replaces this with **C++ zero-cost exception
26. handling**:
27. 
28. - `RAISE` calls `RTStack__ThrowM3Exc`, a C++ function that executes
29.   `throw _M3Exc{act}`, putting the M3 activation record into a C++ exception.
30. - The C++ runtime unwinds the stack using platform DWARF/EH tables, landing
31.   in `catch (_M3Exc& _m3exc)` clauses that `M3C.m3` generates around every
32.   call site inside a `TRY` block.
33. - `m3front` compiles `TRY/EXCEPT` via `Compile1`, which emits
34.   `CG.Start_try()` / `CG.End_try()` / `CG.Invoke_direct()` /
35.   `CG.Landing_pad()` instead of setjmp.
36. 
37. The result is that `TRY` blocks have zero overhead when no exception is
38. raised; cost is only incurred during unwinding.
39. 
40. ---
41. 
42. ## Requirement: C Backend (`M3_BACKEND_MODE = "C"`)
43. 
44. The `ex_stack` EH model **requires the C backend**.
45. 
46. `Compile1` in `m3front` emits `CG.Start_try()`, `CG.End_try()`,
47. `CG.Invoke_direct()`, and `CG.Landing_pad()`.  These operations are
48. implemented only in `M3C.m3` (the C code generator).  They cause `M3C.m3`
49. to emit C++ `try { … } catch (_M3Exc& _m3exc) { … }` blocks, which the
50. platform C++ compiler (clang/g++) then lowers to DWARF EH tables.
51. 
52. The native x86 assembly backend (`M3_BACKEND_MODE = "3"`, used by `M3x86`)
53. does **not** implement these operations.  Enabling `M3_USE_STACK_WALKER`
54. with a native backend would crash the compiler at code-generation time on
55. any `TRY` statement.
56. 
57. **Always pair `M3_USE_STACK_WALKER = TRUE` with `M3_BACKEND_MODE = "C"`.**
58. 
59. ARM64_DARWIN already requires `M3_BACKEND_MODE = "C"` because no native
60. ARM64 code generator exists in CM3.
61. 
62. ---
63. 
64. ## Files Changed
65. 
66. ### Runtime — `m3-libs/m3core`
67. 
68. #### `src/runtime/ARM64_DARWIN/RTMachine.i3`
69. Declares `Has_stack_walker = TRUE` and the extended `FrameInfo` record
70. that holds libunwind cursor state (`cursor`, `start_ip`, `end_ip`, `lsda`,
71. `persFn`, `landingPad`, `excRef`, `tTypeIndex`).  The `Has_stack_walker`
72. constant is **hardcoded TRUE** for `ARM64_DARWIN`, meaning the runtime
73. always uses C++ throw regardless of the config-file flag.
74. 
75. #### `src/runtime/ARM64_DARWIN/RTStackC.c`
76. Implements all stack-walking primitives using Apple's built-in libunwind
77. (part of `libSystem.B.dylib`; no extra link flags needed):
78. 
79. - `RTStack__CurFrame` — captures the current unwinder cursor.
80. - `RTStack__PrevFrame` — steps one frame up the stack.
81. - `RTStack__Unwind` — resumes execution at a specific landing pad
82.   (used in the manual-unwind path; not used by the C++ throw path).
83. - `RTStack__ThrowM3Exc(void* act)` — the key entry point.  Defined
84.   **outside** `extern "C"` so the C++ compiler's full EH machinery is
85.   engaged:
86. 
87.   ```c
88.   struct _M3Exc { void* act; };
89. 
90.   extern "C" void RTStack__ThrowM3Exc(void* act) {
91.       throw _M3Exc{act};
92.   }
93.   ```
94. 
95.   The `_M3Exc` struct must be declared in the same translation unit that
96.   contains the `catch (_M3Exc& …)` clauses.  `M3C.m3` emits the struct
97.   definition at the top of every generated `.c` file.
98. 
99. #### `src/runtime/ex_stack/RTExStack.m3`
100. Implements `RTException.Raise` and `RTException.ResumeRaise` for the
101. `ex_stack` runtime.  Key points:
102. 
103. - The `RaiseActivation` record must be **heap-allocated** before throwing,
104.   because the C++ unwinder destroys the original stack frame before landing
105.   in the catch clause.  A stack-allocated `act` would dangle:
106. 
107.   ```modula3
108.   excRef := NEW(REF RaiseActivation);
109.   excRef^ := act;
110.   RTStack.ThrowM3Exc(ADR(excRef^));
111.   ```
112. 
113. - `RTStack.ThrowM3Exc` never returns; the call to `InvokeBackstop` below it
114.   is an unreachable safety net only.
115. 
116. - The assertion `<*ASSERT RTStack.Has_walker*>` at module initialisation
117.   verifies that `ex_stack` is never accidentally linked into a build that
118.   has `Has_stack_walker = FALSE`.
119. 
120. #### `src/runtime/m3makefile`
````

</details>

120. #### `src/runtime/m3makefile`
121. The `HAS_STACK_WALKER` quake table controls which targets can use `ex_stack`:
122. 
123. ```quake
124. readonly HAS_STACK_WALKER = {
125.   "AMD64_LINUX"   : TRUE,
126.   "ARM64_DARWIN"  : TRUE,
127. }
128. ```
129. 
130. When `M3_USE_STACK_WALKER = TRUE` is set in the platform config **and** the
131. target appears in `HAS_STACK_WALKER`, `include_dir("ex_stack")` and
132. `include_dir(TARGET)` are used instead of `include_dir("ex_frame")`.
133. 
134. ---
135. 
136. ### Compiler front-end — `m3-sys/m3front`
137. 
138. The `Compile1` code path (enabled by `Target.Has_stack_walker`, set from the
139. `M3_USE_STACK_WALKER` config variable) required three correctness fixes.
140. 
141. #### `src/stmts/TryStmt.m3`
142. **Problem**: The original `Compile1` passed `last := TRUE` to
143. `CompileHandler1` for the final handler in a `TRY/EXCEPT` chain.  With
144. `last = TRUE` the type check was skipped, so the catch clause accepted
145. *any* M3 exception — silently routing unmatched exceptions (e.g.,
146. `OSError.E`) to the wrong handler (e.g., `Thread.Alerted`).
147. 
148. **Fix**:
149. 1. Always pass `last := FALSE` to `CompileHandler1`, ensuring every handler
150.    emits an explicit type check.
151. 2. Add a mandatory `ELSE` branch at the end of the handler chain.  When no
152.    handler matches, the `ELSE` branch calls `RTHooks.ResumeRaiseEx` to
153.    re-throw the exception so enclosing `TRY` blocks or the module-body
154.    backstop can handle it.
155. 
156. Without this fix, misrouted exceptions produced "Fatal Error: interrupted"
157. instead of the correct runtime error.
158. 
159. #### `src/stmts/TryFinStmt.m3`
160. **Problem**: `CG.End_try()` was placed *after* `CG.Set_label(l+1)` — putting
161. the FINALLY body *inside* the try region.  Any exception raised in the
162. FINALLY block (including the re-raise of the original exception) would be
163. caught by the same `catch` clause, causing infinite recursion.
164. 
165. **Fix**: Move `CG.End_try()` to just *before* `CG.Set_label(l+1)` so the
166. FINALLY body executes outside the try region.
167. 
168. #### `src/stmts/LockStmt.m3`
169. **Problem**: The same `End_try` placement issue in the `LOCK` statement's
170. `Compile1` path.  The mutex-release code and any exception handler ran
171. inside the try region.
172. 
173. **Fix**: Move `CG.End_try()` before `CG.Set_label(lab+1)` so the
174. lock-release and handler code are outside the try region.
175. 
176. ---
177. 
178. ### Compiler back-end — `m3-sys/m3back`
179. 
180. #### `src/M3C.m3`
181. **Problem**: `RTStack.ThrowM3Exc` is declared `<*EXTERNAL*>` with C calling
182. convention and returns void.  Without special treatment the C code generator
183. did not mark it as `[[noreturn]]`, so the C compiler emitted spurious
184. "control reaches end of non-void function" warnings and potentially generated
185. incorrect code for the callers of `RTExStack.Raise`.
186. 
187. **Fix**: Detect `RTStack__ThrowM3Exc` by name in `import_procedure` and set
188. `proc.no_return := TRUE`, causing `M3C.m3` to emit the `__attribute__((noreturn))`
189. (or `[[noreturn]]`) annotation in the generated C prototype.
190. 
191. The relevant fields and code added to `M3C.m3`:
192. 
193. ```modula3
194. (* in the T record fields, ~line 96 *)
195. RTStack_ThrowM3Exc_id : M3ID.T;
196. 
197. (* in begin_unit, ~line 3155 *)
198. self.RTStack_ThrowM3Exc_id := M3ID.Add("RTStack__ThrowM3Exc");
199. 
200. (* in import_procedure, ~line 6096 *)
201. ELSIF name = self.RTStack_ThrowM3Exc_id THEN
202.   proc.no_return := TRUE;
203.   no_return(self);
204. ```
205. 
206. The `start_try`, `end_try`, `invoke_direct`, `invoke_indirect`, and
207. `landing_pad` procedures in `M3C.m3` emit the C++ try/catch structure.
208. `invoke_direct` replaces `call_direct` inside a try region: instead of a
209. plain C function call it emits a C++ `try { f(…); goto next; } catch
210. (_M3Exc& _m3exc) { goto handler; }` pattern.
211. 
212. ---
213. 
214. ### Config — `m3-sys/cminstall/src/config/ARM64_DARWIN`
215. 
216. ```quake
217. M3_USE_STACK_WALKER = TRUE
218. 
219. % libunwind is part of libSystem.B.dylib on macOS — no extra link flags.
220. SYSTEM_LIBS{"UNWIND"} = []
221. ```
222. 
223. `SYSTEM_LIBS{"UNWIND"} = []` must be set unconditionally (outside any
224. `if defined("M3_USE_STACK_WALKER")` guard) so that the `import_sys_lib
225. ("UNWIND")` call in `m3core/src/runtime/m3makefile` does not fail with a
226. "does not define a value for UNWIND" error regardless of whether the config
227. variable is defined.
228.

241. generation), but is still linked against the safe `ex_frame` runtime.

257.    cd m3-sys/m3back   && cm3 -clean && cm3 -build && cm3 -ship   # includes noreturn fix

265. ### Why the Stage 3 binary cannot compile the new `RTExStack.m3` directly
266. 
267. The Stage 3 backup binary has an old `m3back` statically linked that
268. contains an assertion:
269. 
270. ```
271. <* ASSERT NOT proc.is_RTException_Raise *>
272. ```
273. 
274. This fires because `RTException.Raise` (declared in `RTExStack.m3`) is
275. detected as `is_RTException_Raise` in `declare_procedure`.  In the old
276. `ex_frame` implementation, `Raise` had a setjmp-based body that the old
277. m3back knew how to handle.  The new `ex_stack` body — which calls
278. `RTStack.ThrowM3Exc` inside a `RAISES ANY` scope — triggers a different
279. code-generation path in old m3back that trips the assertion.
280. 
281. The Phase 1 bootstrap sidesteps this by never asking the old m3back to
282. compile `RTExStack.m3` with `M3_USE_STACK_WALKER` active.  Once the Phase 1
283. binary is built, its internal m3back has the fixed code and does not contain
284. the problematic assertion.

311. ### Verification
312. 
313. A simple sanity test after Phase 2:
314. 
315. ```modula3
316. MODULE Main;
317. IMPORT IO, OSError, FileRd, Thread;
318. EXCEPTION LocalExc(TEXT);
319. 
320. BEGIN
321.   (* Basic raise/catch *)
322.   TRY RAISE LocalExc("hello") EXCEPT LocalExc(m) => IO.Put("caught: " & m & "\n") END;
323. 
324.   (* Cross-exception dispatch — must NOT catch wrong type *)
325.   TRY
326.     TRY RAISE LocalExc("x") EXCEPT OSError.E => IO.Put("FAIL\n") END;
327.   EXCEPT LocalExc => IO.Put("reraise ok\n") END;
328. 
329.   (* FINALLY must run even when an exception propagates through *)
330.   VAR ran := FALSE;
331.   BEGIN
332.     TRY TRY RAISE LocalExc("f") FINALLY ran := TRUE END EXCEPT LocalExc => END;
333.     IF ran THEN IO.Put("finally ok\n") ELSE IO.Put("FAIL\n") END;
334.   END;
335. 
336.   (* LOCK must release the mutex when an exception escapes *)
337.   VAR mu := NEW(MUTEX);
338.   BEGIN
339.     TRY LOCK mu DO RAISE LocalExc("lock") END EXCEPT LocalExc => IO.Put("lock ok\n") END;
340.   END;
341. 
342.   (* Thread.Alerted must be caught by the correct handler *)
343.   TRY
344.     Thread.Alert(Thread.Self()); Thread.AlertPause(0.0d0);
345.   EXCEPT Thread.Alerted => IO.Put("alerted ok\n") END;
346. END Main.
347. ```

350. 
351. ## Portability Notes
352. 
353. ### AMD64_LINUX
354. 
355. `AMD64_LINUX` has `Has_stack_walker = TRUE` in its `RTMachine.i3` and is
356. listed in `HAS_STACK_WALKER`, so the build infrastructure is ready.  Its
357. `RTStackC.c` already implements `RTStack__CurFrame`, `RTStack__PrevFrame`,
358. and `RTStack__Unwind` using `libunwind`.
359. 
360. However, `AMD64_LINUX` typically uses the native x86_64 code generator
361. (`M3_BACKEND_MODE = "3"`), which cannot generate `Start_try`/`End_try`/
362. `Landing_pad`.  To use `ex_stack` on AMD64_LINUX you must also set
363. `M3_BACKEND_MODE = "C"` and add `RTStack__ThrowM3Exc` to
364. `AMD64_LINUX/RTStackC.c` (a ~10-line addition identical in structure to
365. the `ARM64_DARWIN` version).
366. 
367. ### AMD64_DARWIN
368. 
369. Apple Silicon Macs can run x86_64 code under Rosetta 2, but Rosetta's
370. pthreads emulation has subtle issues (notably, some mutex/condvar operations
371. can deadlock when mixed with x86-64 CM3 binaries).  A native `AMD64_DARWIN`
372. `ex_stack` port is feasible — macOS `libSystem.B.dylib` provides libunwind
373. on x86_64 too — but would require:
374. 
375. 1. Creating `m3-libs/m3core/src/runtime/AMD64_DARWIN/RTMachine.i3` (copy
376.    from `ARM64_DARWIN`, adjust `FrameInfo` if needed).
377. 2. Creating `AMD64_DARWIN/RTStackC.c` with both frame walking and
378.    `RTStack__ThrowM3Exc`.
379. 3. Adding `"AMD64_DARWIN" : TRUE` to `HAS_STACK_WALKER` in
380.    `m3core/src/runtime/m3makefile`.
381. 4. Setting `M3_BACKEND_MODE = "C"` and `M3_USE_STACK_WALKER = TRUE` in
382.    the `AMD64_DARWIN` config (Darwin.common currently defaults to `"3"`).
383. 
384. ### Other targets
385. 
386. Any target using `M3_BACKEND_MODE = "C"` with a C++ compiler that supports
387. DWARF EH is a candidate.  The native x86 backend (`M3_BACKEND_MODE = "3"`)
388. cannot be used.
````

</details>

The newer CM3 binary built\nfrom source generates explicit `#define Infinity INFINITY` in the preamble.\n\nThese two code paths collide when building with older generated code: the\nolder code has bare `Infinity`/`NaN` identifiers, but newer generated code\ntries to `#define` them — a redefinition error.\n\n**Fix** in `m3-sys/m3back/src/M3C.m3` — add `#ifndef` guards around both\noccurrences of the preamble definitions:\n\n```diff\n+#ifndef Infinity\n #define Infinity INFINITY\n+#endif\n+#ifndef NaN\n #define NaN NAN\n+#endif\n```\n\n### 7. Rosetta 2 pthread deadlock with parallel compilation\n\nCM3 uses `M3_PARALLEL_BACK` to control how many parallel threads are spawned\nto compile generated C++ files.  The default is 20.\n\nUnder Rosetta 2, `pthread_create` from AMD64 translated code acquires\nRosetta's internal JIT/thread-registration lock. (Rosetta runtime)\n```\n\n**Fix** in the installed `ARM64_DARWIN` config:\n\n```quake\nM3_PARALLEL_BACK = 1\n```\n\nThis forces sequential C compilation during Stage 1 (cross-build with the\nAMD64 binary under Rosetta).  Once the native ARM64 cm3 is in use, this\nsetting is no longer needed — the native binary doesn't go through Rosetta\nand can safely use a higher value.\n\n### 8. `cm3 -ship` does not overwrite the running cm3 binary\n\n`program (\"cm3\")` in `m3-sys/cm3/src/m3makefile` (lowercase, not\n`Program`) tells CM3 to build the binary but not auto-ship it.  The ship\nstep only installs interface and library files.  This is intentional — it\nprevents accidentally overwriting the running compiler mid-bootstrap.\n\n**Workaround**: After each bootstrap stage, manually copy the new binary:\n\n```sh\ncp m3-sys/cm3/src/ARM64_DARWIN/cm3 ~/cm3/bin/cm3\n```\n\n---\n\n## Bootstrap Process\n\n### Prerequisites\n\n- Apple Silicon Mac (M1/M2/M3/…)\n- Existing AMD64_DARWIN CM3 installation at `~/cm3` (runs under Rosetta 2)\n- CM3 source tree at `~/Downloads/cm3-d5.12.0` (or similar)\n- Xcode Command Line Tools (provides `clang`, `ar`, etc.)\n\n### Stage 1 — Cross-compile for ARM64 using AMD64 cm3 under Rosetta\n\nThe AMD64 cm3 binary is told to target ARM64_DARWIN by pointing it at the\nARM64 config file via `M3CONFIG`, and passing `-DTARGET=ARM64_DARWIN` to\noverride the startup target detection.\n\n```sh\ncd ~/Downloads/cm3-d5.12.0\n\nexport ROOT=$(pwd)\nexport CM3_TARGET=ARM64_DARWIN\nexport INSTALLROOT=$HOME/cm3-ARM64_DARWIN\nexport M3CONFIG=$HOME/cm3-ARM64_DARWIN/bin/cm3.cfg\nexport BUILDARGS=\"-DTARGET=ARM64_DARWIN\"\nexport PATH=$HOME/cm3/bin:$PATH    # AMD64 cm3 under Rosetta\n\n# Build all \"front\" packages (m3core through cm3)\n./scripts/do-cm3-front.sh buildlocal\n\n# Ship libraries to ~/cm3-ARM64_DARWIN/\n./scripts/do-cm3-front.sh ship\n\n# Manually install the cm3 binary (ship doesn't overwrite it)\ncp m3-sys/cm3/src/ARM64_DARWIN/cm3 ~/cm3-ARM64_DARWIN/bin/cm3\n```\n\nVerify:\n```sh\nfile ~/cm3-ARM64_DARWIN/bin/cm3\n# → Mach-O 64-bit executable arm64\n\n~/cm3-ARM64_DARWIN/bin/cm3 -version\n# → host: ARM64_DARWIN, target: ARM64_DARWIN\n```\n\n### Stage 2 — Self-hosted build using the new native ARM64 cm3\n\nWith the Stage 1 ARM64 binary in place, rebuild everything natively.  No\n`M3CONFIG` override or `-DTARGET` flag is needed: the native binary calls\n`uname()` → `arm64` → `ARM64_DARWIN` automatically.\n\n```sh\ncd ~/Downloads/cm3-d5.12.0\n\n# Clean stale x86_64 build artifacts\nfind . -name \"ARM64_DARWIN\" -type d | xargs rm -rf\n\nexport ROOT=$(pwd)\nexport CM3_TARGET=ARM64_DARWIN\nexport INSTALLROOT=$HOME/cm3-ARM64_DARWIN\nexport PATH=$HOME/cm3-ARM64_DARWIN/bin:$PATH   # native ARM64 cm3\n\n./scripts/do-cm3-front.sh buildglobal   # build + ship in one step\n\n# Manually install the cm3 binary\ncp m3-sys/cm3/src/ARM64_DARWIN/cm3 ~/cm3-ARM64_DARWIN/bin/cm3\n```\n\n### Stage 3 — Stability verification (optional)\n\nRepeat Stage 2 identically to confirm the output is stable (the binary\nshould compile itself to produce a functionally identical result).\n\n```sh\nfind . -name \"ARM64_DARWIN\" -type d | xargs rm -rf\n./scripts/do-cm3-front.sh buildglobal\ncp m3-sys/cm3/src/ARM64_DARWIN/cm3 ~/cm3-ARM64_DARWIN/bin/cm3\n```\n\nThe Stage 2 and Stage 3 binaries will differ slightly in size due to\nembedded `__DATE__`/`__TIME__` strings in `Version.c`, but the executable\ncode is identical.\n\n### Promote to default installation\n\nAfter verifying Stage 3:\n\n```sh\nmv ~/cm3 ~/cm3-AMD64_DARWIN      # preserve Rosetta backup\nmv ~/cm3-ARM64_DARWIN ~/cm3      # promote native ARM64\n```\n\n`INSTALL_ROOT` in `cm3.cfg` is computed dynamically as `path() & \"/..\"`\nrelative to the config file, so renaming the directory automatically updates\nall paths.\n\n---\n\n## Summary of Changes\n\n| File | Change |\n|------|--------|\n| `m3-sys/m3middle/src/Target.m3` | `Target.Extended` set to 64-bit for ARM64 and AMD64_DARWIN targets |\n| `m3-sys/m3back/src/M3C.m3` | `typedef double EXTENDED` for `__aarch64__` and `(x86_64 && APPLE)`; `#ifndef` guards on `Infinity`/`NaN`; same condition in all four `cvt_int` helpers |\n| `m3-libs/m3core/src/float/IEEE/m3makefile` | Select `ext64/` for ARM64 and AMD64_DARWIN |\n| `m3-libs/m3core/src/float/IEEE-le/m3makefile` | Select `ext64/` for ARM64 and AMD64_DARWIN |\n| `m3-libs/libm3/src/random/IEEE/m3makefile` | Select `ext64/` for ARM64 and AMD64_DARWIN |\n| `m3-sys/cminstall/src/config/ARM64_DARWIN` | `M3_BACKEND_MODE = \"C\"`; `M3_USE_STACK_WALKER = TRUE`; `M3_PARALLEL_BACK = 1`; `SYSTEM_LIBS{\"UNWIND\"} = []` |\n\n---\n\n## Notes on `m3cc`\n\nThe `m3cc` package (GCC-based backend) always fails on ARM64_DARWIN with:\n\n```\nGNU platform is not known for ARM64_DARWIN\n```\n\nThis is expected and harmless.  CM3 uses its own C backend (`m3back`,\n`M3_BACKEND_MODE = \"C\"`) on Darwin, not the GCC backend.\n```\n\n---\n\n## Current README-ex_stack.md content:\n\n```\n# Native C++ Exception Handling for ARM64_DARWIN (`ex_stack`)\n\nThis document describes the native stack-unwinding exception handling\nimplementation added for `ARM64_DARWIN`, explains the changes made to the\ncompiler and runtime, and documents the bootstrap process required to\ntransition from the old `ex_frame` (setjmp/longjmp) implementation to the\nnew `ex_stack` (C++ throw/catch) implementation.\n\n---\n\n## Background\n\nCM3 has historically used a portable \"frame-linked\" exception handling\nmechanism (`ex_frame`) in which:\n\n- Each `TRY` block pushes a `jmp_buf` onto a per-thread singly-linked list.\n- `RAISE` walks that list, calling `longjmp` to jump to the matching handler.\n- `m3front` compiles `TRY/EXCEPT` via `Compile2`, which emits `setjmp` calls\n  and the associated frame setup/teardown.\n\nThis approach is fully portable but has non-trivial overhead on every `TRY`\nentry (a `setjmp` call) and does not interact with C++ destructors or other\nlanguage runtimes sharing the same stack.\n\nThe `ex_stack` implementation replaces this with **C++ zero-cost exception\nhandling**:\n\n- `RAISE` calls `RTStack__ThrowM3Exc`, a C++ function that executes\n  `throw _M3Exc{act}`, putting the M3 activation record into a C++ exception.\n- The C++ runtime unwinds the stack using platform DWARF/EH tables, landing\n  in `catch (_M3Exc& _m3exc)` clauses that `M3C.m3` generates around every\n  call site inside a `TRY` block.\n- `m3front` compiles `TRY/EXCEPT` via `Compile1`, which emits\n  `CG.Start_try()` / `CG.End_try()` / `CG.Invoke_direct()` /\n  `CG.Landing_pad()` instead of setjmp.\n\nThe result is that `TRY` blocks have zero overhead when no exception is\nraised; cost is only incurred during unwinding.\n\n---\n\n## Requirement: C Backend (`M3_BACKEND_MODE = \"C\"`)\n\nThe `ex_stack` EH model **requires the C backend**.\n\n`Compile1` in `m3front` emits `CG.Start_try()`, `CG.End_try()`,\n`CG.Invoke_direct()`, and `CG.Landing_pad()`.  These operations are\nimplemented only in `M3C.m3` (the C code generator).  They cause `M3C.m3`\nto emit C++ `try { … } catch (_M3Exc& _m3exc) { … }` blocks, which the\nplatform C++ compiler (clang/g++) then lowers to DWARF EH tables.\n\nThe native x86 assembly backend (`M3_BACKEND_MODE = \"3\"`, used by `M3x86`)\ndoes **not** implement these operations.  Enabling `M3_USE_STACK_WALKER`\nwith a native backend would crash the compiler at code-generation time on\nany `TRY` statement.\n\n**Always pair `M3_USE_STACK_WALKER = TRUE` with `M3_BACKEND_MODE = \"C\"`.**\n\nARM64_DARWIN already requires `M3_BACKEND_MODE = \"C\"` because no native\nARM64 code generator exists in CM3.\n\n---\n\n## Files Changed\n\n### Runtime — `m3-libs/m3core`\n\n#### `src/runtime/ARM64_DARWIN/RTMachine.i3`\nDeclares `Has_stack_walker = TRUE` and the extended `FrameInfo` record\nthat holds libunwind cursor state (`cursor`, `start_ip`, `end_ip`, `lsda`,\n`persFn`, `landingPad`, `excRef`, `tTypeIndex`).  The `Has_stack_walker`\nconstant is **hardcoded TRUE** for `ARM64_DARWIN`, meaning the runtime\nalways uses C++ throw regardless of the config-file flag.\n\n#### `src/runtime/ARM64_DARWIN/RTStackC.c`\nImplements all stack-walking primitives using Apple's built-in libunwind\n(part of `libSystem.B.dylib`; no extra link flags needed):\n\n- `RTStack__CurFrame` — captures the current unwinder cursor.\n- `RTStack__PrevFrame` — steps one frame up the stack.\n- `RTStack__Unwind` — resumes execution at a specific landing pad\n  (used in the manual-unwind path; not used by the C++ throw path).\n- `RTStack__ThrowM3Exc(void* act)` — the key entry point.  Defined\n  **outside** `extern \"C\"` so the C++ compiler's full EH machinery is\n  engaged:\n\n  ```c\n  struct _M3Exc { void* act; };\n\n  extern \"C\" void RTStack__ThrowM3Exc(void* act) {\n      throw _M3Exc{act};\n  }\n  ```\n\n  The `_M3Exc` struct must be declared in the same translation unit that\n  contains the `catch (_M3Exc& …)` clauses.  `M3C.m3` emits the struct\n  definition at the top of every generated `.c` file.\n\n#### `src/runtime/ex_stack/RTExStack.m3`\nImplements `RTException.Raise` and `RTException.ResumeRaise` for the\n`ex_stack` runtime.  Key points:\n\n- The `RaiseActivation` record must be **heap-allocated** before throwing,\n  because the C++ unwinder destroys the original stack frame before landing\n  in the catch clause.  A stack-allocated `act` would dangle:\n\n  ```modula3\n  excRef := NEW(REF RaiseActivation);\n  excRef^ := act;\n  RTStack.ThrowM3Exc(ADR(excRef^));\n  ```\n\n- `RTStack.ThrowM3Exc` never returns; the call to `InvokeBackstop` below it\n  is an unreachable safety net only.\n\n- The assertion `<*ASSERT RTStack.Has_walker*>` at module initialisation\n  verifies that `ex_stack` is never accidentally linked into a build that\n  has `Has_stack_walker = FALSE`.\n\n#### `src/runtime/m3makefile`\nThe `HAS_STACK_WALKER` quake table controls which targets can use `ex_stack`:\n\n```quake\nreadonly HAS_STACK_WALKER = {\n  \"AMD64_LINUX\"   : TRUE,\n  \"AMD64_DARWIN\"  : TRUE,\n  \"ARM64_DARWIN\"  : TRUE,\n}\n```\n\nWhen `M3_USE_STACK_WALKER = TRUE` is set in the platform config **and** the\ntarget appears in `HAS_STACK_WALKER`, `include_dir(\"ex_stack\")` and\n`include_dir(TARGET)` are used instead of `include_dir(\"ex_frame\")`.\n\n---\n\n### Compiler front-end — `m3-sys/m3front`\n\nThe `Compile1` code path (enabled by `Target.Has_stack_walker`, set from the\n`M3_USE_STACK_WALKER` config variable) required three correctness fixes.\n\n#### `src/stmts/TryStmt.m3`\n**Problem**: The original `Compile1` passed `last := TRUE` to\n`CompileHandler1` for the final handler in a `TRY/EXCEPT` chain.  With\n`last = TRUE` the type check was skipped, so the catch clause accepted\n*any* M3 exception — silently routing unmatched exceptions (e.g.,\n`OSError.E`) to the wrong handler (e.g., `Thread.Alerted`).\n\n**Fix**:\n1. Always pass `last := FALSE` to `CompileHandler1`, ensuring every handler\n   emits an explicit type check.\n2. Add a mandatory `ELSE` branch at the end of the handler chain.  When no\n   handler matches, the `ELSE` branch calls `RTHooks.ResumeRaiseEx` to\n   re-throw the exception so enclosing `TRY` blocks or the module-body\n   backstop can handle it.\n\nWithout this fix, misrouted exceptions produced \"Fatal Error: interrupted\"\ninstead of the correct runtime error.\n\n#### `src/stmts/TryFinStmt.m3`\n**Problem**: `CG.End_try()` was placed *after* `CG.Set_label(l+1)` — putting\nthe FINALLY body *inside* the try region.  Any exception raised in the\nFINALLY block (including the re-raise of the original exception) would be\ncaught by the same `catch` clause, causing infinite recursion.\n\n**Fix**: Move `CG.End_try()` to just *before* `CG.Set_label(l+1)` so the\nFINALLY body executes outside the try region.\n\n#### `src/stmts/LockStmt.m3`\n**Problem**: The same `End_try` placement issue in the `LOCK` statement's\n`Compile1` path.  The mutex-release code and any exception handler ran\ninside the try region.\n\n**Fix**: Move `CG.End_try()` before `CG.Set_label(lab+1)` so the\nlock-release and handler code are outside the try region.\n\n---\n\n### Compiler back-end — `m3-sys/m3back`\n\n#### `src/M3C.m3`\n**Problem**: `RTStack.ThrowM3Exc` is declared `<*EXTERNAL*>` with C calling\nconvention and returns void.  Without special treatment the C code generator\ndid not mark it as `[[noreturn]]`, so the C compiler emitted spurious\n\"control reaches end of non-void function\" warnings and potentially generated\nincorrect code for the callers of `RTExStack.Raise`.\n\n**Fix**: Detect `RTStack__ThrowM3Exc` by name in `import_procedure` and set\n`proc.no_return := TRUE`, causing `M3C.m3` to emit the `__attribute__((noreturn))`\n(or `[[noreturn]]`) annotation in the generated C prototype.\n\nThe relevant fields and code added to `M3C.m3`:\n\n```modula3\n(* in the T record fields, ~line 96 *)\nRTStack_ThrowM3Exc_id : M3ID.T;\n\n(* in begin_unit, ~line 3155 *)\nself.RTStack_ThrowM3Exc_id := M3ID.Add(\"RTStack__ThrowM3Exc\");\n\n(* in import_procedure, ~line 6096 *)\nELSIF name = self.RTStack_ThrowM3Exc_id THEN\n  proc.no_return := TRUE;\n  no_return(self);\n```\n\nThe `start_try`, `end_try`, `invoke_direct`, `invoke_indirect`, and\n`landing_pad` procedures in `M3C.m3` emit the C++ try/catch structure.\n`invoke_direct` replaces `call_direct` inside a try region: instead of a\nplain C function call it emits a C++ `try { f(…); goto next; } catch\n(_M3Exc& _m3exc) { goto handler; }` pattern.\n\n---\n\n### Config — `m3-sys/cminstall/src/config/ARM64_DARWIN` and `AMD64_DARWIN`\n\nBoth Darwin targets use identical config requirements for ex_stack:\n\n```quake\nM3_BACKEND_MODE = \"C\"        % must be before includes\nM3_USE_STACK_WALKER = TRUE   % must be before includes\n\n% libunwind is part of libSystem.B.dylib on macOS — no extra link flags.\nSYSTEM_LIBS{\"UNWIND\"} = []\n```\n\n`SYSTEM_LIBS{\"UNWIND\"} = []` must be set unconditionally (outside any\n`if defined(\"M3_USE_STACK_WALKER\")` guard) so that the `import_sys_lib\n(\"UNWIND\")` call in `m3core/src/runtime/m3makefile` does not fail with a\n\"does not define a value for UNWIND\" error regardless of whether the config\nvariable is defined.\n\n---\n\n## Bootstrap Process\n\nTransitioning from `ex_frame` to `ex_stack` cannot be done in a single step\nbecause the old compiler binary (statically linked with the old m3back)\ncannot compile the new `RTExStack.m3`.  A two-phase bootstrap is required.\n\n[rest of bootstrap process section is correct and unchanged]\n\n---\n\n## Portability Notes\n\n### AMD64_LINUX\n\n`AMD64_LINUX` has `Has_stack_walker = TRUE` in its `RTMachine.i3` and is\nlisted in `HAS_STACK_WALKER`, so the build infrastructure is ready.  Its\n`RTStackC.c` already implements `RTStack__CurFrame`, `RTStack__PrevFrame`,\nand `RTStack__Unwind` using `libunwind`.\n\nHowever, `AMD64_LINUX` typically uses the native x86_64 code generator\n(`M3_BACKEND_MODE = \"3\"`), which cannot generate `Start_try`/`End_try`/\n`Landing_pad`.  To use `ex_stack` on AMD64_LINUX you must also set\n`M3_BACKEND_MODE = \"C\"` and add `RTStack__ThrowM3Exc` to\n`AMD64_LINUX/RTStackC.c` (a ~10-line addition identical in structure to\nthe `ARM64_DARWIN` version).\n\n### AMD64_DARWIN\n\nAMD64_DARWIN (x86_64 macOS, running under Rosetta 2 on Apple Silicon) is\nnow fully ported — see `README-AMD64_DARWIN.md` for the full bootstrap\nprocedure and notes.\n\nThe port was straightforward: Apple's libunwind API on x86_64 macOS is\nidentical to the arm64 API (both are in `libSystem.B.dylib`), so\n`RTStackC.c` is identical to the ARM64_DARWIN version.\n\nAll five verification tests pass under Rosetta 2.\n\n### Other targets\n\nAny target using `M3_BACKEND_MODE = \"C\"` with a C++ compiler that supports\nDWARF EH is a candidate.  The native x86 backend (`M3_BACKEND_MODE = \"3\"`)\ncannot be used.\n```\n\n---\n\nNow produce the following output, with each file's content clearly marked:\n\n**Output file 1: README-ARM64_DARWIN.md**  \n**Output file 2: README-AMD64_DARWIN.md** (new file, modelled on README-ARM64_DARWIN.md but for AMD64_DARWIN)  \n**Output file 3: README-ex_stack.md**\n\nFor README-AMD64_DARWIN.md, model it closely on README-ARM64_DARWIN.md but covering:\n- Starting point: ARM64_DARWIN cm3 at ~/cm3 (native Apple Silicon binary)\n- Issues: EXTENDED=64-bit for AMD64_DARWIN (not 128-bit like AMD64_LINUX), `if not defined(\"TARGET\")` guard problem in cm3.cfg, M3_PARALLEL_BACK placement (must be after includes since AMD64.common unconditionally sets it to 20), `M3_BACKEND_MODE = \"C\"` must be before includes, no compat header needed\n- Bootstrap: Stage 1 (ARM64 cm3 cross-compiles AMD64 with buildlocal, manual install), Stage 2 (ARM64 cm3 cross-compiles with buildglobal, install cm3 binary), Stage 3 (AMD64 cm3 under Rosetta self-hosts with buildglobal — Stage 2=Stage 3=7,437,432 bytes)\n- Summary of changes table\n- Note on m3cc failure (expected)\n\nWrite clean, accurate, well-structured Markdown.
