## Current README-ARM64_DARWIN.md content:

```
# Porting CM3 to ARM64_DARWIN (Apple Silicon)

This document describes the work done to bootstrap a native ARM64_DARWIN
CM3 compiler on Apple Silicon Macs (M1/M2/M3/…), starting from an existing
AMD64_DARWIN installation running under Rosetta 2.

---

## Starting Point

CM3 was already installed at `~/cm3` as an AMD64_DARWIN binary.  On Apple
Silicon this binary runs transparently under Rosetta 2, which translates
x86_64 instructions to ARM64 at runtime.  The source tree at
`~/Downloads/cm3-d5.12.0` was available for cross-compilation.

The goal was a fully self-hosted native ARM64 CM3 compiler installed at
`~/cm3`.

---

## Issues Encountered and Fixed

### 1. ARM64 target not auto-detected by build scripts

`scripts/sysinfo.sh` handles the Darwin case by inspecting `uname -p`.  It
handles `powerpc` and `i386` but has no branch for `arm` or `arm64`, so it
falls through without setting `CM3_TARGET`.  This causes the wrapper scripts
(`pkgmap.sh`, `do-cm3-front.sh`) to error with "does not know about uname -a".

**Fix**: Set `CM3_TARGET=ARM64_DARWIN` explicitly in the environment before
invoking any build script.

### 2. CM3 target not overridable via `M3CONFIG` alone

The CM3 startup sequence in `m3-sys/m3quake/src/MxConfigC.m3` calls
`uname()` first and sets `HOST` to whatever the OS reports.  Under Rosetta,
`uname` returns `x86_64`, so `HOST = AMD64_DARWIN`.  The `DefineIfNotDefined`
call for `TARGET` runs before `cm3.cfg` is read, so the `if not
defined("TARGET")` guard in `cm3.cfg` is always false — `M3CONFIG` alone
cannot change `TARGET`.

**Fix**: Pass `-DTARGET=ARM64_DARWIN` explicitly on the `cm3` command line,
via the `BUILDARGS` environment variable that `pkgcmds.sh` appends to the
build command:

```sh
export BUILDARGS="-DTARGET=ARM64_DARWIN"
```

This is only required for the AMD64 cm3 cross-building for ARM64.  Once the
native ARM64 binary is in use, `uname()` returns `arm64` and `TARGET` is set
correctly from `cm3.cfg` without any override.

### 3. `EXTENDED` float type: ARM64 has no x87 extended precision

The Modula-3 type `EXTENDED` historically maps to the x87 80-bit extended
precision type on x86.  CM3 implements this via one of two subdirectories:

- `ext128/` — 128-bit EXTENDED using GCC's `_Float128` type (x86, Linux)
- `ext64/` — EXTENDED = LONGREAL (64-bit double), correct for Windows and ARM64

ARM64 has no x87 unit and no hardware support for any precision beyond 64-bit
double.  The existing condition that selected `ext64` only covered Windows
(`TARGET_OS = "NT"`); all other targets including ARM64 fell into `ext128`.

Three `m3makefile` files needed the additional ARM64 condition:

#### `m3-libs/m3core/src/float/IEEE/m3makefile`
```diff
-if equal (TARGET_OS, "NT") and not IsBackendLlvm ()
+if (equal (TARGET_OS, "NT") and not IsBackendLlvm ()) or equal (TARGET_ARCH, "ARM64")
   include_dir ("ext64")
 else
   include_dir ("ext128")
```

#### `m3-libs/m3core/src/float/IEEE-le/m3makefile`
Same change (selects `ExtendedRep.i3`).

#### `m3-libs/libm3/src/random/IEEE/m3makefile`
Same change (selects random float implementation).

### 4. `Target.Extended` size mismatch between compiler and runtime

`m3-sys/m3middle/src/Target.m3` sets `Target.Extended.size` at runtime when
the compiler initialises for a given target.  The default is 128 bits (quad
precision).  An override to 64 bits existed only for `WIN32`.  When the new
ARM64 cm3 binary compiled with `ext128` in m3core tried to use
`LOOPHOLE(EXTENDED, T)` where `T` is 64 bits, m3front detected the size
mismatch and errored.

**Fix** in `m3-sys/m3middle/src/Target.m3`:

```diff
-    IF (Text.Equal(OS_name, "WIN32")) AND NOT LlvmSet THEN
+    IF (Text.Equal(OS_name, "WIN32") OR
+        TextUtils.StartsWith(system, "ARM64")) AND NOT LlvmSet THEN
       (* treat EXTENDED AS LONGREAL: Windows (no x87 ext) and ARM64 (no _Float128) *)
       Extended := Float_type{ ..., 64, 64, 8, ... };
```

### 5. Apple clang lacks `_Float128` and quad-precision math functions

`M3C.m3` generates a C++ preamble containing:

```c
# if defined(_MSC_VER)
typedef double EXTENDED;
# else
typedef _Float128 EXTENDED;
# endif
```

Apple clang (LLVM) on ARM64 does not support `_Float128` (a GCC extension).
It also lacks the quad-precision math functions `truncq`, `floorq`, `ceilq`,
and `llroundq`.  Additionally, the conversion helper functions
(`m3_round`, `m3_trunc`, `m3_floor`, `m3_ceil`) used `#ifdef _WIN32` to
select the simple `llround(f)` form, falling back to `llroundq(_Float128)`
on other platforms — which also doesn't exist on ARM64.

**Fix 1** in `m3-sys/m3back/src/M3C.m3` — add ARM64 and AMD64_DARWIN to the `typedef double`
branch:

```diff
-# if defined(_MSC_VER)
+# if defined(_MSC_VER) || defined(__aarch64__) || (defined(__x86_64__) && defined(__APPLE__))
 typedef double EXTENDED;
```

**Fix 2** in `m3-sys/m3back/src/M3C.m3` — add the same condition to all four conversion
helper guards:

```diff
-#if defined(_WIN32)
+#if defined(_WIN32) || defined(__aarch64__) || (defined(__x86_64__) && defined(__APPLE__))
 static INT64 __stdcall m3_round(EXTENDED f) { return llround(f); }
 ...
```

### 6. `Infinity` and `NaN` identifier conflicts

Older pre-built AMD64 CM3 binaries generate C++ files that use `Infinity`
and `NaN` as identifiers without ever `#define`-ing them (relying on a GCC
built-in extension not present in Apple clang).  The newer CM3 binary built
from source generates explicit `#define Infinity INFINITY` in the preamble.

These two code paths collide when building with older generated code: the
older code has bare `Infinity`/`NaN` identifiers, but newer generated code
tries to `#define` them — a redefinition error.

**Fix** in `m3-sys/m3back/src/M3C.m3` — add `#ifndef` guards around both
occurrences of the preamble definitions:

```diff
+#ifndef Infinity
 #define Infinity INFINITY
+#endif
+#ifndef NaN
 #define NaN NAN
+#endif
```

### 7. Rosetta 2 pthread deadlock with parallel compilation

CM3 uses `M3_PARALLEL_BACK` to control how many parallel threads are spawned
to compile generated C++ files.  The default is 20.

Under Rosetta 2, `pthread_create` from AMD64 translated code acquires
Rosetta's internal JIT/thread-registration lock.  Spawning 20 threads
simultaneously deadlocks this lock — the build stalls indefinitely, with
`sample` showing all 2433 samples in:

```
ThreadPThread__thread_create → ??? (Rosetta runtime)
```

**Fix** in the installed `ARM64_DARWIN` config:

```quake
M3_PARALLEL_BACK = 1
```

This forces sequential C compilation during Stage 1 (cross-build with the
AMD64 binary under Rosetta).  Once the native ARM64 cm3 is in use, this
setting is no longer needed — the native binary doesn't go through Rosetta
and can safely use a higher value.

### 8. `cm3 -ship` does not overwrite the running cm3 binary

`program ("cm3")` in `m3-sys/cm3/src/m3makefile` (lowercase, not
`Program`) tells CM3 to build the binary but not auto-ship it.  The ship
step only installs interface and library files.  This is intentional — it
prevents accidentally overwriting the running compiler mid-bootstrap.

**Workaround**: After each bootstrap stage, manually copy the new binary:

```sh
cp m3-sys/cm3/src/ARM64_DARWIN/cm3 ~/cm3/bin/cm3
```

---

## Bootstrap Process

### Prerequisites

- Apple Silicon Mac (M1/M2/M3/…)
- Existing AMD64_DARWIN CM3 installation at `~/cm3` (runs under Rosetta 2)
- CM3 source tree at `~/Downloads/cm3-d5.12.0` (or similar)
- Xcode Command Line Tools (provides `clang`, `ar`, etc.)

### Stage 1 — Cross-compile for ARM64 using AMD64 cm3 under Rosetta

The AMD64 cm3 binary is told to target ARM64_DARWIN by pointing it at the
ARM64 config file via `M3CONFIG`, and passing `-DTARGET=ARM64_DARWIN` to
override the startup target detection.

```sh
cd ~/Downloads/cm3-d5.12.0

export ROOT=$(pwd)
export CM3_TARGET=ARM64_DARWIN
export INSTALLROOT=$HOME/cm3-ARM64_DARWIN
export M3CONFIG=$HOME/cm3-ARM64_DARWIN/bin/cm3.cfg
export BUILDARGS="-DTARGET=ARM64_DARWIN"
export PATH=$HOME/cm3/bin:$PATH    # AMD64 cm3 under Rosetta

# Build all "front" packages (m3core through cm3)
./scripts/do-cm3-front.sh buildlocal

# Ship libraries to ~/cm3-ARM64_DARWIN/
./scripts/do-cm3-front.sh ship

# Manually install the cm3 binary (ship doesn't overwrite it)
cp m3-sys/cm3/src/ARM64_DARWIN/cm3 ~/cm3-ARM64_DARWIN/bin/cm3
```

Verify:
```sh
file ~/cm3-ARM64_DARWIN/bin/cm3
# → Mach-O 64-bit executable arm64

~/cm3-ARM64_DARWIN/bin/cm3 -version
# → host: ARM64_DARWIN, target: ARM64_DARWIN
```

### Stage 2 — Self-hosted build using the new native ARM64 cm3

With the Stage 1 ARM64 binary in place, rebuild everything natively.  No
`M3CONFIG` override or `-DTARGET` flag is needed: the native binary calls
`uname()` → `arm64` → `ARM64_DARWIN` automatically.

```sh
cd ~/Downloads/cm3-d5.12.0

# Clean stale x86_64 build artifacts
find . -name "ARM64_DARWIN" -type d | xargs rm -rf

export ROOT=$(pwd)
export CM3_TARGET=ARM64_DARWIN
export INSTALLROOT=$HOME/cm3-ARM64_DARWIN
export PATH=$HOME/cm3-ARM64_DARWIN/bin:$PATH   # native ARM64 cm3

./scripts/do-cm3-front.sh buildglobal   # build + ship in one step

# Manually install the cm3 binary
cp m3-sys/cm3/src/ARM64_DARWIN/cm3 ~/cm3-ARM64_DARWIN/bin/cm3
```

### Stage 3 — Stability verification (optional)

Repeat Stage 2 identically to confirm the output is stable (the binary
should compile itself to produce a functionally identical result).

```sh
find . -name "ARM64_DARWIN" -type d | xargs rm -rf
./scripts/do-cm3-front.sh buildglobal
cp m3-sys/cm3/src/ARM64_DARWIN/cm3 ~/cm3-ARM64_DARWIN/bin/cm3
```

The Stage 2 and Stage 3 binaries will differ slightly in size due to
embedded `__DATE__`/`__TIME__` strings in `Version.c`, but the executable
code is identical.

### Promote to default installation

After verifying Stage 3:

```sh
mv ~/cm3 ~/cm3-AMD64_DARWIN      # preserve Rosetta backup
mv ~/cm3-ARM64_DARWIN ~/cm3      # promote native ARM64
```

`INSTALL_ROOT` in `cm3.cfg` is computed dynamically as `path() & "/.."`
relative to the config file, so renaming the directory automatically updates
all paths.

---

## Summary of Changes

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `m3-sys/m3middle/src/Target.m3` | `Target.Extended` set to 64-bit for ARM64 and AMD64_DARWIN targets |
| `m3-sys/m3back/src/M3C.m3` | `typedef double EXTENDED` for `__aarch64__` and `(x86_64 && APPLE)`; `#ifndef` guards on `Infinity`/`NaN`; same condition in all four `cvt_int` helpers |
| `m3-libs/m3core/src/float/IEEE/m3makefile` | Select `ext64/` for ARM64 and AMD64_DARWIN |
| `m3-libs/m3core/src/float/IEEE-le/m3makefile` | Select `ext64/` for ARM64 and AMD64_DARWIN |
| `m3-libs/libm3/src/random/IEEE/m3makefile` | Select `ext64/` for ARM64 and AMD64_DARWIN |
| `m3-sys/cminstall/src/config/ARM64_DARWIN` | `M3_BACKEND_MODE = "C"`; `M3_USE_STACK_WALKER = TRUE`; `M3_PARALLEL_BACK = 1`; `SYSTEM_LIBS{"UNWIND"} = []` |

---

## Notes on `m3cc`

The `m3cc` package (GCC-based backend) always fails on ARM64_DARWIN with:

```
GNU platform is not known for ARM64_DARWIN
```

This is expected and harmless.  CM3 uses its own C backend (`m3back`,
`M3_BACKEND_MODE = "C"`) on Darwin, not the GCC backend.
```

---

## Current README-ex_stack.md content:

```
# Native C++ Exception Handling for ARM64_DARWIN (`ex_stack`)

This document describes the native stack-unwinding exception handling
implementation added for `ARM64_DARWIN`, explains the changes made to the
compiler and runtime, and documents the bootstrap process required to
transition from the old `ex_frame` (setjmp/longjmp) implementation to the
new `ex_stack` (C++ throw/catch) implementation.

---

## Background

CM3 has historically used a portable "frame-linked" exception handling
mechanism (`ex_frame`) in which:

- Each `TRY` block pushes a `jmp_buf` onto a per-thread singly-linked list.
- `RAISE` walks that list, calling `longjmp` to jump to the matching handler.
- `m3front` compiles `TRY/EXCEPT` via `Compile2`, which emits `setjmp` calls
  and the associated frame setup/teardown.

This approach is fully portable but has non-trivial overhead on every `TRY`
entry (a `setjmp` call) and does not interact with C++ destructors or other
language runtimes sharing the same stack.

The `ex_stack` implementation replaces this with **C++ zero-cost exception
handling**:

- `RAISE` calls `RTStack__ThrowM3Exc`, a C++ function that executes
  `throw _M3Exc{act}`, putting the M3 activation record into a C++ exception.
- The C++ runtime unwinds the stack using platform DWARF/EH tables, landing
  in `catch (_M3Exc& _m3exc)` clauses that `M3C.m3` generates around every
  call site inside a `TRY` block.
- `m3front` compiles `TRY/EXCEPT` via `Compile1`, which emits
  `CG.Start_try()` / `CG.End_try()` / `CG.Invoke_direct()` /
  `CG.Landing_pad()` instead of setjmp.

The result is that `TRY` blocks have zero overhead when no exception is
raised; cost is only incurred during unwinding.

---

## Requirement: C Backend (`M3_BACKEND_MODE = "C"`)

The `ex_stack` EH model **requires the C backend**.

`Compile1` in `m3front` emits `CG.Start_try()`, `CG.End_try()`,
`CG.Invoke_direct()`, and `CG.Landing_pad()`.  These operations are
implemented only in `M3C.m3` (the C code generator).  They cause `M3C.m3`
to emit C++ `try { … } catch (_M3Exc& _m3exc) { … }` blocks, which the
platform C++ compiler (clang/g++) then lowers to DWARF EH tables.

The native x86 assembly backend (`M3_BACKEND_MODE = "3"`, used by `M3x86`)
does **not** implement these operations.  Enabling `M3_USE_STACK_WALKER`
with a native backend would crash the compiler at code-generation time on
any `TRY` statement.

**Always pair `M3_USE_STACK_WALKER = TRUE` with `M3_BACKEND_MODE = "C"`.**

ARM64_DARWIN already requires `M3_BACKEND_MODE = "C"` because no native
ARM64 code generator exists in CM3.

---

## Files Changed

### Runtime — `m3-libs/m3core`

#### `src/runtime/ARM64_DARWIN/RTMachine.i3`
Declares `Has_stack_walker = TRUE` and the extended `FrameInfo` record
that holds libunwind cursor state (`cursor`, `start_ip`, `end_ip`, `lsda`,
`persFn`, `landingPad`, `excRef`, `tTypeIndex`).  The `Has_stack_walker`
constant is **hardcoded TRUE** for `ARM64_DARWIN`, meaning the runtime
always uses C++ throw regardless of the config-file flag.

#### `src/runtime/ARM64_DARWIN/RTStackC.c`
Implements all stack-walking primitives using Apple's built-in libunwind
(part of `libSystem.B.dylib`; no extra link flags needed):

- `RTStack__CurFrame` — captures the current unwinder cursor.
- `RTStack__PrevFrame` — steps one frame up the stack.
- `RTStack__Unwind` — resumes execution at a specific landing pad
  (used in the manual-unwind path; not used by the C++ throw path).
- `RTStack__ThrowM3Exc(void* act)` — the key entry point.  Defined
  **outside** `extern "C"` so the C++ compiler's full EH machinery is
  engaged:

  ```c
  struct _M3Exc { void* act; };

  extern "C" void RTStack__ThrowM3Exc(void* act) {
      throw _M3Exc{act};
  }
  ```

  The `_M3Exc` struct must be declared in the same translation unit that
  contains the `catch (_M3Exc& …)` clauses.  `M3C.m3` emits the struct
  definition at the top of every generated `.c` file.

#### `src/runtime/ex_stack/RTExStack.m3`
Implements `RTException.Raise` and `RTException.ResumeRaise` for the
`ex_stack` runtime.  Key points:

- The `RaiseActivation` record must be **heap-allocated** before throwing,
  because the C++ unwinder destroys the original stack frame before landing
  in the catch clause.  A stack-allocated `act` would dangle:

  ```modula3
  excRef := NEW(REF RaiseActivation);
  excRef^ := act;
  RTStack.ThrowM3Exc(ADR(excRef^));
  ```

- `RTStack.ThrowM3Exc` never returns; the call to `InvokeBackstop` below it
  is an unreachable safety net only.

- The assertion `<*ASSERT RTStack.Has_walker*>` at module initialisation
  verifies that `ex_stack` is never accidentally linked into a build that
  has `Has_stack_walker = FALSE`.

#### `src/runtime/m3makefile`
The `HAS_STACK_WALKER` quake table controls which targets can use `ex_stack`:

```quake
readonly HAS_STACK_WALKER = {
  "AMD64_LINUX"   : TRUE,
  "AMD64_DARWIN"  : TRUE,
  "ARM64_DARWIN"  : TRUE,
}
```

When `M3_USE_STACK_WALKER = TRUE` is set in the platform config **and** the
target appears in `HAS_STACK_WALKER`, `include_dir("ex_stack")` and
`include_dir(TARGET)` are used instead of `include_dir("ex_frame")`.

---

### Compiler front-end — `m3-sys/m3front`

The `Compile1` code path (enabled by `Target.Has_stack_walker`, set from the
`M3_USE_STACK_WALKER` config variable) required three correctness fixes.

#### `src/stmts/TryStmt.m3`
**Problem**: The original `Compile1` passed `last := TRUE` to
`CompileHandler1` for the final handler in a `TRY/EXCEPT` chain.  With
`last = TRUE` the type check was skipped, so the catch clause accepted
*any* M3 exception — silently routing unmatched exceptions (e.g.,
`OSError.E`) to the wrong handler (e.g., `Thread.Alerted`).

**Fix**:
1. Always pass `last := FALSE` to `CompileHandler1`, ensuring every handler
   emits an explicit type check.
2. Add a mandatory `ELSE` branch at the end of the handler chain.  When no
   handler matches, the `ELSE` branch calls `RTHooks.ResumeRaiseEx` to
   re-throw the exception so enclosing `TRY` blocks or the module-body
   backstop can handle it.

Without this fix, misrouted exceptions produced "Fatal Error: interrupted"
instead of the correct runtime error.

#### `src/stmts/TryFinStmt.m3`
**Problem**: `CG.End_try()` was placed *after* `CG.Set_label(l+1)` — putting
the FINALLY body *inside* the try region.  Any exception raised in the
FINALLY block (including the re-raise of the original exception) would be
caught by the same `catch` clause, causing infinite recursion.

**Fix**: Move `CG.End_try()` to just *before* `CG.Set_label(l+1)` so the
FINALLY body executes outside the try region.

#### `src/stmts/LockStmt.m3`
**Problem**: The same `End_try` placement issue in the `LOCK` statement's
`Compile1` path.  The mutex-release code and any exception handler ran
inside the try region.

**Fix**: Move `CG.End_try()` before `CG.Set_label(lab+1)` so the
lock-release and handler code are outside the try region.

---

### Compiler back-end — `m3-sys/m3back`

#### `src/M3C.m3`
**Problem**: `RTStack.ThrowM3Exc` is declared `<*EXTERNAL*>` with C calling
convention and returns void.  Without special treatment the C code generator
did not mark it as `[[noreturn]]`, so the C compiler emitted spurious
"control reaches end of non-void function" warnings and potentially generated
incorrect code for the callers of `RTExStack.Raise`.

**Fix**: Detect `RTStack__ThrowM3Exc` by name in `import_procedure` and set
`proc.no_return := TRUE`, causing `M3C.m3` to emit the `__attribute__((noreturn))`
(or `[[noreturn]]`) annotation in the generated C prototype.

The relevant fields and code added to `M3C.m3`:

```modula3
(* in the T record fields, ~line 96 *)
RTStack_ThrowM3Exc_id : M3ID.T;

(* in begin_unit, ~line 3155 *)
self.RTStack_ThrowM3Exc_id := M3ID.Add("RTStack__ThrowM3Exc");

(* in import_procedure, ~line 6096 *)
ELSIF name = self.RTStack_ThrowM3Exc_id THEN
  proc.no_return := TRUE;
  no_return(self);
```

The `start_try`, `end_try`, `invoke_direct`, `invoke_indirect`, and
`landing_pad` procedures in `M3C.m3` emit the C++ try/catch structure.
`invoke_direct` replaces `call_direct` inside a try region: instead of a
plain C function call it emits a C++ `try { f(…); goto next; } catch
(_M3Exc& _m3exc) { goto handler; }` pattern.

---

### Config — `m3-sys/cminstall/src/config/ARM64_DARWIN` and `AMD64_DARWIN`

Both Darwin targets use identical config requirements for ex_stack:

```quake
M3_BACKEND_MODE = "C"        % must be before includes
M3_USE_STACK_WALKER = TRUE   % must be before includes

% libunwind is part of libSystem.B.dylib on macOS — no extra link flags.
SYSTEM_LIBS{"UNWIND"} = []
```

`SYSTEM_LIBS{"UNWIND"} = []` must be set unconditionally (outside any
`if defined("M3_USE_STACK_WALKER")` guard) so that the `import_sys_lib
("UNWIND")` call in `m3core/src/runtime/m3makefile` does not fail with a
"does not define a value for UNWIND" error regardless of whether the config
variable is defined.

---

## Bootstrap Process

Transitioning from `ex_frame` to `ex_stack` cannot be done in a single step
because the old compiler binary (statically linked with the old m3back)
cannot compile the new `RTExStack.m3`.  A two-phase bootstrap is required.

[rest of bootstrap process section is correct and unchanged]

---

## Portability Notes

### AMD64_LINUX

`AMD64_LINUX` has `Has_stack_walker = TRUE` in its `RTMachine.i3` and is
listed in `HAS_STACK_WALKER`, so the build infrastructure is ready.  Its
`RTStackC.c` already implements `RTStack__CurFrame`, `RTStack__PrevFrame`,
and `RTStack__Unwind` using `libunwind`.

However, `AMD64_LINUX` typically uses the native x86_64 code generator
(`M3_BACKEND_MODE = "3"`), which cannot generate `Start_try`/`End_try`/
`Landing_pad`.  To use `ex_stack` on AMD64_LINUX you must also set
`M3_BACKEND_MODE = "C"` and add `RTStack__ThrowM3Exc` to
`AMD64_LINUX/RTStackC.c` (a ~10-line addition identical in structure to
the `ARM64_DARWIN` version).

### AMD64_DARWIN

AMD64_DARWIN (x86_64 macOS, running under Rosetta 2 on Apple Silicon) is
now fully ported — see `README-AMD64_DARWIN.md` for the full bootstrap
procedure and notes.

The port was straightforward: Apple's libunwind API on x86_64 macOS is
identical to the arm64 API (both are in `libSystem.B.dylib`), so
`RTStackC.c` is identical to the ARM64_DARWIN version.

All five verification tests pass under Rosetta 2.

### Other targets

Any target using `M3_BACKEND_MODE = "C"` with a C++ compiler that supports
DWARF EH is a candidate.  The native x86 backend (`M3_BACKEND_MODE = "3"`)
cannot be used.

<sub>⏱️ 4389m 26s</sub>

### 💬 Copilot

Build artifacts live in `TARGET/` subdirectories (e.g., `AMD64_DARWIN/`, `ARM64_DARWIN/`) inside each package. You have two options:

**Per-package clean (via cm3):**
```sh
cd m3-sys/cm3/src
cm3 -clean           # removes TARGET/ for installed packages
cm3 -clean -override # removes TARGET/ for local builds
```

**Nuke all build dirs at once:**
```sh
find . -type d \( -name 'AMD64_DARWIN' -o -name 'ARM64_DARWIN' \) | grep -v '^\./ARM64_DARWIN$' | xargs rm -rf
```

Or using the scripts:
```sh
./scripts/do-cm3-std.sh realclean   # runs rm -rf ${TARGET} per package
```

The `realclean` action is the most thorough — it deletes the entire `TARGET/` directory in each package without invoking `cm3` at all. Use it when you want a completely fresh build. Be careful not to accidentally delete the top-level `ARM64_DARWIN/` or `AMD64_DARWIN/` installation trees if they live inside this checkout.

/* Copyright (C) 1990, Digital Equipment Corporation           */
/* All rights reserved.                                        */
/* See the file COPYRIGHT for a full description.              */

/* Stack walking functions for ARM64_DARWIN using Apple's libunwind.
   Apple's libunwind (part of libSystem.B.dylib) provides a compatible
   implementation of the nongnu libunwind API; no extra link flags needed. */

#include <stdlib.h>
#include <stdio.h>
#include <string.h>
#include <setjmp.h>
#include <signal.h>
#include <libunwind.h>


/* _M3Exc is the C++ exception type thrown by RTStack__ThrowM3Exc and caught
   by the "catch (_M3Exc& _m3exc)" clauses that M3C.m3 generates in each
   translation unit.  It must be a proper C++ struct (not inside extern "C")
   so that C++ EH type-matching works correctly.  The identical definition
   appears in the M3C.m3 preamble for generated translation units; ODR is
   satisfied because the layout is the same everywhere. */
#ifdef __cplusplus
struct _M3Exc { void* act; };
#endif

#ifdef __cplusplus
extern "C" {
#endif

/* Exception handling register numbers per the AArch64 DWARF ABI.
   Register 0 carries the exception object pointer; register 1 the
   selector (tTypeIndex).  __builtin_eh_return_data_regno() maps these
   abstract indices to the concrete DWARF register numbers for the target. */
#define EHObjRegNo  0
#define EHTypeRegNo 1

/* Personality function stub — the real dispatch is done in RTEHScan. */
void * __m3_personality_v0();

/* External M3 allocator — avoids a memory leak in CurFrame. */
extern char * RTException__AllocBuf(int size);

/*
  FrameInfo = RECORD
    pc  : ADDRESS;
    sp  : ADDRESS;
    bp  : ADDRESS;        (* base pointer — unused *)
    lock: INTEGER;        (* sentinel to detect cursor overrun *)
    excRef  : ADDRESS;    (* ref to the exception activation *)
    tTypeIndex : INTEGER; (* tTypeIndex from exception table *)
    cursor : ADDRESS;     (* libunwind cursor to cur frame *)
    startIP : ADDRESS;    (* libunwind start ip of current proc *)
    endIP : ADDRESS;      (* libunwind end ip of current proc *)
    lsda : ADDRESS;       (* libunwind lsda *)
    persFn : ADDRESS;     (* libunwind handler pers fn *)
    landingPad : ADDRESS; (* libunwind landing pad *)
  END;
 * The typedef below must agree with the definition above
 * and in RTMachine.i3.
 */

typedef struct {
  unsigned long pc;
  unsigned long sp;
  unsigned long bp;
  long lock;
  unsigned long exceptionRef;
  long tTypeIndex;
  unw_cursor_t *cursor;
  unw_word_t start_ip;
  unw_word_t end_ip;
  unw_word_t lsda;
  unw_word_t persFn;
  unw_word_t landingPad;
} Frame;

#define FrameLock 0x1234567890

void * __m3_personality_v0() {
  printf("m3 personality\n");
  return NULL;
}

/*---------------------------------------------------------------------------*/
/*
 * Populate proc_info fields (start_ip, end_ip, lsda, persFn) for the
 * frame identified by the libunwind cursor in *f.
 */

void RTStack__GetProcInfo(Frame *f) {
  int res;
  unw_proc_info_t info;

  res = unw_get_proc_info(f->cursor, &info);
  if (res < 0) {
    printf("unw_get_proc_info error\n");
    abort();
  }
  f->start_ip = info.start_ip;
  f->end_ip   = info.end_ip;
  f->lsda     = info.lsda;
  f->persFn   = info.handler;
}

/*---------------------------------------------------------------------------*/
/* PROCEDURE ProcName (READONLY f: Frame): ADDRESS;
   Return the null-terminated constant string that names the procedure
   corresponding to the stack frame "f".  Returns NIL if no name is
   known. */

char* RTStack__ProcName (Frame *f)
{
  int res;
  char *name;
  long name_len = 50;
  unw_word_t ofp;

  /* Small leak is acceptable — only called for debug/diagnostic output. */
  name = (char *) malloc(name_len);

  res = unw_get_proc_name(f->cursor, name, name_len, &ofp);
  if (res == 0) {
    return name;
  } else {
    return 0;
  }
}

/*---------------------------------------------------------------------------*/
/* PROCEDURE GetThreadFrame (VAR f: Frame;  start: ADDRESS;  len: INTEGER);
   Return in "f" the frame of the thread whose machine state is in bytes
   [start .. start+len).  Returns with f.pc=NIL on failure. */

void RTStack__GetThreadFrame (Frame *f, char *start, int len)
{
  /* Not implemented. */
  abort();
}

/*---------------------------------------------------------------------------*/
/* PROCEDURE CurrentFrame (VAR(*OUT*) f: Frame)
 * Returns the frame that corresponds to the caller of this function. */

void RTStack__CurFrame (Frame *f)
{
  unw_context_t *uc;
  unw_cursor_t *cursor;
  unw_word_t ip, sp = 0;

  /* Allocate from the M3 heap so the cursor lifetime is managed there. */
  uc     = (unw_context_t *) RTException__AllocBuf(sizeof(unw_context_t));
  cursor = (unw_cursor_t *)  RTException__AllocBuf(sizeof(unw_cursor_t));

  f->lock = FrameLock;
  unw_getcontext(uc);
  unw_init_local(cursor, uc);
  unw_get_reg(cursor, UNW_REG_IP, &ip);
  unw_get_reg(cursor, UNW_REG_SP, &sp);

  f->cursor = cursor;
  f->pc     = ip;
  f->sp     = sp;
  RTStack__GetProcInfo(f);

  if (f->lock != FrameLock) abort();
}

/*---------------------------------------------------------------------------*/
/* PROCEDURE PreviousFrame (READONLY callee: Frame;  VAR(*OUT*) caller: Frame)
   Return the stack frame that called "callee".  Returns with pc = NIL if
   "callee" is the first frame on the stack or its predecessor is ill-formed.
   */

void RTStack__PrevFrame (Frame* callee, Frame* caller)
{
  unw_word_t ip, sp = 0;
  int res;

  if (!callee->cursor)           abort();
  if (callee->lock != FrameLock) abort();

  *caller = *callee;

  res = unw_step(caller->cursor);
  if (res > 0) {
    unw_get_reg(caller->cursor, UNW_REG_IP, &ip);
    unw_get_reg(caller->cursor, UNW_REG_SP, &sp);

    caller->pc = ip;
    caller->sp = sp;
    RTStack__GetProcInfo(caller);
  } else {
    caller->pc = 0;
    caller->sp = 0;
  }

  if (caller->lock != FrameLock) abort();
}

/*---------------------------------------------------------------------------*/
/* PROCEDURE Unwind (READONLY f: Frame);
   Restore the machine state back to the frame "f".  All callee-saved
   registers must be restored to the state they were in when frame "f"
   made its last call. */

void RTStack__Unwind (Frame *target)
{
  int res;

  if (!target->cursor)           abort();
  if (target->lock != FrameLock) abort();

  /* Set IP to the landing pad computed by RTEHScan.ScanEHTable. */
  unw_set_reg(target->cursor, UNW_REG_IP, target->landingPad);

  /* Pass the exception object pointer in EH data register 0. */
  unw_set_reg(target->cursor,
              __builtin_eh_return_data_regno(EHObjRegNo),
              target->exceptionRef);

  /* Pass the tTypeIndex (exception selector) in EH data register 1. */
  unw_set_reg(target->cursor,
              __builtin_eh_return_data_regno(EHTypeRegNo),
              target->tTypeIndex);

  res = unw_resume(target->cursor);
  /* unw_resume only returns on error. */
  if (res < 0) {
    printf("RTStack__Unwind - unw_resume error\n");
    abort();
  }
}

#ifdef __cplusplus
} /* extern "C" */
#endif

#ifdef __cplusplus
/* RTStack__ThrowM3Exc is defined outside the extern "C" block so that the
   C++ compiler's exception-handling machinery is fully engaged (the throw
   expression needs C++ EH unwinding, not C abort semantics).  The
   extern "C" on the definition gives the symbol C linkage so that M3
   code can call it via the EXTERNAL pragma in RTStack.i3. */
extern "C" void RTStack__ThrowM3Exc(void* act) {
  throw _M3Exc{act};
}
#endif

<sub>⏱️ 4469m 8s</sub>

**No, it's not needed.** Here's why:

- `configure_c_compiler()` is defined as a *proc* in `Darwin.common` — it's not called at the top level
- It's invoked lazily inside `Darwin.common`'s `internal_configure_system_lib()` proc whenever `SYSTEM_LIBS` entries are resolved
- For x86 targets, it's also called at line 51 when setting up `SYSTEM_ASM` — but that covers AMD64 already
- The existing `I386_DARWIN` and `PPC_DARWIN` configs don't have an explicit call and work fine

The explicit `configure_c_compiler()` in our configs is **harmless** (it returns immediately if `SYSTEM_CC` is already set), but redundant. It was likely carried over from the installed `~/cm3/bin/config/ARM64_DARWIN` which had it as a leftover from the compat-header era.

<sub>⏱️ 4476m 36s</sub>

### 💬 Copilot

**No, it's not strictly necessary** — `cm3.cfg` already sets `TARGET` before doing `include(... TARGET)`, so the platform config receives it pre-set. The `readonly TARGET` line in the platform config just re-assigns the same value.

However, I'd recommend **keeping it**. Here's why:

1. **Convention** — every other platform config (`I386_DARWIN`, `PPC_DARWIN`, `AMD64_LINUX`, etc.) has it
2. **Safety** — the `readonly` prevents anything later in the config from accidentally mutating `TARGET`
3. **Standalone use** — if the config file is ever used directly (e.g., passed via `-config` instead of cm3.cfg), TARGET would be undefined without it

The one risk is if cm3.cfg sets TARGET as `readonly` before including the platform config — then the redundant assignment would crash. But looking at the cm3.cfg files, TARGET is set as a plain mutable variable, so re-assigning + marking readonly in the platform config is fine.

**Verdict: leave it in place.**

<sub>⏱️ 4482m 54s</sub>

### 💬 Copilot

**Yes, ex_stack should work on AMD64_LINUX — the infrastructure is already there.** Here's what already exists:

- `AMD64_LINUX` is already in `HAS_STACK_WALKER`
- `RTMachine.i3` and `RTStackC.c` already exist (identical `FrameInfo` layout to the Darwin versions)
- The `AMD64_LINUX` config already has the `M3_USE_STACK_WALKER` plumbing, including the correct `SYSTEM_LIBS{"UNWIND"}` link flags for nongnu libunwind

The key differences from Darwin:

1. **Link flags** — Linux uses the nongnu libunwind (`-lunwind-x86_64 -lunwind -lunwind-generic`), which is a separate package (`libunwind-dev`), not built into libSystem like on macOS
2. **`_Float128`** — AMD64_LINUX uses `_Float128` for `EXTENDED` (GCC supports it), unlike AMD64_DARWIN which must use `double`. This is already correct in `Target.m3` and `M3C.m3`.

<sub>⏱️ 4483m 5s</sub>

### 💬 Copilot

As suspected — the AMD64_LINUX `RTStackC.c` is missing `_M3Exc` and `RTStack__ThrowM3Exc`. It has the `#ifdef __cplusplus` guards from the ex_frame era but not the C++ throw machinery needed for ex_stack.

To enable ex_stack on AMD64_LINUX you'd need to:

1. **Uncomment** `M3_USE_STACK_WALKER = TRUE` in the config (it's already there, just commented out)
2. **Add** `_M3Exc` struct and `RTStack__ThrowM3Exc` to `RTStackC.c` — same pattern as the Darwin versions
3. Install `libunwind-dev` on the Linux system

The runtime code itself is essentially identical to the Darwin versions (libunwind API is the same). It would be a small, low-risk port.

/* This file implements the stack walking functions of
   the RTStack interface. */

#include <stdlib.h>
#include <stdio.h>
#include <string.h>
#include <setjmp.h>
#include <signal.h>
#include <libunwind.h>


#ifdef __cplusplus
extern "C" {
#endif

//Define the exception handling register number. 0 should be safe
//across most architectures.
#define EHObjRegNo  0
#define EHTypeRegNo 1

//declare a personality function
void * __m3_personality_v0();

//external M3 alloc memory
extern char * RTException__AllocBuf(int size);

/*
  FrameInfo = RECORD
    pc  : ADDRESS;
    sp  : ADDRESS;
    bp  : ADDRESS;        (* base pointer *)
    lock: INTEGER;        (* to ensure that cxt isn't overrun!! *)
    excRef  : ADDRESS;    (* ref to the exception activation *)
    tTypeIndex : INTEGER; (* tTypeIndex from exception table *)
    cursor : ADDRESS;     (* libunwind cursor to cur frame *)
    startIP : ADDRESS;    (* libunwind start ip of current proc *)
    endIP : ADDRESS;      (* libunwind end ip of current proc *)
    lsda : ADDRESS;       (* libunwind lsda *)
    persFn : ADDRESS;     (* libunwind handler pers fn *)
    landingPad : ADDRESS; (* libunwind landing pad *)
  END;
 * The typedef below must agree with the definition replicated here
 * and defined in RTMachine.i3
 */

typedef struct {
  unsigned long pc;
  unsigned long sp;
  unsigned long bp; //not used
  long lock;
  unsigned long exceptionRef;
  long tTypeIndex;
  unw_cursor_t *cursor;
  unw_word_t start_ip;
  unw_word_t end_ip;
  unw_word_t lsda;
  unw_word_t persFn;
  unw_word_t landingPad;
} Frame;

#define FrameLock 0x1234567890

void * __m3_personality_v0() {
  printf("m3 personality\n");
  return NULL;
}

/*---------------------------------------------------------------------------*/
/*
 * Get the procedure info for this frame including the personality function
 * and language specific data
 *
 * The unw_get_proc_info() routine returns auxiliary information about the procedure that created the stack frame identified by argument cp. The pip argument is a pointer to a structure of type unw_proc_info_t which is used to return the information. 
 */

void RTStack__GetProcInfo(Frame *f) {
  int res;
  unw_proc_info_t info;

  res = unw_get_proc_info(f->cursor, &info);
  if (res < 0) {
    printf("unw_get_proc_info error\n");
    abort();
  }
  f->start_ip = info.start_ip;
  f->end_ip = info.end_ip;
  f->lsda = info.lsda;
  f->persFn = info.handler;
}

/*---------------------------------------------------------------------------*/
/* PROCEDURE ProcName (READONLY f: Frame): ADDRESS;
   Return the null-terminated constant string that names the procedure
   corresponding to the stack frame "f".  Returns NIL if no name is
   known. */

char* RTStack__ProcName (Frame *f)
{
  int res;
  char *name;
  long name_len = 50;
  unw_word_t ofp;

  name = (char *) malloc(name_len);
  //there is a small mem leak here but as it is only called
  //during debugex of the stack unwinder it should be fine.

  res = unw_get_proc_name(f->cursor, name, name_len, &ofp);
  if (res == 0) {
    return name;
  } else {
    return 0;
  }
}

/*---------------------------------------------------------------------------*/
/* PROCEDURE GetThreadFrame (VAR f: Frame;  start: ADDRESS;  len: INTEGER);
   Return in "f" the frame of the thread whose machine state is in bytes
   [start .. start+len).  Returns with f.pc=NIL on failure. */

void RTStack__GetThreadFrame (Frame *f, char *start, int len)
{
  // not implemented 
  abort();
}

/*---------------------------------------------------------------------------*/
/* PROCEDURE CurrentFrame (VAR(*OUT*) f: Frame)
 * returns the frame that corresponds to its caller. */

void RTStack__CurFrame (Frame *f)
{
  unw_context_t *uc;
  unw_cursor_t *cursor;
  unw_word_t ip, sp = 0;

  //we alloc in m3 otherwise a serious memory leak 
  //uc = (unw_context_t *) malloc(sizeof(unw_context_t));
  //cursor = (unw_cursor_t *) malloc(sizeof(unw_cursor_t));
  uc = (unw_context_t *) RTException__AllocBuf(sizeof(unw_context_t));
  cursor = (unw_cursor_t *) RTException__AllocBuf(sizeof(unw_cursor_t));

  f->lock = FrameLock;
  unw_getcontext(uc);
  unw_init_local(cursor, uc);
  unw_get_reg(cursor, UNW_REG_IP, &ip);
  unw_get_reg(cursor, UNW_REG_SP, &sp);
  
  f->cursor = cursor;
  f->pc = ip;
  f->sp = sp;
  RTStack__GetProcInfo(f);

  if (f->lock != FrameLock) abort ();
}

/*---------------------------------------------------------------------------*/
/* PROCEDURE PreviousFrame (READONLY callee: Frame;  VAR(*OUT*)caller: Frame)
   Return the stack frame that called "callee".  Returns with pc = NIL if
   "callee" is the first frame on the stack or its predecessor is ill-formed.
   */

void RTStack__PrevFrame (Frame* callee, Frame* caller)
{
  unw_word_t ip, sp = 0;
  int res;

  if (!callee->cursor) abort();

  if (callee->lock != FrameLock) abort ();
  *caller = *callee;

  res = unw_step(caller->cursor);
  if (res > 0) {
    unw_get_reg(caller->cursor, UNW_REG_IP, &ip);
    unw_get_reg(caller->cursor, UNW_REG_SP, &sp);
    
    caller->pc = ip;
    caller->sp = sp;
    RTStack__GetProcInfo(caller);

  } else {
    caller->pc = 0;
    caller->sp = 0;
  }
  if (caller->lock != FrameLock) abort ();
}

/*---------------------------------------------------------------------------*/
/* PROCEDURE Unwind (READONLY f: Frame);
   Restore the machine state back to the frame "f".  All callee-saved
   registers must be restored to the state they were in when frame "f"
   made its last call. */

void RTStack__Unwind (Frame *target)
{
  int res;

  if (!target->cursor) abort();
  if (target->lock != FrameLock) abort ();
  
  //set the IP to landingPad 
  unw_set_reg(target->cursor, UNW_REG_IP, target->landingPad);
  
  //set the eh register zero to return the exception object
  unw_set_reg(target->cursor,
	      __builtin_eh_return_data_regno(EHObjRegNo),
	      target->exceptionRef);
 
  //set the eh register one to the tTypeIndex for gcc
  unw_set_reg(target->cursor,
	      __builtin_eh_return_data_regno(EHTypeRegNo),
	      target->tTypeIndex);

  res = unw_resume(target->cursor);
  //success means unreachable from here
  if (res < 0) {
    printf("RTStack__Unwind - unw_resume error\n");
    abort();
  }
}

    printf ("ip = %lx, sp = %lx\n", (long) ip, (long) sp);

    ret = unw_get_proc_name(&cursor, name, name_len, &ofp);
    printf("name %s\n",name);
  }
}
*/

} /* extern "C" */
#endif

<sub>⏱️ 4493m 41s</sub>

### 💬 Copilot

Now I have a clear picture. Here's the full list of changes needed:

**1. `RTStackC.c` — add `_M3Exc` + `RTStack__ThrowM3Exc` (critical missing piece)**

The Linux file ends at the `} /* extern "C" */` closing brace with no `ThrowM3Exc`. Need to add the same C++ throw function that the Darwin versions have:

```c
#ifdef __cplusplus
extern "C" void RTStack__ThrowM3Exc(void* act) {
  throw _M3Exc{act};
}
#endif
```

And `struct _M3Exc` must be defined *outside* the `extern "C"` block (before it).

**2. Config: `SYSTEM_CC` must use `g++` with `-x c++`**

AMD64_LINUX currently sets `SYSTEM_CC = "gcc -g -m64 -fPIC"`. But with ex_stack, M3C.m3 emits `catch (_M3Exc& _m3exc)` and `throw` in the generated C files — those are C++ constructs and need a C++ compiler. Darwin works because `configure_c_compiler()` sets `SYSTEM_CC = "g++ ... -x c++"`. Linux would need the same when `M3_USE_STACK_WALKER` is enabled:

```
M3_USE_STACK_WALKER = TRUE
SYSTEM_CC = "g++ -g -m64 -fPIC -x c++"
```

**3. Config: uncomment `M3_USE_STACK_WALKER = TRUE`** (already noted)

**4. `SYSTEM_LIBS{"UNWIND"}` path** — Already conditionally set in the config, but the hardcoded `/usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu` path may not exist on all distros (e.g., Arch, Fedora). A more portable alternative would be to rely on the linker's default search path and just use `["-lunwind-x86_64", "-lunwind"]`.

**Nothing else needs to change** — `HAS_STACK_WALKER` already has `AMD64_LINUX`, `RTMachine.i3` already has `Has_stack_walker = TRUE`, the `m3makefile` already exists, and M3C.m3's C++ EH emission is already unconditional (not guarded by target).

Want me to make these changes?

/* _M3Exc is the C++ exception type thrown by RTStack__ThrowM3Exc and caught
   by the "catch (_M3Exc& _m3exc)" clauses that M3C.m3 generates in each
   translation unit.  It must be a proper C++ struct (not inside extern "C")
   so that C++ EH type-matching works correctly.  The identical definition
   appears in the M3C.m3 preamble for generated translation units; ODR is
   satisfied because the layout is the same everywhere. */
#ifdef __cplusplus
struct _M3Exc { void* act; };
#endif

#ifdef __cplusplus
extern "C" {
#endif

//Define the exception handling register number. 0 should be safe
//across most architectures.

...
    ret = unw_get_proc_name(&cursor, name, name_len, &ofp);
    printf("name %s\n",name);
  }
}
*/

#ifdef __cplusplus
} /* extern "C" */
#endif

#ifdef __cplusplus
/* RTStack__ThrowM3Exc is defined outside the extern "C" block so that the
   C++ compiler's exception-handling machinery is fully engaged (the throw
   expression needs C++ EH unwinding, not C abort semantics).  The
   extern "C" on the definition gives the symbol C linkage so that M3
   code can call it via the EXTERNAL pragma in RTStack.i3. */
extern "C" void RTStack__ThrowM3Exc(void* act) {
  throw _M3Exc{act};
}
#endif

### 💬 Copilot

Done. Summary of changes:

**`m3-libs/m3core/src/runtime/AMD64_LINUX/RTStackC.c`:**
- Added `struct _M3Exc { void* act; }` outside the `extern "C"` block (after `#include \<libunwind.h\>`)
- Added `RTStack__ThrowM3Exc` with `throw _M3Exc{act}` after the closing `extern "C"` brace

**`m3-sys/cminstall/src/config/AMD64_LINUX`:**
- Enabled `M3_USE_STACK_WALKER = TRUE`
- Overrides `SYSTEM_CC` to `g++ -g -m64 -fPIC -x c++` (required since M3C.m3-generated files contain `catch (_M3Exc&)` / `throw` which are C++ constructs)
- Simplified `SYSTEM_LIBS{"UNWIND"}` to remove the hardcoded `/usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu` path — modern distros put libunwind in the default linker search path

Note: the `SYSTEM_CC` override must come *after* `include("Linux.common")` since Linux.common may also reference it, but since we're unconditionally re-assigning it, order within the post-includes section is fine.

<sub>⏱️ 4499m 14s</sub>

### 💬 Copilot

**No — AMD64_LINUX defaults to backend mode `"3"` (the native GCC/m3cc backend).** Nothing in `AMD64_LINUX`, `AMD64.common`, or `Linux.common` sets `M3_BACKEND_MODE`; the default `"3"` comes from `cm3cfg.common`'s `if not defined` guard.

This is a critical gap in my changes. The ex_stack C++ catch/throw infrastructure (`catch (_M3Exc& _m3exc)`, `throw`) is only emitted by **M3C.m3** (the C backend). With the GCC backend, those clauses are never generated, so `RTStack__ThrowM3Exc`'s C++ exception would be uncaught.

AMD64_LINUX needs `M3_BACKEND_MODE = "C"` — same as ARM64_DARWIN and AMD64_DARWIN:

<sub>⏱️ 4500m 35s</sub>

### 💬 Copilot

Good. One more thing — `SYSTEM_CC` is initialised to `"gcc ..."` at line 4, then the includes run (with `M3_BACKEND_MODE = "C"` already set), then line 24 overrides it to `g++`. The initial `gcc` value at line 4 is harmless since it just gets overridden; it's there because the original config set it and `SYSTEM_ASM` (which is `readonly`) must come before the includes. That's fine.

Final state of all changes for AMD64_LINUX ex_stack:

| What | Change |
|---|---|
| `RTStackC.c` | Added `struct _M3Exc` (outside `extern "C"`) + `RTStack__ThrowM3Exc` (after closing brace) |
| Config: `M3_BACKEND_MODE` | Set to `"C"` before includes — without the C backend, M3C.m3 never generates the `catch (_M3Exc&)` clauses |
| Config: `M3_USE_STACK_WALKER` | Set to `TRUE` before includes |
| Config: `SYSTEM_CC` | Overridden to `g++ -x c++` after includes — C++ required for both RTStackC.c and M3-generated files |
| Config: `SYSTEM_LIBS{"UNWIND"}` | Simplified to `["-lunwind-x86_64", "-lunwind"]` (no hardcoded lib path) |

```
1. # Native C++ Exception Handling for ARM64_DARWIN and AMD64_DARWIN (`ex_stack`)
2. 
3. This document describes the native stack-unwinding exception handling
4. implementation added for the Darwin ports, explains the changes made to the
5. compiler and runtime, and documents the bootstrap process required to
6. transition from the old `ex_frame` (setjmp/longjmp) implementation to the
7. new `ex_stack` (C++ throw/catch) implementation.
8. 
9. ---
10. 
11. ## Background
12. 
13. CM3 has historically used a portable "frame-linked" exception handling
14. mechanism (`ex_frame`) in which:
15. 
16. - Each `TRY` block pushes a `jmp_buf` onto a per-thread singly-linked list.
17. - `RAISE` walks that list, calling `longjmp` to jump to the matching handler.
18. - `m3front` compiles `TRY/EXCEPT` via `Compile2`, which emits `setjmp` calls
19.   and the associated frame setup/teardown.
20. 
21. This approach is fully portable but has non-trivial overhead on every `TRY`
22. entry (a `setjmp` call) and does not interact with C++ destructors or other
23. language runtimes sharing the same stack.
24. 
25. The `ex_stack` implementation replaces this with **C++ zero-cost exception
26. handling**:
27. 
28. - `RAISE` calls `RTStack__ThrowM3Exc`, a C++ function that executes
29.   `throw _M3Exc{act}`, putting the M3 activation record into a C++ exception.
30. - The C++ runtime unwinds the stack using platform DWARF/EH tables, landing
31.   in `catch (_M3Exc& _m3exc)` clauses that `M3C.m3` generates around every
32.   call site inside a `TRY` block.
33. - `m3front` compiles `TRY/EXCEPT` via `Compile1`, which emits
34.   `CG.Start_try()` / `CG.End_try()` / `CG.Invoke_direct()` /
35.   `CG.Landing_pad()` instead of setjmp.
36. 
37. The result is that `TRY` blocks have zero overhead when no exception is
38. raised; cost is only incurred during unwinding.
39. 
40. ---
41. 
42. ## Requirement: C Backend (`M3_BACKEND_MODE = "C"`)
43. 
44. The `ex_stack` EH model **requires the C backend**.
45. 
46. `Compile1` in `m3front` emits `CG.Start_try()`, `CG.End_try()`,
47. `CG.Invoke_direct()`, and `CG.Landing_pad()`.  These operations are
48. implemented only in `M3C.m3` (the C code generator).  They cause `M3C.m3`
49. to emit C++ `try { … } catch (_M3Exc& _m3exc) { … }` blocks, which the
50. platform C++ compiler (clang/g++) then lowers to DWARF EH tables.
51. 
52. The native x86 assembly backend (`M3_BACKEND_MODE = "3"`, used by `M3x86`)
53. does **not** implement these operations.  Enabling `M3_USE_STACK_WALKER`
54. with a native backend would crash the compiler at code-generation time on
55. any `TRY` statement.
56. 
57. **Always pair `M3_USE_STACK_WALKER = TRUE` with `M3_BACKEND_MODE = "C"`.**
58. 
59. Both Darwin targets discussed here use `M3_BACKEND_MODE = "C"`.
60. 
61. ---
62. 
63. ## Files Changed
64. 
65. ### Runtime — `m3-libs/m3core`
66. 
67. #### `src/runtime/ARM64_DARWIN/RTMachine.i3`
68. Declares `Has_stack_walker = TRUE` and the extended `FrameInfo` record
69. that holds libunwind cursor state (`cursor`, `start_ip`, `end_ip`, `lsda`,
70. `persFn`, `landingPad`, `excRef`, `tTypeIndex`).  The `Has_stack_walker`
71. constant is hardcoded `TRUE` for `ARM64_DARWIN`, meaning the runtime uses
72. C++ throw/catch support when `ex_stack` is selected.
73. 
74. #### `src/runtime/ARM64_DARWIN/RTStackC.c`
75. Implements all stack-walking primitives using Apple's built-in libunwind
76. (part of `libSystem.B.dylib`; no extra link flags needed):
77. 
78. - `RTStack__CurFrame` — captures the current unwinder cursor.
79. - `RTStack__PrevFrame` — steps one frame up the stack.
80. - `RTStack__Unwind` — resumes execution at a specific landing pad
```

229. ### Config — `m3-sys/cminstall/src/config/ARM64_DARWIN` and `AMD64_DARWIN`
230. 
231. Both Darwin targets use the same config requirements for `ex_stack`:
232. 
233. ```quake
234. M3_BACKEND_MODE = "C"        % must be before includes
235. M3_USE_STACK_WALKER = TRUE   % must be before includes
236. 
237. % ... include target/common config here ...
238. 
239. % Keep Rosetta-based bootstrap builds single-threaded.
240. M3_PARALLEL_BACK = 1
241. 
242. % libunwind is part of libSystem.B.dylib on macOS — no extra link flags.
243. SYSTEM_LIBS{"UNWIND"} = []
244. ```
245. 
246. `M3_BACKEND_MODE` and `M3_USE_STACK_WALKER` must be set **before** the target
247. config includes so the guards in the common Darwin config files see the
248. correct values.
249. 
250. `SYSTEM_LIBS{"UNWIND"} = []` must be set unconditionally (outside any
251. `if defined("M3_USE_STACK_WALKER")` guard) so that the `import_sys_lib
252. ("UNWIND")` call in `m3core/src/runtime/m3makefile` does not fail with a
253. "does not define a value for UNWIND" error.
254. 
255. On `AMD64_DARWIN`, `M3_PARALLEL_BACK = 1` must come **after** the includes,
256. because `AMD64.common` resets it to 20.
257.

383. ## Portability Notes
384. 
385. ### AMD64_LINUX
386. 
387. `AMD64_LINUX` has `Has_stack_walker = TRUE` in its `RTMachine.i3` and is
388. listed in `HAS_STACK_WALKER`, so the build infrastructure is ready.  Its
389. `RTStackC.c` already implements `RTStack__CurFrame`, `RTStack__PrevFrame`,
390. and `RTStack__Unwind` using `libunwind`.
391. 
392. However, `AMD64_LINUX` typically uses the native x86_64 code generator
393. (`M3_BACKEND_MODE = "3"`), which cannot generate `Start_try`/`End_try`/
394. `Landing_pad`.  To use `ex_stack` on `AMD64_LINUX` you must also set
395. `M3_BACKEND_MODE = "C"` and add `RTStack__ThrowM3Exc` to
396. `AMD64_LINUX/RTStackC.c`; it does **not** already provide that entry point.
397. 
398. ### AMD64_DARWIN
399. 
400. `AMD64_DARWIN` is now fully ported.
401. 
402. The completed work includes:
403. 
404. 1. `m3-libs/m3core/src/runtime/AMD64_DARWIN/RTMachine.i3`
405. 2. `m3-libs/m3core/src/runtime/AMD64_DARWIN/RTStackC.c`
406. 3. `m3-libs/m3core/src/runtime/AMD64_DARWIN/m3makefile`
407. 4. adding `"AMD64_DARWIN" : TRUE` to `HAS_STACK_WALKER`
408. 5. setting `M3_BACKEND_MODE = "C"` and `M3_USE_STACK_WALKER = TRUE` in the
409.    `AMD64_DARWIN` config
410. 
411. All five verification tests pass under Rosetta 2.  See
412. `README-AMD64_DARWIN.md` for the full bootstrap procedure and target-specific
413. notes.
414. 
415. ### Other targets
416. 
417. Any target using `M3_BACKEND_MODE = "C"` with a C++ compiler that supports
418. DWARF EH is a candidate.  The native x86 backend (`M3_BACKEND_MODE = "3"`)
419. cannot be used.
420.
```

</details>

97. #### `src/runtime/AMD64_DARWIN/RTMachine.i3`
98. The `AMD64_DARWIN` port adds the corresponding x86_64 macOS runtime
99. description.  Like the ARM64 version, it declares `Has_stack_walker = TRUE`
100. and uses the same `FrameInfo` layout for libunwind state.
101. 
102. #### `src/runtime/AMD64_DARWIN/RTStackC.c`
103. Implements the same stack-walking primitives and `RTStack__ThrowM3Exc`
104. entry point for `AMD64_DARWIN`.
105. 
106. The implementation is effectively identical to the ARM64 file: Apple's
107. libunwind API on x86_64 macOS is the same interface used on arm64, and the
108. exception throw path is the same C++ `throw _M3Exc{act}` model.
109. 
110. All five verification tests pass under Rosetta 2.
111. 
112. #### `src/runtime/ex_stack/RTExStack.m3`
113. Implements `RTException.Raise` and `RTException.ResumeRaise` for the
114. `ex_stack` runtime.  Key points:
115. 
116. - The `RaiseActivation` record must be **heap-allocated** before throwing,
117.   because the C++ unwinder destroys the original stack frame before landing
118.   in the catch clause.  A stack-allocated `act` would dangle:
119. 
120.   ```modula3
121.   excRef := NEW(REF RaiseActivation);
122.   excRef^ := act;
123.   RTStack.ThrowM3Exc(ADR(excRef^));
124.   ```
125. 
126. - `RTStack.ThrowM3Exc` never returns; the call to `InvokeBackstop` below it
127.   is an unreachable safety net only.
128. 
129. - The assertion `<*ASSERT RTStack.Has_walker*>` at module initialisation
130.   verifies that `ex_stack` is never accidentally linked into a build that
131.   has `Has_stack_walker = FALSE`.
132. 
133. #### `src/runtime/m3makefile`
````

</details>

<sub>⏱️ 4510m 11s</sub>

### 👤 User

Should we use a similar guard for AMD64_DARWIN and ARM64_DARWIN in case a future gcc-based backend comes along?

---

<sub>⏱️ 4511m 2s</sub>

### 💬 Copilot

There's an important distinction between the two:

**ARM64_DARWIN — no, guard not appropriate.**  
`M3_BACKEND_MODE = "C"` is unconditional for ARM64 because there is no ARM64 native backend. Even without ex_stack you'd still need the C backend. The `M3_BACKEND_MODE` line is not logically coupled to `M3_USE_STACK_WALKER` there.

**AMD64_DARWIN — arguably yes.**  
AMD64 does have a native x86_64 backend (m3cc/m3cgc1, mode `"3"`). Without ex_stack, AMD64_DARWIN could in principle use it. The pattern would mirror AMD64_LINUX exactly:

```quake
M3_USE_STACK_WALKER = TRUE

if defined("M3_USE_STACK_WALKER")
  M3_BACKEND_MODE = "C"
end

include("AMD64.common")
include("Darwin.common")

M3_PARALLEL_BACK = 1
SYSTEM_LIBS{"UNWIND"} = []
```

However there's a practical counter-argument: the Darwin configs have always used the C backend, and the UNWIND lib entry must be set **unconditionally** on Darwin (unlike Linux) because `import_sys_lib("UNWIND")` in the m3makefile fires regardless of `M3_USE_STACK_WALKER`. So the guard would only cover `M3_BACKEND_MODE`, not `SYSTEM_LIBS{"UNWIND"}` — which is a bit asymmetric and could mislead.

**Verdict:** Leave both Darwin configs as-is. The AMD64_LINUX guard works well there because ex_stack is genuinely opt-in (native backend is the historical default, and `SYSTEM_LIBS{"UNWIND"}` is also guarded). For Darwin, the C backend is effectively the default and the UNWIND entry must be unconditional anyway — adding a partial guard would add complexity without real benefit.

---

Would it make sense to combine the README-AMD64_DARWIN and README-ARM64_DARWIN md files into one README-DARWIN.md?

---

<sub>⏱️ 4513m 55s</sub>

### 💬 Copilot

Good question. There are arguments both ways:

**For combining:**
- Significant shared material: libunwind API is identical on both, `RTStackC.c` is the same file, `Darwin.common` is shared, the `ex_stack` mechanism is identical, and the `EXTENDED = double` rationale applies to both
- The key source changes (`Target.m3`, `M3C.m3`, float m3makefiles) affect both targets and would only need to be explained once
- Easier to cross-reference (e.g. "AMD64_DARWIN bootstrap differs from ARM64_DARWIN in the following ways…")

**Against combining:**
- The bootstrap procedures are quite different: ARM64 is a native build, AMD64 is a cross-compile from ARM64 running under Rosetta with the `TARGET` unconditional assignment pitfall, stage-1 manual install, etc.
- Someone bootstrapping just one target has to read through material for the other
- The AMD64_DARWIN doc has several unique pitfalls (`TARGET` guard, `M3_PARALLEL_BACK` placement, `_Float128` mismatch root cause) that would clutter a combined doc

**My recommendation: keep them separate but add a cross-reference.** The bootstrap procedures are the bulk of each document and they're genuinely distinct. What you could do instead is extract the shared "Darwin platform notes" (libunwind, EXTENDED type, ex_stack mechanics, source config structure) into a brief common section at the top of each, with a `See also: README-ARM64_DARWIN.md / README-AMD64_DARWIN.md` cross-reference — which the docs likely already have.

The `README-ex_stack.md` already serves as the shared technical reference for the ex_stack mechanism itself, so the per-target READMEs can stay focused on the bootstrap procedure for their respective target.

Want me to add cross-references between the two?

<sub>⏱️ 4538m 12s</sub>

### 👤 User

DO we need -lunwind-generic in AMD64_LINUX?

---

<sub>⏱️ 4538m 34s</sub>

### 💬 Copilot

No — and we already dropped it. The original config had:

```quake
"-L/usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu",
"-lunwind-x86_64",
"-lunwind",
"-lunwind-generic"
```

`-lunwind-generic` was a separate shared object on some older nongnu libunwind packages. On modern Debian/Ubuntu (and Fedora/RHEL) `libunwind-dev` only ships `libunwind.so` and `libunwind-x86_64.so` — there is no `libunwind-generic.so` to link against, so including it would cause a linker error ("cannot find -lunwind-generic") on those systems.

The two flags we kept — `-lunwind-x86_64` (arch-specific implementation) and `-lunwind` (the API library) — are all that's needed on any current distribution.

<sub>⏱️ 4568m 12s</sub>

### 💬 Copilot

The `#ifndef Infinity`/`#ifndef NaN` guards were introduced during the ARM64_DARWIN Stage 2 bootstrap when it failed with:

```
'Infinity' macro redefined
```

The compat header `m3_arm64_compat.h` (which `ARM64_DARWIN` config was including via `-include`) already defined `Infinity (__builtin_inf())`. When the new ARM64 cm3 binary (compiled from the then-current M3C.m3 source) emitted `#define Infinity INFINITY` in every TU's preamble without a guard, it collided with the compat header's definition.

The fix was to wrap M3C.m3's `#define Infinity` and `#define NaN` in `#ifndef`/`#endif` guards so whichever came first would win without an error.

The switch from `#include \<limits\>` + `std::numeric_limits\<double\>::infinity()` to `__builtin_inff()` / `__builtin_nanf("")` was also part of the same fix — `__builtin_*` forms work in both C and C++ compilation modes, avoiding a C++-only dependency in the preamble.

Since the compat header has since been **deleted** (`m3_arm64_compat.h` was removed), the redefinition conflict no longer exists. The `#ifndef` guards are now purely defensive/harmless — not strictly required, but still good practice in case other system headers define those names.

Both bootstraps pass ✅:

**ARM64_DARWIN** — all 14 front packages built successfully. `m3cc` fails: `arm-apple-darwin25.4.0 not supported` (GCC 4.7 doesn't know ARM64 Apple — expected).

1. # Porting CM3 to ARM64_DARWIN (Apple Silicon)
2. 
3. This document describes the work done to bootstrap a native ARM64_DARWIN
4. CM3 compiler on Apple Silicon Macs (M1/M2/M3/…), starting from an existing
5. AMD64_DARWIN installation running under Rosetta 2.
6. 
7. **See also:**
8. - [`README-AMD64_DARWIN.md`](README-AMD64_DARWIN.md) — bootstrapping the x86_64 Darwin target from ARM64_DARWIN
9. - [`README-ex_stack.md`](README-ex_stack.md) — full technical reference for the C++ zero-cost EH implementation shared by both Darwin targets
10. 
11. ---
12. 
13. ## Starting Point
14. 
15. CM3 was already installed at `~/cm3` as an AMD64_DARWIN binary.  On Apple
16. Silicon this binary runs transparently under Rosetta 2, which translates
17. x86_64 instructions to ARM64 at runtime.  The source tree at
18. `~/Downloads/cm3-d5.12.0` was available for cross-compilation.
19. 
20. The goal was a fully self-hosted native ARM64 CM3 compiler installed at
21. `~/cm3`.
22. 
23. ---
24. 
25. ## Issues Encountered and Fixed
26. 
27. ### 1. ARM64 target not auto-detected by build scripts
28. 
29. `scripts/sysinfo.sh` handles the Darwin case by inspecting `uname -p`.  It
30. handles `powerpc` and `i386` but has no branch for `arm` or `arm64`, so it
31. falls through without setting `CM3_TARGET`.  This causes the wrapper scripts
32. (`pkgmap.sh`, `do-cm3-front.sh`) to error with "does not know about uname -a".
33. 
34. **Fix**: Set `CM3_TARGET=ARM64_DARWIN` explicitly in the environment before
35. invoking any build script.
36. 
37. ### 2. CM3 target not overridable via `M3CONFIG` alone
38. 
39. The CM3 startup sequence in `m3-sys/m3quake/src/MxConfigC.m3` calls
40. `uname()` first and sets `HOST` to whatever the OS reports.  Under Rosetta,
41. `uname` returns `x86_64`, so `HOST = AMD64_DARWIN`.  The `DefineIfNotDefined`
42. call for `TARGET` runs before `cm3.cfg` is read, so the `if not
43. defined("TARGET")` guard in `cm3.cfg` is always false — `M3CONFIG` alone
44. cannot change `TARGET`.
45. 
46. **Fix**: Pass `-DTARGET=ARM64_DARWIN` explicitly on the `cm3` command line,
47. via the `BUILDARGS` environment variable that `pkgcmds.sh` appends to the
48. build command:
49. 
50. ```sh
51. export BUILDARGS="-DTARGET=ARM64_DARWIN"
52. ```
53. 
54. This is only required for the AMD64 cm3 cross-building for ARM64.  Once the
55. native ARM64 binary is in use, `uname()` returns `arm64` and `TARGET` is set
56. correctly from `cm3.cfg` without any override.
57. 
58. ### 3. `EXTENDED` float type: ARM64_DARWIN uses `ext64`, not `ext128`
59. 
60. The Modula-3 type `EXTENDED` historically maps to the x87 80-bit extended
61. precision type on x86.  CM3 implements this via one of two subdirectories:
62. 
63. - `ext128/` — 128-bit EXTENDED using GCC's `_Float128` type
64. - `ext64/` — EXTENDED = LONGREAL (64-bit double)
65. 
66. ARM64 has no x87 unit and no hardware support for any precision beyond 64-bit
67. double.  Apple clang also does not provide `_Float128` on Darwin.  The
68. existing condition that selected `ext64` only covered Windows
69. (`TARGET_OS = "NT"`); all other targets including ARM64 fell into `ext128`.
70. 
71. The float `m3makefile` logic was updated so that `ARM64_DARWIN` and
72. `AMD64_DARWIN` both select `ext64`:
73. 
74. #### `m3-libs/m3core/src/float/IEEE/m3makefile`
75. ```diff
76. -if equal (TARGET_OS, "NT") and not IsBackendLlvm ()
77. +if (equal (TARGET_OS, "NT") and not IsBackendLlvm ()) or
78. +   equal (TARGET_ARCH, "ARM64") or
79. +   equal (TARGET, "AMD64_DARWIN")
80.    include_dir ("ext64")
81.  else
82.    include_dir ("ext128")
83. ```
84. 
85. #### `m3-libs/m3core/src/float/IEEE-le/m3makefile`
86. Same change (selects `ExtendedRep.i3`).
87. 
88. #### `m3-libs/libm3/src/random/IEEE/m3makefile`
89. Same change (selects random float implementation).
90. 
91. ### 4. `Target.Extended` size mismatch between compiler and runtime
92. 
93. `m3-sys/m3middle/src/Target.m3` sets `Target.Extended.size` at runtime when
94. the compiler initialises for a given target.  The default is 128 bits (quad
95. precision).  An override to 64 bits existed only for `WIN32`.  When the new
96. ARM64 cm3 binary compiled with `ext64` in m3core but the compiler still
97. believed `EXTENDED` was 128 bits, m3front detected the size mismatch and
98. errored.
99. 
100. The original ARM64-only fix was refined so that `AMD64_DARWIN` is also
````

</details>

1. # Porting CM3 to AMD64_DARWIN (x86_64 macOS)
2. 
3. This document describes the work done to bootstrap an `AMD64_DARWIN`
4. CM3 compiler on macOS, starting from an existing native `ARM64_DARWIN`
5. installation on Apple Silicon and producing a self-hosted x86_64 compiler
6. that runs under Rosetta 2.
7. 
8. **See also:**
9. - [`README-ARM64_DARWIN.md`](README-ARM64_DARWIN.md) — bootstrapping the native Apple Silicon target
10. - [`README-ex_stack.md`](README-ex_stack.md) — full technical reference for the C++ zero-cost EH implementation shared by both Darwin targets
11. 
12. ---
13. 
14. ## Starting Point
15. 
16. CM3 was already installed at `~/cm3` as a native `ARM64_DARWIN` binary on an
17. Apple Silicon Mac.  The source tree at `~/Downloads/cm3-d5.12.0` was
18. available for cross-compilation.
19. 
20. The goal was a fully self-hosted `AMD64_DARWIN` CM3 compiler installed at
21. `~/cm3-AMD64_DARWIN`, with both the C backend and `ex_stack` support working
22. correctly under Rosetta 2.
23. 
24. ---
25. 
26. ## Issues Encountered and Fixed
27. 
28. ### 1. CM3 target not overridable via `M3CONFIG` alone
29. 
30. The CM3 startup sequence in `m3-sys/m3quake/src/MxConfigC.m3` calls
31. `uname()` first and sets `HOST` to whatever the OS reports.  On Apple
32. Silicon, `uname` returns `arm64`, so `HOST = ARM64_DARWIN`.  The
33. `DefineIfNotDefined` call for `TARGET` runs before `cm3.cfg` is read, so the
34. usual `if not defined("TARGET")` guard in `cm3.cfg` is always false —
35. `M3CONFIG` alone cannot change `TARGET` during a cross-build.
36. 
37. **Fix**: Pass `-DTARGET=AMD64_DARWIN` explicitly on the `cm3` command line,
38. via the `BUILDARGS` environment variable:
39. 
40. ```sh
41. export BUILDARGS="-DTARGET=AMD64_DARWIN"
42. ```
43. 
44. This is required for the ARM64 cm3 cross-building for AMD64.  In addition,
45. the installed `~/cm3-AMD64_DARWIN/bin/cm3.cfg` must set:
46. 
47. ```quake
48. TARGET = "AMD64_DARWIN"
49. ```
50. 
51. **unconditionally**, with no `if not defined("TARGET")` guard.  Otherwise a
52. cross-build launched from the ARM64 compiler can leave `TARGET` stuck at
53. `ARM64_DARWIN`.
54. 
55. ### 2. `EXTENDED` float type: AMD64_DARWIN is 64-bit, not 128-bit
56. 
57. The Modula-3 type `EXTENDED` historically maps to x87 extended precision on
58. x86, and CM3 often models this via `_Float128` on platforms that have it.
59. That is correct for `AMD64_LINUX`, but **not** for `AMD64_DARWIN`: Apple
60. clang on x86_64 macOS does not support `_Float128`, so `EXTENDED` must be
61. treated as a 64-bit `double`, exactly as on `ARM64_DARWIN`.
62. 
63. This was the root cause of the long-standing cross-build failure:
64. 
65. ```
66. bad version stamps: M3C.m3 / Target.Real mismatch
67. ```
68. 
69. when compiling `AMD64_DARWIN` from an ARM64 host.
70. 
71. The float `m3makefile` logic was updated so that `AMD64_DARWIN` selects
72. `ext64` instead of `ext128`:
73. 
74. #### `m3-libs/m3core/src/float/IEEE/m3makefile`
75. ```diff
76. -if equal (TARGET_OS, "NT") and not IsBackendLlvm ()
77. +if (equal (TARGET_OS, "NT") and not IsBackendLlvm ()) or
78. +   equal (TARGET_ARCH, "ARM64") or
79. +   equal (TARGET, "AMD64_DARWIN")
80.    include_dir ("ext64")
81.  else
82.    include_dir ("ext128")
83. ```
84. 
85. #### `m3-libs/m3core/src/float/IEEE-le/m3makefile`
86. Same change (selects `ExtendedRep.i3`).
87. 
88. #### `m3-libs/libm3/src/random/IEEE/m3makefile`
89. Same change (selects random float implementation).
90. 
91. ### 3. `Target.Extended` size mismatch between compiler and runtime
92. 
93. `m3-sys/m3middle/src/Target.m3` sets `Target.Extended.size` at runtime when
94. the compiler initialises for a given target.  The default is 128 bits.  An
95. override to 64 bits existed only for `WIN32`.
96. 
97. To make `AMD64_DARWIN` match the new `ext64` runtime layout, `Target.m3`
98. was refined so that `AMD64_DARWIN` is explicitly treated as 64-bit
99. `EXTENDED`:
100.
````

1. # Native C++ Exception Handling for ARM64_DARWIN, AMD64_DARWIN, and AMD64_LINUX (`ex_stack`)
2. 
3. This document describes the native stack-unwinding exception handling
4. implementation added for the Darwin ports and AMD64_LINUX, explains
5. the changes made to the compiler and runtime, and documents the
6. bootstrap process required to transition from the old `ex_frame`
7. (setjmp/longjmp) implementation to the new `ex_stack` (C++
8. throw/catch) implementation.
9. 
10. ---
11. 
12. ## Background
13. 
14. CM3 has historically used a portable "frame-linked" exception handling
15. mechanism (`ex_frame`) in which:
16. 
17. - Each `TRY` block pushes a `jmp_buf` onto a per-thread singly-linked list.
18. - `RAISE` walks that list, calling `longjmp` to jump to the matching handler.
19. - `m3front` compiles `TRY/EXCEPT` via `Compile2`, which emits `setjmp` calls
20.   and the associated frame setup/teardown.
21. 
22. This approach is fully portable but has non-trivial overhead on every `TRY`
23. entry (a `setjmp` call) and does not interact with C++ destructors or other
24. language runtimes sharing the same stack.
25. 
26. The `ex_stack` implementation replaces this with **C++ zero-cost exception
27. handling**:
28. 
29. - `RAISE` calls `RTStack__ThrowM3Exc`, a C++ function that executes
30.   `throw _M3Exc{act}`, putting the M3 activation record into a C++ exception.
31. - The C++ runtime unwinds the stack using platform DWARF/EH tables, landing
32.   in `catch (_M3Exc& _m3exc)` clauses that `M3C.m3` generates around every
33.   call site inside a `TRY` block.
34. - `m3front` compiles `TRY/EXCEPT` via `Compile1`, which emits
35.   `CG.Start_try()` / `CG.End_try()` / `CG.Invoke_direct()` /
36.   `CG.Landing_pad()` instead of setjmp.
37. 
38. The result is that `TRY` blocks have zero overhead when no exception is
39. raised; cost is only incurred during unwinding.
40. 
41. ---
42. 
43. ## Requirement: C Backend (`M3_BACKEND_MODE = "C"`)
44. 
45. The `ex_stack` EH model **requires the C backend**.
46. 
47. `Compile1` in `m3front` emits `CG.Start_try()`, `CG.End_try()`,
48. `CG.Invoke_direct()`, and `CG.Landing_pad()`.  These operations are
49. implemented only in `M3C.m3` (the C code generator).  They cause `M3C.m3`
50. to emit C++ `try { … } catch (_M3Exc& _m3exc) { … }` blocks, which the
51. platform C++ compiler (clang/g++) then lowers to DWARF EH tables.
52. 
53. The native x86 assembly backend (`M3_BACKEND_MODE = "3"`, used by `M3x86`)
54. does **not** implement these operations.  Enabling `M3_USE_STACK_WALKER`
55. with a native backend would crash the compiler at code-generation time on
56. any `TRY` statement.
57. 
58. **Always pair `M3_USE_STACK_WALKER = TRUE` with `M3_BACKEND_MODE = "C"`.**
59. 
60. Both Darwin targets discussed here use `M3_BACKEND_MODE = "C"`, as does `AMD64_LINUX`.
61. 
62. ---
63. 
64. ## Files Changed
65. 
66. ### Runtime — `m3-libs/m3core`
67. 
68. #### `src/runtime/ARM64_DARWIN/RTMachine.i3`
69. Declares `Has_stack_walker = TRUE` and the extended `FrameInfo` record
70. that holds libunwind cursor state (`cursor`, `start_ip`, `end_ip`, `lsda`,
71. `persFn`, `landingPad`, `excRef`, `tTypeIndex`).  The `Has_stack_walker`
72. constant is hardcoded `TRUE` for `ARM64_DARWIN`, meaning the runtime uses
73. C++ throw/catch support when `ex_stack` is selected.
74. 
75. #### `src/runtime/ARM64_DARWIN/RTStackC.c`
76. Implements all stack-walking primitives using Apple's built-in libunwind
77. (part of `libSystem.B.dylib`; no extra link flags needed):
78. 
79. - `RTStack__CurFrame` — captures the current unwinder cursor.
80. - `RTStack__PrevFrame` — steps one frame up the stack.
81. - `RTStack__Unwind` — resumes execution at a specific landing pad
82.   (used in the manual-unwind path; not used by the C++ throw path).
83. - `RTStack__ThrowM3Exc(void* act)` — the key entry point.  Defined
84.   outside `extern "C"` so the C++ compiler's full EH machinery is engaged:
85. 
86.   ```c
87.   struct _M3Exc { void* act; };
88. 
89.   extern "C" void RTStack__ThrowM3Exc(void* act) {
90.       throw _M3Exc{act};
91.   }
92.   ```
93. 
94.   The `_M3Exc` struct must be declared in the same translation unit that
95.   contains the `catch (_M3Exc& …)` clauses.  `M3C.m3` emits the struct
96.   definition at the top of every generated `.c` file.
97. 
98. #### `src/runtime/AMD64_DARWIN/RTMachine.i3`
99. The `AMD64_DARWIN` port adds the corresponding x86_64 macOS runtime
100. description.  Like the ARM64 version, it declares `Has_stack_walker = TRUE`
````

114. ### 5. Apple clang lacks `_Float128` and quad-precision math functions
115. 
116. `M3C.m3` generates a C++ preamble containing:
117. 
118. ```c
119. # if defined(_MSC_VER)
120. typedef double EXTENDED;
121. # else
122. typedef _Float128 EXTENDED;
123. # endif
124. ```
125. 
126. Apple clang on ARM64 does not support `_Float128`.  It also lacks the
127. quad-precision math functions `truncq`, `floorq`, `ceilq`, and `llroundq`.
128. Additionally, the conversion helper functions (`m3_round`, `m3_trunc`,
129. `m3_floor`, `m3_ceil`) used `#ifdef _WIN32` to select the simple
130. `llround(f)` / `trunc(f)` / `floor(f)` / `ceil(f)` forms, falling back to
131. the quad-precision `*q()` versions elsewhere.
132. 
133. The Darwin-specific fix now covers both Apple Silicon and x86_64 macOS:
134. 
135. ```diff
136. -# if defined(_MSC_VER)
137. +# if defined(_MSC_VER) || defined(__aarch64__) || (defined(__x86_64__) && defined(__APPLE__))
138.  typedef double EXTENDED;
139. ```
140. 
141. The same condition was added to all four conversion helper guards:
142. 
143. ```diff
144. -#if defined(_WIN32)
145. +#if defined(_WIN32) || defined(__aarch64__) || (defined(__x86_64__) && defined(__APPLE__))
146.  static INT64 __stdcall m3_round(EXTENDED f) { return llround(f); }
147.  ...
148. ```
149. 
150. ### 6. `Infinity` and `NaN` identifier conflicts — no compat header required anymore
151. 
152. Older pre-built AMD64 CM3 binaries generate C++ files that use `Infinity`
153. and `NaN` as identifiers without ever `#define`-ing them.  Newer generated
154. code emits explicit definitions in the preamble.
155. 
156. The fix in `m3-sys/m3back/src/M3C.m3` is to guard both definitions:
157. 
158. ```diff
159. +#ifndef Infinity
160.  #define Infinity INFINITY
161. +#endif
162. +#ifndef NaN
163.  #define NaN NAN
164. +#endif
165. ```
166. 
167. With the `#ifndef` guards in place, and with the Apple-Darwin
168. `typedef double EXTENDED` / simple `m3_round`-family guards now covering
169. both `__aarch64__` and `(__x86_64__ && __APPLE__)`, the old injected
170. compatibility header is no longer needed.
171. 
172. The following cleanup was done:
173. 
174. - `~/cm3/include/m3_arm64_compat.h` was deleted
175. - `-include m3_arm64_compat.h` was removed from `~/cm3/bin/config/ARM64_DARWIN`
176. - the source config `m3-sys/cminstall/src/config/ARM64_DARWIN` now exists and
177.   does **not** reference any compat header
178. 
179. ### 7. Rosetta 2 pthread deadlock with parallel compilation
180. 
181. CM3 uses `M3_PARALLEL_BACK` to control how many parallel threads are spawned
182. to compile generated C++ files.  The default is 20.
183. 
184. Under Rosetta 2, `pthread_create` from AMD64 translated code acquires
185. Rosetta's internal JIT/thread-registration lock.  Spawning many threads
186. simultaneously can deadlock this lock — the build stalls indefinitely.
187. 
188. **Fix** in the `ARM64_DARWIN` config:
189. 
190. ```quake
191. M3_PARALLEL_BACK = 1
192. ```
193. 
194. This forces sequential C compilation during the Rosetta-driven bootstrap
195. stage.  The source config file `m3-sys/cminstall/src/config/ARM64_DARWIN`
196. now exists and contains:
197. 
198. - `M3_BACKEND_MODE = "C"`
199. - `M3_USE_STACK_WALKER = TRUE`
200. - `M3_PARALLEL_BACK = 1`
````

117. - The `RaiseActivation` record must be **heap-allocated** before throwing,
118.   because the C++ unwinder destroys the original stack frame before landing
119.   in the catch clause.  A stack-allocated `act` would dangle:

125.   ```
126. 
127. - `RTStack.ThrowM3Exc` never returns; the call to `InvokeBackstop` below it
128.   is an unreachable safety net only.
129. 
130. - The assertion `<*ASSERT RTStack.Has_walker*>` at module initialisation
131.   verifies that `ex_stack` is never accidentally linked into a build that
132.   has `Has_stack_walker = FALSE`.

135. Previously had the libunwind frame-walking primitives but was missing the C++
136. throw entry point.  Added `struct _M3Exc { void* act; }` (outside the
137. `extern "C"` block) and `RTStack__ThrowM3Exc` (after the closing `extern "C"`
138. brace), identical in structure to the Darwin versions.
139.

141. The `HAS_STACK_WALKER` quake table controls which targets can use `ex_stack`:
142. 
143. ```quake
144. readonly HAS_STACK_WALKER = {
145.   "AMD64_LINUX"   : TRUE,
146.   "AMD64_DARWIN"  : TRUE,
147.   "ARM64_DARWIN"  : TRUE,
148. }
149. ```
150. 
151. When `M3_USE_STACK_WALKER = TRUE` is set in the platform config **and** the
152. target appears in `HAS_STACK_WALKER`, `include_dir("ex_stack")` and
153. `include_dir(TARGET)` are used instead of `include_dir("ex_frame")`.
